entries.description: HORROR COLLECTOR premiered in Japan on October 10, 2026. Check the 12-episode schedule, official Japanese streaming rollout, cast, staff, music and story.
entries.content: AIRING NOW · RELEASE GUIDE HORROR COLLECTOR Anime: Release Date, Schedule and Where to Watch HORROR COLLECTOR premiered on NHK General TV in Japan on October 10, 2026 at 11:45 p.m. JST. Find the current 12-episode schedule, official Japanese streaming rollout, cast and what international viewers should check. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Updated: October 24, 2026 · How we verify releases Official anime key visual. Source: NHK Enterprises · © Midori Sato, Norio Tsuruta / KADOKAWA / NHK, NEP. Release at a glance Japan TV October 10, 2026 · Saturdays at 23:45 JST · NHK General TV Japan streaming Thursday rollout from 12:00 JST; provider schedules vary Format and studio 12 episodes · Studio Palette International Check your local catalog; worldwide availability unconfirmed Official project source JAPAN PREMIERE October 10, 2026 · NHK General TV JAPAN STREAMING Thursday rollout · 12:00 p.m. JST onward SEASON 12 episodes · Studio Palette When did HORROR COLLECTOR premiere? HORROR COLLECTOR began airing in Japan on October 10, 2026. The NHK General TV slot is Saturday at 11:45 p.m. Japan Standard Time (JST), and the official announcement confirms a 12-episode first season. The premiere date has passed; viewers should check their local service for the latest episode. Because the Japanese slot is close to midnight, other time zones may show a different calendar date. Use NHK's current listing to confirm a particular week's broadcast. Where can you stream the episodes? The official anime site lists a Japanese streaming rollout on ABEMA Premium, DMM TV, Hulu, U-NEXT, Anime Hōdai, J:COM STREAM, TELASA, Lemino, Anime Times, d Anime Store and additional domestic services. Its October 9 notice schedules Episode 1 for October 15 at 12:00 p.m. JST. The streaming page says later services begin from noon on the Thursday after broadcast, in sequence; it does not promise that every provider publishes at the same minute. These are Japanese listings, not worldwide availability. The cited official notices do not confirm a platform or hour for every international territory. If you are outside Japan, search the title in your country's current catalog and check the episode page itself. AniNextUp's Fall 2026 anime calendar can help compare other seasonal premieres. Related reading: The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Schedule & Where to Watch . What is the anime about? The official synopsis follows Fushigi Chino, a boy in a red hood who travels to collect urban legends that have taken physical form in a notebook. He is trying to catch Himitsu, a girl connected to the legends' manifestation, and travels with Jimmy, his human-faced dog partner. Each disturbance brings a supernatural mystery, while Fushigi's pursuit of Himitsu gives the story a continuing thread. The premise centers on rumors and modern urban legends becoming real, rather than one haunted location or creature driving the whole season. That is based on the official synopsis; it does not confirm that each episode adapts one separate legend or follows a one-story-per-episode structure. How many episodes are confirmed? The first TV season is confirmed for 12 episodes. That establishes the season length, but not how many books, chapters or legends it covers. It also does not confirm a second season. Readers deciding whether to start the novels should treat the anime as a separate adaptation until the production identifies its endpoint. Related reading: Black Clover Season 2 Schedule & Where to Watch . Who voices the main characters? Hiiro Ishibashi voices Fushigi, Jun Fukuyama voices Jimmy, Saori Hayami voices Himitsu, and Nobuhiko Okamoto voices the Blue Umbrella Man, according to the official cast page. These roles match the central group introduced in the synopsis: the boy tracking the legends, his companion, the girl linked to them and a mysterious figure whose purpose is not fully explained there. The official character pages provide Japanese names, cast credits and short descriptions. This guide sticks to roles on that official listing rather than combining them with guest cast announced for individual episodes. Which studio and staff are making the series? Studio Palette handles animation. Yuki Inaba directs and oversees series composition; Kaori Yoshikawa designs the characters; Masato Koda composes the music; and Tetsuya Gunji is sound director. The original work is credited to Midori Sato and Norio Tsuruta, with character concepts by Yon. NHK Enterprises is named in production, and NHK is credited alongside KADOKAWA. Related reading: Dandivine Release Date & Where to Watch: Japan Schedule, Cast and Story . These credits confirm that the anime adapts an existing children's horror novel series rather than being described as an original project. For another Fall 2026 supernatural title, compare its schedule with AniNextUp's Demon's Crest viewing guide ; the two shows have separate source material and creative teams. What songs are in HORROR COLLECTOR? Shikao Suga wrote and performs both the opening and ending themes, the official music announcement says. The staff page names the opening as “Kageboshi,” but does not list the ending title, so this guide leaves that title open. Suga also noted his interest in Japanese horror when discussing his work on both songs. How does the anime connect to the novels? KADOKAWA's Tsubasa Bunko publishes the source novels by Sato and Tsuruta, illustrated by Yon. Its page for volume 29, released October 7, 2026, describes it as the climax of Fushigi and Himitsu's pursuit. That shows the novels have a long publishing history, but it does not tell viewers where a 12-episode anime season will stop. The publisher's description applies to the novels, not necessarily the TV adaptation. Related reading: Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Episode Schedule & Where to Watch . The publisher catalogs the books for middle elementary readers. Families can use that category as a reference for the novels, then consult the anime synopsis and episodes to judge the animated version's scarier scenes for themselves. What is still unconfirmed? The official sources establish the Japanese TV slot, episode count, local streaming sequence, lead cast, staff and opening song. They do not establish a worldwide release hour, the number of legends adapted or the season's endpoint in the books. NHK ENTERPRISES Animation published the official teaser on September 17, 2026 at 20:00:03 PDT (UTC−07:00), equivalent to September 18 at 12:00:03 JST. The original YouTube page declares this upload timestamp. Playback availability depends on the viewer’s country. Watch the official teaser ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER YouTube · NHK ENTERPRISES Animation NHK's official site lists the video in its Movies section. Updated: October 24, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error Official sources: official synopsis and announcement , official cast, staff and music credits , Japanese streaming schedule , Episode 1 streaming notice , Suga Shikao theme announcement , NHK Anime broadcast/cast/teaser announcement , and KADOKAWA volume 29 details .

entries.title: I Got a Cheat Skill Season 2: January 2027 Release, Cast and Trailer
entries.description: I Got a Cheat Skill Season 2 is set for January 2027. Check the official story, cast, studio, trailer, release status and what remains unknown.
entries.content: ANIME NEWS · OCTOBER 15, 2026 I Got a Cheat Skill Season 2: January 2027 Release, Cast and Trailer Season 2 of I Got a Cheat Skill in Another World is confirmed for January 2027. Here are the official story details, new and returning cast, staff, trailer and what is still unknown. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · October 15, 2026 · Editorial policy Official Season 2 key visual © Miku, Rein Kuwashima / KADOKAWA / Iseleve 2 Production Committee. Source: official anime website . Release at a glance Release window January 2027 (exact day and time not announced) Japanese release Broadcast and streaming announced for January; schedule pending International streaming Not announced Animation studio Millepensee Official Season 2 news and schedule updates I Got a Cheat Skill in Another World and Became Unrivaled in the Real World, Too is returning with a second TV season in January 2027 . The official anime site and publisher KADOKAWA confirm the month, and the production posted its first Season 2 promotional video and key visual on October 15, 2026. The exact premiere day, Japanese channel, episode count and international streaming services have not been announced. When does I Got a Cheat Skill Season 2 come out? The answer available now is January 2027. The official site describes the new season as beginning broadcast and streaming that month, while KADOKAWA’s listing gives the same month-long window. Neither source gives a calendar day or a first-episode time. Treat January as a confirmed release month, not as confirmation of a January 1 premiere or a weekly schedule. The official wording refers to Japanese release information. It does not identify a service for viewers in the United States, Latin America, Europe or other regions. A Japanese streaming notice also does not establish an international simulcast. Until a distributor publishes its own regional listing, the safest answer to “where can I watch Season 2?” is that international availability is still pending. What did the October 2026 announcement confirm? On October 15, the anime’s official news page published three separate updates: the first Season 2 PV, the first Season 2 key visual and two new character-and-cast announcements. The material confirms active promotion and named creative credits, but it is not a complete broadcast schedule. The key visual is official artwork from the production committee and appears above; the PV is linked from the production’s own movie page and YouTube channel. The teaser is useful for seeing the new season’s tone and character designs, but viewers should not treat short promotional footage as a full story outline. The official site has not announced the episode total, opening or ending songs, weekly broadcast day, or a release calendar for territories outside Japan. We will update this guide when the production or a licensed distributor confirms those details. What story will Season 2 cover? The official Season 2 introduction gives a clearer premise than speculation based on the teaser. After welcoming the legendary Creation Dragon Ouma and Kuro—the embodiment of “Evil” hidden inside Yuti—into his group and defeating the Fist Saint, Yuya trains to make the newly acquired power of Evil his own. At the same time, the forces of Evil continue to grow. In the otherworldly Kingdom of Regar, a formal match is arranged between Yuya and the strongest Holy Sword Saint. That setup signals two connected pressures: Yuya must understand a dangerous power, while a public contest in Regar puts him against a renowned opponent. The series’ central appeal remains the link between an ordinary modern setting and a fantasy world, but the official synopsis does not explain the full outcome of the duel or identify which light-novel volumes Season 2 adapts. Those details should remain open until the anime staff publishes a longer synopsis. Who joins the Season 2 cast? The October 15 cast release adds Ikumi Hasegawa as Iris Noublade and Sora Amamiya as Mai Kagurazaka . In her official comment, Hasegawa describes Iris as strong, dignified and cool, and says viewers should watch how her relationship with Yuya develops. Amamiya describes Mai as a mysterious shrine maiden who can be prickly yet considerate, with a shy side. The production has not yet detailed how either character enters the story beyond those comments and the official character listing. The returning principal cast listed on the Season 2 page includes Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Yuya Tenjo, Akari Kito as Kaori Hojo, Kaori Maeda as Lexia von Arselia, Ai Kakuma as Luna, Rina Hidaka as Yuti and Marina Inoue as Kuro. This is a useful confirmed lineup, though it should not be read as a complete cast list for every character in the new arc. Who is making the new season? The official staff page credits Shin Itagaki as director and Hiromi Kimura for character design. Millepensee is the animation studio, with Akihiro Tachibana and SHIKI credited for music and UNLIMITED PRODUCE by TMS for planning and production. The source novels are written by Miku and illustrated by Rein Kuwashima , under KADOKAWA’s Fantasia Bunko imprint. These credits give readers a concrete way to distinguish confirmed production information from fan guesses about staff changes. Is there an official Season 2 trailer? Yes. The official site dates “2nd Season PV 1” to October 15, 2026, and links directly to the video. The official announcement supplies the publication date but does not state the exact upload time or time zone. Because that precision is not available from the cited announcement, AniNextUp does not present an exact timestamp or a VideoObject uploadDate for this PV. Use the official video link below; if the embedded preview does not load, the YouTube link remains available. What is still unconfirmed? As of October 25, 2026, there is no official exact January premiere date, broadcast hour, episode count, confirmed international simulcast, or full territory-by-territory viewing list in the cited Season 2 materials. There is also no official statement here naming the exact light-novel volumes adapted. These are genuine gaps in the announcement, not clues that viewers should fill with an assumed date or platform. For reliable updates, check the official Iseleve news page , the official Season 2 story introduction , the Season 2 staff and cast list , and KADOKAWA’s Season 2 listing . AniNextUp will revise the release and viewing details when an exact schedule or regional platform is announced. Updated: October 25, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error

entries.description: I Lost My Adventurer's License anime premieres in January 2027. See the teaser, Douglas and Rabi's voice cast, studio and what remains unconfirmed.
entries.content: OFFICIAL ANIME NEWS · OCTOBER 15, 2026 I Lost My Adventurer's License Anime: January 2027 Premiere, Trailer and Cast The fantasy series about Douglas and Rabi is set to begin airing in Japan in January 2027. A new teaser video, promotional visual and the main cast and staff have been announced. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Previously released official announcement artwork featuring Douglas and Rabi, via Comic Natalie . The October 2026 teaser visual is available on the official anime website . © Manimani Ononata / SB Creative / anime production committee. Release at a glance Japanese premiere January 2027; exact date pending Animation studio studio Palette Main cast Hiroki Yasumoto as Douglas; Yuka Iguchi as Rabi Streaming Not officially announced Verified October 15, 2026 against the official anime website . When does I Lost My Adventurer's License premiere? I Lost My Adventurer's License, but It's Fine Because I Have an Adorable Daughter Now is scheduled to premiere on Japanese television in January 2027. The production confirmed the month in its October 15, 2026 update, alongside a teaser visual and promotional video. An exact broadcast day and time have not yet been disclosed. The January announcement gives fans a confirmed seasonal window, but it should not be confused with a specific worldwide streaming launch. The official production has not confirmed an international platform or regional release schedule. Does the January 2027 announcement confirm a worldwide release? No. The production's October 15 teaser confirms a Japanese television premiere window in January 2027, not a global simulcast schedule. A teaser PV and promotional visual show that the adaptation is being promoted, but neither identifies an international streaming service or an exact episode date. Viewers outside Japan should check a future licensed distributor announcement rather than assume the Japanese broadcast date applies to their region. New teaser trailer and visual revealed The October 15 update introduced a teaser PV and a new promotional visual for the TV anime. Both are available from the official production website , which also links to the anime's official X account . Watch the official teaser embedded below rather than fan-edited or unofficial reuploads. The illustration above is from the earlier anime announcement and is labeled accordingly, not presented as the new October key visual. Watch the official January 2027 teaser trailer The production released its first teaser PV on October 15, 2026. Watch the official video below, sourced directly from the anime's production website. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Teaser PV · October 15, 2026 Official production announcement . Who voices Douglas and Rabi? Hiroki Yasumoto voices Douglas , a former legendary magician whose declining strength leaves him without his adventurer's license. Yuka Iguchi voices Rabi , a young girl Douglas encounters while wandering. Their developing father-daughter bond is central to the adaptation. Both performers were announced with comments about their characters and the story on October 15. Additional voice cast members have not yet been detailed in the same announcement. Which studio is animating the series? studio Palette is producing the animation. Yuki Inaba directs and also oversees series composition and scripts. Kaori Yoshikawa handles character design and serves as chief animation director. Ohshu and Daiki Okuno compose the music, with SPACE SHOWER MUSIC responsible for music production. What is the anime about? Douglas was once a powerful enhancement magician, but age and changing circumstances cost him his position in the hero's party and ultimately his adventurer's license. After meeting Rabi, a cursed girl with no family to turn to, he begins a new journey with her. The story mixes fantasy quests and travel with everyday moments as Douglas and Rabi gradually grow closer. It adapts the light novel written by Manimani Ononata and illustrated by Fuzichoco, published under SB Creative's GA Novel imprint. A manga adaptation is also available through Square Enix's Manga UP! service. Where can you watch I Lost My Adventurer's License? No international streaming platform has been confirmed in the October 15 announcement. A Japanese television premiere in January 2027 does not automatically establish a Crunchyroll, Netflix or other international release. AniNextUp will update this guide when a distributor announces official availability. Where can readers find the manga? The original story is a light novel by Manimani Ononata with illustrations by Fuzichoco. A manga adaptation is also available in English through Square Enix's Manga UP! listing , which credits Manimani Ononata, Fumi Tadaura, Itsuki Watanabe and Fuzichoco. The listing provides a way to sample the story while waiting for the television adaptation. Douglas and Rabi's journey combines encounters with danger and quieter moments of companionship. Their bond is the center of the announced premise, but the production has not said how many manga chapters or novel volumes will be covered in the anime. What did the October announcement add? The adaptation itself was announced before the October update. The newer announcement supplied a January 2027 Japanese broadcast window, a teaser, the two lead voice actors and the main production staff. It did not include an exact day, an episode count or a named international streaming partner. For the next update, check the official anime website for Japanese broadcast details and a distributor's own announcement for regional viewing information. A promotional video can introduce the characters without functioning as a complete release schedule. Frequently asked questions Is the January 2027 premiere official? Yes. The official anime website lists January 2027 as the Japanese broadcast window. Has an exact release date been announced? No. As of October 15, 2026, only the month and year are confirmed. Who are the lead voice actors? Hiroki Yasumoto plays Douglas and Yuka Iguchi plays Rabi. Is the anime coming to Crunchyroll or Netflix? Neither service has been confirmed for this title in the announcement covered here. Official sources and further reading Official anime website and October 15 announcements · Official production account · Crunchyroll's announcement report · ORICON staff and cast details . Explore other confirmed anime news in AniNextUp's latest updates and track upcoming premieres in the anime release calendar . Updated: October 26, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error

Release date, studio and streaming details for Fall 2026. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases RELEASE DATE October 8, 2026 STREAMING Crunchyroll STUDIO ZERO-G Release at a glance Release October 8, 2026 Where to watch Crunchyroll in licensed territories Region and timing International simulcast. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Crunchyroll’s Fall 2026 anime lineup · The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World official site What carries over into the second season Ray's relationships with his friends remain the entry point to a continuation that introduces the Magicks War between rival schools. The school conflict provides an immediate source of tension, while the announced darker threat suggests that the stakes extend beyond the competition. The premise does not yet explain how those threats connect, so their relationship should not be presented as confirmed. How to compare the two Japanese broadcasts TBS and BS11 have separate broadcast slots, so the October 8 and October 9 listings do not indicate two different season premieres. They describe when the same continuation reaches different Japanese channels. For international viewers, check the current Crunchyroll simulcast hour; a Japanese broadcast time cannot establish that by itself. When does The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World II premiere? The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World II is scheduled for October 8, 2026 . The announced streaming platform is Crunchyroll . Related reading: Full Clearing Another World under a Goddess with Zero Believers: Premiere, Cast, Streaming and Official Trailer . Season 2 Episode 1 release time Crunchyroll's updated Fall 2026 lineup lists subtitled episodes on Thursdays at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time. Check the local episode listing for regional availability. In Japan, the official schedule lists TBS in the Thursday, October 8 late-night slot at 1:28 a.m., equivalent to Friday, October 9 at 1:28 a.m. JST in ordinary calendar notation. BS11 follows on October 9 at 11:00 p.m. JST. Japan broadcast time vs. international streaming The TBS Thursday late-night listing corresponds to October 9 at 1:28 a.m. JST, rather than the early morning of October 8. It does not establish the release hour for Crunchyroll viewers in other countries. BS11 has a separate Japanese broadcast on October 9 at 11:00 p.m. JST. The official Japanese streaming schedule lists d Anime Store, U-NEXT and Anime Hodai from October 8 at 25:58, equivalent to October 9 at 1:58 a.m. JST. For an international episode reminder, use the local Crunchyroll listing for the current simulcast time rather than converting the TBS time into a presumed worldwide release. What the Magicks War adds to the sequel The announced competition between rival schools creates a visible challenge for Ray and his friends, while the promotional premise also points to a separate, darker danger. That contrast is the useful distinction for returning viewers: a school contest is not necessarily the full scope of the new season. The published synopsis does not explain how the two conflicts intersect or who ultimately prevails, so those outcomes remain open. Related reading: In a World Full of Zombies Anime: January 2027 Premiere, New Trailer, Cast and Music . What is it about? Ray and his friends face the Magicks War between rival schools while a darker threat emerges. Watch the official Season 2 trailer Where can you watch it? Announced availability: North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, CIS, Southeast Asia and Korea. Related reading: Kagurabachi Episodes 1–2 to Premiere March 25, 2027: World Tour Finale Details . More Fall 2026 anime See the AniNextUp Fall 2026 calendar and our where-to-watch guide for more confirmed releases. Official source View the official announcement → Release dates, times and streaming availability can vary by region. AniNextUp updates guides when new official information is confirmed. What happens at the start of Season 2? The official episode introduction describes the Magicks War as a newly organized team competition that crosses academy boundaries. Ray White forms a team with Amelia Rose and Ariane Olgren, while Evi and Albert also prepare to enter. Ray gives Amelia and Ariane separate training to address their weaknesses before the contest. This setup gives returning viewers a clear point of entry: the season brings familiar students together around a contest, while their preparation and relationships create challenges of their own. The official summary of the next episode also describes Ariane visiting Ray's family home for training. These are introductory details, not a claim about the tournament's eventual winner or later revelations. Who voices Ray and his friends in Japanese? TBS credits Junya Enoki as Ray White, Iori Saeki as Amelia Rose and Akira Sekine as Ariane Olgren. The broadcaster's cast listing also names Miyu Kubota as Elisa Griffith, Azumi Waki as Rebecca Bradley and Kaede Hondo as Clarisse Cleveland. These are the Japanese voice credits; cast and audio availability can differ for other language editions. TBS lists Masahiro Takata as director, series composer and sound director for this season, with Mariko Kawamoto handling character design and ZERO-G producing the animation. The first season's credits and the new season's credits should be checked separately when comparing the production teams. Opening and ending songs The official music page identifies “Diamond Dust” by Sizuk as the opening and “COMPRESSION :[” by Maaya Uchida as the ending. The production announced creditless versions of the first episode's opening and ending on October 9. Those videos present the theme sequences without the usual overlaid credits; they are promotional clips rather than additional episodes. Is there an English dub? Crunchyroll announced on October 24 that the Season 2 English dub was streaming, with Kevin D. Thelwell as Ray and Alexis Tipton as Amelia in its Episode 1 cast listing. Check the series page in your country for currently available dubbed episodes and languages; a dub announcement does not establish the same rollout for every territory. Sources checked October 26, 2026: the official anime website, TBS and Crunchyroll. Broadcast and streaming schedules can change. entries.content: UPDATED OCTOBER 25, 2026 · FALL 2026 #I'm Looking For a Zombie: Release Date, Schedule & Story The October 3 premiere is underway in Japan. See the official Saturday broadcast and streaming times, the series’ zombie-comedy premise, confirmed cast and staff, theme songs, and what viewers outside Japan should check. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases JAPANESE PREMIERE October 3, 2026 STREAMING Regional availability varies STUDIO studio COMET Release at a glance Japanese TV premiere October 3, 2026 · Saturday at 11:30 p.m. JST on TV Asahi’s 24-station IMAnimation block Japan streaming ABEMA and d Anime Store · Saturdays at 24:00 JST; other services listed from October 8 Studio studio COMET Outside Japan Check your regional catalog; service and episode times vary Schedule checked October 25, 2026 · Official broadcast and streaming schedule OFFICIAL VIDEO Watch the main PV ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL MAIN PV Opens the official YouTube video The official anime video page links to this main PV. The official pages reviewed do not expose its exact upload hour and timezone, so AniNextUp reports no uploadDate in structured video data. When did #I'm Looking for a Zombie premiere? #I'm Looking for a Zombie began its Japanese television run on October 3, 2026. The official anime website lists the Saturday premiere in TV Asahi's nationwide 24-station IMAnimation block, with BS Asahi and AT-X carrying separate schedules. The official site also lists Japanese streaming services and weekly release times, which are more useful than treating “October 3” as one universal drop time. What is the Japanese broadcast schedule? The official broadcast and streaming schedule gives TV Asahi's IMAnimation slot as every Saturday at 11:30 p.m. Japan time, starting October 3. BS Asahi lists the same start date and a 1:00 a.m. late-night slot; AT-X began on Monday, October 5 at 9:00 p.m., with repeat broadcasts Wednesday morning and Friday afternoon. Japanese schedules sometimes describe after-midnight times as part of the previous evening, so viewers should check the station's calendar for the actual local date as well as the clock time. The official page warns that broadcast times can change. ABEMA and d Anime Store are listed for the earliest Japanese stream, every Saturday at 24:00 from October 3. In ordinary calendar notation, 24:00 Saturday is midnight at the start of Sunday. The official schedule then lists a wider group of on-demand services from Thursday, October 8 at 24:00, including U-NEXT, Anime Hodai, Nico Nico, DMM TV, Lemino, FOD, Bandai Channel, Hulu, TELASA, Prime Video and TVer. The page also names pay-per-view services separately. These are Japanese listings; they do not establish that each service is available in another country. Related reading: Dandivine Release Date & Where to Watch: Japan Schedule, Cast and Story . Where can viewers outside Japan watch? Availability depends on country and platform rights. The official Japanese schedule confirms domestic stations and services, but the sources reviewed for this update do not confirm a current international platform list or one global release hour. Check the anime’s listing in your own regional catalog for audio, subtitles and episode timing; Japanese ABEMA and d Anime Store availability should not be assumed abroad. What is the story about? The official series introduction sets the story thirteen years after “Akai Hi,” a mysterious outbreak that infected and killed 90 percent of humanity. Survivors left the cities and built isolated villages. Aki is part of a younger generation that has no memory of the pre-collapse world. She leaves her village with childhood friends Natsuki and Haru to look for her father, who went away earlier. They encounter zombies outside, but the official premise also describes the ruined world as vast, unfamiliar and beautiful. Yuu and Sakura join them along the way. That contrast explains the series' “non-everyday” comedy angle: the setting is dangerous, while the characters' curiosity about abandoned places and ordinary remnants of civilization gives the journey a lighter, exploratory mood. The official premise does not disclose the father's fate, so a release guide should not present a reunion or final answer as confirmed. The title's hashtag is part of its Japanese branding, and the story is adapted from Katsuwo's manga rather than an original television script. Related reading: Akane-banashi Season 2 Release Date: January 2027 and Story . Who voices the characters, and who makes the anime? The official cast page lists Kyori Nemoto as Aki, Lynn as Natsuki, Toshiya Miyata as Haru, Hibiki Yamamura as Yuu and Yuka Nukui as Sakura. Additional listed characters include Mikazuki, voiced by Yoko Hikasa, and Aki's father, voiced by Kosuke Toriumi. Shinya Une directs the television anime at studio COMET. Kyohei Suzuki is assistant director; Kenichi Yamashita and Aki Itami handle series composition and scripts; Narumi Shimoji designs the characters; and Kenta Higashiohji composes the music. These credits matter for viewers comparing the series with Katsuwo's earlier comedy work: the official staff information confirms the same creator's manga adaptation, while the animation and television storytelling are handled by a separate production team. What are the opening and ending songs? The official music page names “Raki Raki” by Surii as the opening theme and “Soft Apocalypse” by cadode as the ending theme. The music is part of the series' tonal contrast: the story moves through a zombie-affected landscape, but its presentation is not described by the official site as nonstop horror. The main PV introduces the anime's cast and setting alongside the opening song. AniNextUp links the official main PV below; the official video listing reviewed for this update does not show the exact original upload hour and timezone, so no VideoObject uploadDate is asserted. Related reading: The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Schedule & Where to Watch . Is the original manga finished? KADOKAWA lists three collected volumes of Katsuwo's #ゾンビさがしてます (“#I'm Looking for a Zombie”), with the third volume released January 26, 2024. The publisher's description for the final volume follows Aki and her friends as they trace a message from her father to Tokyo Tower. That lets manga readers understand that the source has a finite three-volume run; it does not confirm how many chapters the anime adapts or whether the television version changes the ending. Viewers who want to avoid spoilers can begin with the anime, while readers who want the complete original story can look for all three volumes through KADOKAWA and their usual book retailers. What is confirmed, and what should viewers still check? The confirmed essentials are the October 3 Japanese premiere, the named Japanese weekly schedule, the domestic streaming services, the principal premise, cast, staff and songs. The official sources reviewed here do not provide one worldwide release hour, a single global platform list, or an episode count in the schedule page. Those details can vary by license and should be checked against the current local service. For weekly changes, use the official schedule and official video page ; the latter links the main PV and character videos. This keeps a useful viewing guide clear about the difference between Japan's confirmed timetable and information that depends on a viewer's region. entries.title: In a World Full of Zombies Anime: January 2027 Premiere, New Trailer, Cast and Music
entries.description: The zombie-survival anime arrives on AT-X in January 2027. The official October 10 trailer confirms more cast members and opening and ending songs.
entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · OCTOBER 14, 2026 In a World Full of Zombies Anime: January 2027 Premiere, New Trailer, Cast and Music A main promotional video and new character voices bring the January 2027 adaptation into clearer focus, but an exact premiere day and international streaming service remain unconfirmed. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy Official promotional key visual · © Rokuro Uraji / Frontier Works / Zom-Ore Production Committee. Image distributed with the official press announcement. Release at a glance Japan premiere January 2027; exact day TBA Japanese broadcaster AT-X Animation Acca effe × Frontier Engine International streaming Not announced In a World Full of Zombies I'm the Only One Who Doesn't Get Attacked has a new main trailer, an official key visual and two more confirmed Japanese voice actors. Publisher Frontier Works announced the material on October 10, 2026 , giving viewers a fuller picture of the adaptation before its scheduled January 2027 broadcast in Japan. The update does not establish an exact premiere date, an episode count or an international streaming partner. Those details should remain open rather than be inferred from the release month. When does the zombie anime premiere? The official anime website identifies January 2027 on AT-X as the Japanese broadcast window. AT-X is the named Japanese broadcaster, not a guarantee that the show will appear on a particular international service. Neither a precise broadcast day nor a worldwide simulcast schedule is provided in the October 10 production announcement. Related reading: Full Clearing Another World under a Goddess with Zero Believers: Premiere, Cast, Streaming and Official Trailer . For a calendar reminder, January is currently the most specific defensible date. AniNextUp will add a day and time only after an official schedule is published. Watch the official October 10 main trailer The new promotional video is a main PV , following the earlier teaser. It is hosted on YouTube and linked directly by Frontier Works, rather than uploaded by an unofficial fan channel. The embedded player below opens the publisher-linked trailer. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Official main promotional video New cast announced for the anime The October announcement adds Rikako Ito as Tokiko Kurose and Marie Miyake as Sayaka Makiura . They join the previously revealed central performers Wataru Kato as Yusuke Takemura and Yuno Azuma as Mitsuki Fujino . Who is making the adaptation? Kazuya Fujishiro directs the television anime, with Yasushi Hirano overseeing series composition. Kayo Shimoyama and Makuto Okimi are credited with scripts, Megumi Ishihara with character design, and ISAO with music. Animation production is credited jointly to Acca effe and Frontier Engine . These roles come from the official Japanese staff listing; they should not be confused with unannounced English dub credits. Opening and ending songs confirmed The opening song is “No Reaction” by Retbear , featuring the anonymously credited vocalist unknown Vo: 0in . Retbear is a music project associated with producer Kairiki Bear. The ending is “Tsukikage” by the performance group Itsuka Saisei . Both songs were announced alongside the new trailer. Their inclusion in the publicity package is confirmed; a full soundtrack release date was not supplied in the sources reviewed for this guide. What is the story about? Yusuke Takemura discovers that a zombie outbreak has devastated the world around him. Unlike other survivors, however, he appears not to attract attacks from the infected. That unusual advantage changes the usual survival-horror premise: instead of simply fleeing danger, Yusuke must decide what to do with his relative freedom while other people remain at risk. The story originated in novels by Rokuro Uraji , illustrated by Saburo , and also has a manga adaptation drawn by Chihiro Masuda . Official promotional material presents the series as a darker, adult-oriented zombie action story; viewers should not assume it follows the tone of a conventional all-ages adventure. What the new key visual confirms—and why it is not reproduced here An original production key visual was released on October 10 and can be viewed on the official anime website . Its provenance is verified, but a publicly displayed image is not automatically licensed for republication. Until explicit permission or an applicable reuse license is established, AniNextUp is withholding the cover rather than substituting generated artwork, a homemade SVG or an unrelated thumbnail. Copyright attribution supplied by the rights holder: © Rokuro Uraji / Frontier Works / Zom-Ore Production Committee . Attribution does not itself grant permission to reproduce the artwork. Why the protagonist's immunity changes the premise The official synopsis describes Yusuke as someone zombies do not attack while other survivors remain vulnerable. This changes a familiar survival-horror expectation: his challenge is not simply escaping the infected, but navigating a crisis that affects other people differently. That is an interpretation of the premise, not confirmation of how he uses the advantage or who survives. Where can viewers watch it outside Japan? The confirmed broadcaster is AT-X in Japan. No international streaming platform, territory list or local release time is established by the October 10 official announcement. Even though some anime news outlets cover the project, their reporting does not by itself constitute a streaming license announcement. What should fans watch for next? The next material update would be an exact Japanese premiere day, additional broadcast or streaming arrangements, an episode count or new production announcements. If those details emerge, this article should be updated at the same URL rather than creating a duplicate news page. For confirmed schedules and other upcoming titles, browse AniNextUp's anime release calendar , latest anime news and The Fable Season 2 January 2027 guide . Official sources and verification Frontier Works, October 10, 2026 — main trailer, key visual, Japanese broadcast month, new cast, themes and staff. Official anime website — AT-X and January 2027 schedule. Official publisher-linked YouTube trailer — promotional video. entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · OCTOBER 13, 2026 Inherit the Winds: January 2027 Anime, Cast & Theater Preview The original Shinsengumi anime Inherit the Winds is scheduled for Japanese television in January 2027. Its production has also revealed a new illustration for the limited theatrical preview beginning November 13, 2026. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy The newly revealed October 13 visual is available on the production's website . The cover above is an earlier official teaser visual, not the newly announced October 13 illustration. Release at a glance TV premiere January 2027; exact date not announced Japanese broadcast CBC/TBS network, Agaru Anime, Sundays at 11:30 p.m. JST Theatrical preview November 13, 2026; limited two-week Japan run International streaming Not confirmed Official anime website When does Inherit the Winds premiere? Inherit the Winds (Japanese title Kaze wo Tsugu Mono , 風を継ぐもの) is scheduled to begin Japanese television broadcast in January 2027 . The official announcement places it in CBC and TBS's Sunday “Agaru Anime” block at 11:30 p.m. Japan Standard Time (JST, UTC+9) , carried on 28 network stations. The first episode's exact calendar date has not been announced. A limited theater edition opens first, but it is separate from the regular TV premiere. November 13 theater preview: what audiences need to know The theatrical edition, titled Inherit the Winds: Hajimari , opens in Japan on November 13, 2026 for a limited two-week engagement. The official site describes it as a theatrical advance screening before TV. The cited notice does not state a runtime, total episode count or international cinema rollout. A November Japanese screening date does not establish a release elsewhere. Aniplex has announced cast appearances at selected screenings on November 13 and 14. On opening day, the schedule lists Shinjuku Wald 9 after the 10:00 screening and before the 12:50 screening; TOHO Cinemas Hibiya after the 13:40 screening and before the 16:45 screening; and United Cinemas Toyosu after the 17:10 screening and before the 19:55 screening. On November 14, greetings are scheduled at United Cinemas Aqua City Odaiba after the 11:55 screening and before the 15:00 screening, and at TOHO Cinemas Shinjuku after the 15:25 screening and before the 18:30 screening. All times are Japan local time. Standard reserved tickets cost ¥3,000; Hibiya premium seats cost ¥4,100 or ¥6,200, and Toyosu paired seats cost ¥7,700. Guests may change, so check Aniplex's notice before traveling. The first-week gift is a B6 illustration card drawn by character designer Fumi Ebina, offered November 13–19 while supplies last. A second card begins November 20 and is designed to connect with the first, but its details were still pending in Aniplex's October 19 notice. These are cinema attendance bonuses, not a streaming extra or a guarantee that every theater will have stock. What is the story about? The original historical drama begins in Kyoto in June 1863, during the Bakumatsu period. A young man with no memory is brought to the Mibu Roshigumi quarters. Soji Okita gives him the name Jinsuke Tachikawa, and the story follows his life among the group as it grows into the Shinsengumi. The official synopsis makes Jinsuke's lost memories central: recovering them is expected to change the world around him. The setting draws on a real historical organization, but Jinsuke and his personal mystery belong to the anime's fictional narrative, not a documentary account. The October 13 theatrical visual shows Jinsuke, Okita and Hyogo Koganei beneath a blue sky, while the article's hero is an earlier official teaser and is captioned as such. The production describes the series as a story about young people caught in a turbulent era. Confirmed cast and production Daisuke Sakuma voices Jinsuke Tachikawa, Yuki Kaji is Soji Okita, Aoi Yuki is Hyogo Koganei, Koki Uchiyama is Toshizo Hijikata and Yuichi Nakamura is Isami Kondo. The announced supporting cast includes Nichika Omori as Kurosuke, Takeo Otsuka as Keisuke Yamanami, Shimba Tsuchiya as Sanosuke Harada, Ryohei Kimura as Shinpachi Nagakura, Ayumu Murase as Heisuke Todo and Yasuyuki Kase as Kamo Serizawa. Takaya Kamikawa has a special appearance as Shinbei Umeda. This confirms the named ensemble, not which characters appear in every episode. Tomohiro Kawamura directs, Yutaka Narui writes the series, Fumi Ebina designs the characters and Shigeru Kishida composes the score. Live2D Creative Studio and Drive are credited with animation production. The official site describes a blend of Live2D techniques and cel animation. The site presents that combination as the production approach; it does not say every scene uses one method. Related reading: GROTESQQQUE Release Date: November 6, Netflix Preview & Stories . Where can you watch it? The confirmed television outlet is the Japanese CBC/TBS network block. As of October 25, 2026, the official announcements reviewed here do not name a streaming service or confirm international broadcast rights. Viewers outside Japan should wait for a local distributor announcement rather than assume the title will appear on a particular anime platform. The November theater preview is also confirmed for Japan in the sources below. Check Aniplex's theater and ticket notices for event availability or schedule changes. For the TV run, the exact January date, episode schedule and streaming or subtitle information remain unannounced. Official trailers and sources The official anime website hosts the teaser, first promotional video, cast videos and theatrical preview trailer. Reach the originals through the official video and news sections . The exact original YouTube upload hour and timezone for the trailers could not be verified from those official pages, so this article does not embed a player or publish VideoObject upload metadata. A news post's publication time is not proof of a video's upload timestamp. Official January 2027 TV and broadcast-slot announcement October 13 theatrical visual November 13–14 stage-greeting schedule and ticket details First- and second-week theater gifts Frequently asked questions Is there an exact January 2027 release date? No. January 2027 and the Sunday 11:30 p.m. JST slot are confirmed; the first-episode date has not been announced. Can I stream the November 13 version? No online release is confirmed in the cited sources. November 13 is the start of a limited Japanese theatrical engagement for Hajimari . Is the anime based on a manga? The official site calls this an original TV anime. It uses the Mibu Roshigumi and Shinsengumi as its historical setting, with an original amnesia mystery at its center; the cited announcements do not describe it as a manga adaptation. Release and event information checked October 25, 2026. Broadcast dates, theater schedules and attendance benefits can change; confirm with Aniplex before making plans. entries.content: OFFICIAL ANIME NEWS · OCTOBER 17, 2026 Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san? Anime Release Date: January 7, 2027 The romantic school comedy has an official January 7, 2027 broadcast date in Japan, in the Thursday late-night 24:26 JST slot (January 8 at 00:26 JST on a standard calendar). The official site confirms a simultaneous broadcast across 28 MBS/TBS network stations; international streaming has not been announced. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official promotional visual. Source and artwork credit: official anime website . Release at a glance Japanese premiere January 7, 2027 (Japanese late-night broadcast date) Broadcast MBS/TBS Super Animeism TURBO; 28 stations Animation studio SynergySP International streaming Not announced; official site says streaming details are coming soon Checked against the official anime website . When does Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san? premiere? Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san? begins airing in Japan on the January 7, 2027 late-night broadcast slot (January 8 at 00:26 JST on a standard calendar). The official schedule places the series in MBS and TBS’s Super Animeism TURBO block, with a simultaneous broadcast across 28 stations. Japanese late-night schedules sometimes write this as Thursday at 24:26; it is the same slot as Friday at 12:26 a.m. by calendar time. The official website lists the broadcast date and time, but its streaming section currently says “Coming soon.” No international platform or regional streaming date has been confirmed there. What is the anime about? English-language sources use both Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san? and the earlier rendering Are You a Jirai Girl, Chihara-san? . The English manga publisher Seven Seas uses the Landmine title; earlier anime coverage used the Jirai Girl rendering. AniNextUp keeps both names here to make the series easier to find. Related reading: Takopi's Original Sin: Thank You, See You Tomorrow Release Date . The story follows high-school student Kuroki, who is seated next to Mai Chihara at the start of a new school term. Rumors and Chihara’s dark “jirai-kei” fashion make her seem intimidating. As Kuroki gets to know her, he finds that the girl behind the reputation is more unexpected—and often more awkward—than the rumors suggest. The official site describes it as a school comedy about the classmates’ changing impressions of each other. Cast and staff The official cast includes Sayumi Suzushiro as Mai Chihara , Kazuki Ura as Kuroki , Maaya Uchida as Chinatsu Iwakura , Tomokazu Sugita as Hibiya and Daisuke Ono as Kazami . Yasuaki Fujii directs, Keiichiro Ochi handles series composition, and SynergySP produces the animation. Related reading: Walking Home with You Anime . Watch the official teaser The production’s teaser PV is available from the anime’s official channels. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TEASER January 2027 TV anime Official anime website and broadcast details . What is still unconfirmed? The Japanese premiere date and time are confirmed. An international streaming service and regional availability have not been announced on the official site. AniNextUp will update this page when the production or a licensed distributor confirms more. Explore more confirmed anime news and track scheduled premieres in the AniNextUp release calendar . How to read the Japanese broadcast time The official website lists January 7, 2027 at 0:26 and names the MBS/TBS network of 28 stations. In Japan, programs after midnight are often described as a late-night slot attached to the preceding evening, which can make listings look like they disagree by one date. The production describes the slot as Thursday night beginning January 7 at 0:26. Read as a Thursday-night schedule, that corresponds to Friday January 8 at 00:26 JST; check the broadcaster’s detailed listing for confirmation before setting a reminder. Viewers outside Japan should convert that timestamp to their own time zone rather than copying a “late night” label as a local date. The site currently marks streaming information as coming soon. That is a real boundary on what this guide can promise: the Japanese television schedule is confirmed, while no international platform or regional release time has been named in the source reviewed here. A broadcaster’s 28-station network also does not mean the show is automatically available on a streaming service in those same markets. Where can readers find the manga? The original manga is written and illustrated by Ryon. Seven Seas Entertainment publishes it in English as Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san? and lists the first volume for October 13, 2026. The publisher also references the alternate English rendering, Are You a Jirai Girl, Chihara-san? Both titles refer to the same work. The story's school comedy begins with Kuroki judging his new seatmate by her reputation and fashion, then gradually discovering a different side of Mai. Readers can explore the manga ahead of the television adaptation without treating its volume schedule as a guide to the anime's episode count. Where should international viewers check for streaming? The production's official on-air page lists Japanese television details and marks streaming information as coming soon. A later platform announcement will be needed to establish the licensed service, territory and local release time. The Japanese station schedule does not by itself confirm a worldwide simulcast. What makes Mai and Kuroki’s dynamic the hook The official synopsis begins with a class change and a seat beside Mai Chihara, whose appearance has made classmates call her dangerous. Kuroki’s first impression changes as he sees that her reserved look hides a more open, unpredictable and sometimes clumsy personality. The comedy grows from the distance between a rumor and the person sitting next to him, with their ordinary pauses and conversations doing as much work as the bigger gags. The official cast and staff page names Sayumi Suzushiro as Mai and Kazuki Ura as Kuroki; it also credits SynergySP for animation. Those details let readers identify the announced production without inventing a studio or character dynamic from fan assumptions. The official Japanese title, Jirai Nan Desu ka? Chihara-san , and the English publisher’s “Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san?” are both useful search terms. International streaming, an English dub and a regional premiere time remain unconfirmed. Updated: October 26, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error

entries.title: Kagurabachi Episodes 1–2 to Premiere March 25, 2027: World Tour Finale Details

entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · OCTOBER 12, 2026 Kagurabachi Episodes 1–2 to Premiere March 25, 2027: World Tour Finale Details The anime’s Japan finale will screen two complete episodes before its April 2027 television debut. Here are the confirmed dates, venues and remaining unknowns. By AniNextUp Editorial Team Official Kagurabachi anime promotional art published by Japan Expo for the world tour. © Takeru Hokazono/SHUEISHA, Project Kagurabachi. Release at a glance Release March 25, 2027: episodes 1–2 advance screening Where to watch Kabukiza Theatre, Tokyo; Japanese cinema live screenings planned Applies to Japan event, not worldwide streaming premiere Still pending Start time, participating cinemas and tickets Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Official source When do Kagurabachi episodes 1 and 2 premiere? Kagurabachi will hold the world premiere of its first two complete TV anime episodes on Thursday, March 25, 2027 , at the Kabukiza Theatre in Ginza, Tokyo. The event concludes the production’s international anime world tour. Japanese cinemas will also host live screenings of the finale, allowing audiences beyond the Tokyo venue to see the episodes and the accompanying stage presentation. The official announcement, dated October 12, 2026, confirms the screening date but does not yet specify the starting time, participating cinemas or ticket-sale schedule . Those details will be announced separately. The March event is an advance screening, not the start of the regular television broadcast. Read the anime’s official announcement. Can fans watch the March 25 screening online? The official event announcement confirms a March 25, 2027 Kabukiza screening of Episodes 1 and 2 and a live relay to participating Japanese cinemas. It does not announce a public internet livestream or a worldwide online premiere. The regular anime simulcast is separately scheduled for April 2027 on Crunchyroll. See the official simulcast confirmation. Related reading: Prisma Illya FINALE: 2027 Release, Cast & Broadcast Update . What happens at the Japan world tour finale? The Tokyo finale combines the two-episode premiere with an onstage discussion. Announced guests include Taihi Kimura, who voices Chihiro Rokuhira; Tomokazu Seki, who plays Kunishige Rokuhira; and Katsuyuki Konishi, who voices Togo Shiba. The venue is the Kabukiza Theatre, at 4-12-15 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo. The expansion from an early 20-minute preview to two full episodes is the key change in this announcement. Earlier tour stops offered a glimpse of the first episode, whereas the finale will let attendees see how the adaptation opens across its first two installments. No public online simulcast of the Tokyo event has been confirmed. Singapore, Seoul and Brazil: world tour Part 3 dates Before the finale, three more destinations will screen the opening 20 minutes of episode 1 . These are previews, not screenings of the complete two-episode premiere: Related reading: Full Clearing Another World under a Goddess with Zero Believers: Premiere, Cast, Streaming and Official Trailer . Singapore — November 29, 2026: Anime Festival Asia at Suntec Singapore Convention & Exhibition Centre, 4–5 p.m. Singapore time. Taihi Kimura and animation producer Kan Mizoguchi are scheduled to appear. Seoul — December 6, 2026: a preview and cast/staff event, with the venue and start time still unannounced. Kimura and Mizoguchi are listed as guests. São Paulo — December 2026: a preview at CCXP Brazil. The specific day and time have not yet been confirmed. The distinctions matter for fans searching for premiere dates: the Singapore, Seoul and São Paulo appearances feature only part of episode 1, while the March 2027 Tokyo finale features both full episodes. See the official world tour schedule for later updates. Is Kagurabachi still coming in April 2027? Yes. The regular TV anime broadcast and streaming launch remain scheduled for April 2027 . The production lists Crunchyroll, MUSE and SMG Holdings among its distribution partners, but this announcement does not provide an exact April premiere day, episode release times or a complete territory-by-territory streaming schedule. The March 25 screening should not be mistaken for a worldwide streaming release. Related reading: The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World II . The adaptation is produced by Cypic , directed by Tetsuya Takeuchi, with character designs by Keigo Sasaki. It adapts Takeru Hokazono’s Weekly Shonen Jump manga about Chihiro Rokuhira, a young swordsman pursuing the group responsible for his father’s death and the theft of powerful enchanted blades. The production has also shared a commemorative illustration by Takeuchi marking the manga’s third anniversary; that illustration is separate from the world tour event art. Watch the official Kagurabachi anime teaser The English-language teaser released by CyberAgent ANIME Global introduces the anime’s visual style and April 2027 broadcast window. It is an earlier official teaser, not a new October 12 trailer . ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TEASER The embedded player loads only when selected. How can viewers distinguish the tour stops? The official world-tour page lists each event separately. The Singapore, Seoul and Brazil stops are announced as previews of the opening 20 minutes of episode 1; the March 25 Tokyo finale is the announced screening of complete episodes 1 and 2. Dates, venues and ticket arrangements are event-specific. A ticket or screening announcement for one city does not establish access at another, and the Japan live cinema relay is not a confirmed public online stream. Check the organizer's page for the relevant stop before making travel plans. What fans should watch for next The most important remaining announcements are ticket details for the March 25 Japan premiere, the Seoul venue, the exact CCXP Brazil screening date, and the April 2027 TV premiere day. None should be treated as confirmed until the organizers publish them. For other announced releases, see AniNextUp’s anime release calendar and latest anime news . entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · OCTOBER 14, 2026 The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn't a Guy at All Anime: January 8, 2027 Premiere and Trailer The music-centered romance anime has a confirmed Japanese premiere date, a new promotional video and an expanded Japanese voice cast. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy Official anime promotional video thumbnail via the production trailer . © Sumiko Arai / KADOKAWA / Kinioto Production Committee. Release at a glance Japan premiere January 8, 2027, 11 p.m. JST Studio CloverWorks Broadcaster Nippon TV Streaming Crunchyroll (regional schedule pending) The upcoming adaptation of Sumiko Arai's music-centered romance now has a precise Japanese premiere date, a new full promotional video and an expanded voice cast. Here is what the official announcements establish, and what viewers still need to know before January. When is the anime release date? The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn't a Guy at All premieres in Japan on Friday, January 8, 2027. The official anime website lists weekly broadcasts at 11 p.m. Japan Standard Time. This is a new level of precision compared with the earlier January 2027 premiere window announced in July. A Japanese television debut is not necessarily an international streaming time. Crunchyroll has announced that it will carry the series, but the sources reviewed for this article do not confirm exact local release times or a complete list of territories. Those details should be checked closer to launch. Is January 8 the Crunchyroll release date everywhere? No. January 8, 2027 at 11 p.m. JST is the Japanese Nippon TV broadcast time confirmed by the anime production. Crunchyroll has announced that it will stream the series, but the sources cited here do not establish an identical release hour in every country. The Japanese television schedule and the international platform's local availability are two separate details. Related reading: The True Saint Was Banished Anime: January 2027 & Trailer . What is the anime about? Aya Osawa is a high school student who loves rock music. She meets a stylish employee at a CD shop and becomes fascinated by their shared musical taste. The employee is Mitsuki Koga, Aya's quiet female classmate, though Aya does not initially recognize that connection. The central drama comes from the contrast between Mitsuki's two environments: a reserved student at school and a more confident presence among records. Music provides a way for the characters to connect even when they struggle to express their feelings directly. Watch the official first trailer The first full promotional video, released in October, previews the characters' performances and the soundtrack. It is distinct from the earlier teaser released in July. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Official promotional video Who is in the cast? Mariya Ise voices Mitsuki Koga and Akari Kito voices Aya Osawa. The October announcement added five Japanese voice actors: Kenjiro Tsuda as Joe, Tasuku Hatanaka as Megumu Narita, Yurina Amami as Chizuru, Fairouz Ai as Mao and Maiko Nomura as Kanna. The reviewed announcements do not confirm an English-language dub cast. Japanese casting should not be presented as an international dub lineup. Studio, director and music Masashi Ishihama directs the series at CloverWorks. Rino Yamasaki handles series composition and Kanna Hirayama designs the characters. Kousuke Noma and Takayuki “Kojiro” Sasaki are credited with the music featured in the new PV. The opening theme previously announced for the anime is “Breed” by Nirvana. Its inclusion fits a story whose relationship begins with a shared love of rock. Music is central to the characters' identity, rather than merely background atmosphere. Where can fans watch it? Nippon TV is the confirmed Japanese broadcaster. Crunchyroll has announced streaming plans for 2027. Exact international release hours, territory-by-territory availability and episode count remain unconfirmed in the sources reviewed here. Where can readers find the manga? The anime adapts Sumiko Arai's manga, which English-language publisher Yen Press publishes. Its introductory description explains the misunderstanding at the heart of the story: Aya is attracted to the record-shop employee without recognizing that the person behind the counter is Mitsuki, her classmate. The setting gives the pair a shared language in music. Aya's outgoing personality and Mitsuki's quieter school presence also create different ways for them to approach the same feelings. Those contrasts are part of the announced premise; the anime's own episodes will determine how individual scenes from the manga are presented. What is confirmed about the music? The production has named Nirvana's “Breed” as the opening theme, and its earlier teaser uses the song. The official music announcement identifies the track separately from the original music credits for Kousuke Noma and Takayuki “Kojiro” Sasaki. Those announcements establish an opening selection and the credited music team, but do not give a complete episode-by-episode song list. For new trailers, episode dates and broadcast changes, the production's website remains the best place to check; international viewers should also consult their local Crunchyroll listing. What information is still missing? Future updates should focus on the precise simulcast schedule, possible dub announcements, episode count and new official promotional material. Any verified changes should be added to this guide instead of creating a second article about the same facts. Readers can explore the anime calendar , news section and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 on AniNextUp. Sources • Official anime website — Japanese premiere, staff and cast, October 9 news. • Crunchyroll October 8 report — first PV, cast and release. • Crunchyroll July 3 announcement — production and streaming plans. entries.content: FALL 2026 · RELEASE GUIDE The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life premiered October 6, 2026 on Crunchyroll. Release date, studio and streaming details for Fall 2026. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official promotional visual. Artwork source: official release announcement . RELEASE DATE October 6, 2026 STREAMING Crunchyroll STUDIO P.A.Works Release at a glance Release October 6, 2026 Where to watch Crunchyroll; Japanese audio and English dub launch together Region and timing Licensed territories; local catalog times vary. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Crunchyroll’s English dub announcement What makes Rein's comeback different Rein's strength is tied to the enchantments he already contributed to his former guild. Reclaiming those bonuses exposes how much of the group's success depended on work they undervalued. The premise turns a dismissal into a question about credit and dependence, rather than relying only on a sudden discovery of unrelated powers. Why the support-magic premise stands out Rein's value comes from the enchantments he has already provided to other people, not from suddenly discovering a completely unrelated combat talent. The dismissal exposes how dependent his former guild was on work it failed to appreciate. That gives the story a clear reversal of power and makes it especially relevant to viewers interested in fantasy about overlooked support roles. When does The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage premiere? The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life premiered October 6, 2026. Crunchyroll carries the series as part of its Fall 2026 lineup in supported international territories. What is the anime about? Rein is an Enchanter whose support magic strengthens weapons and armor. After his guild decides his work is no longer necessary and fires him, he recalls the enchantments he previously placed on their equipment and takes those accumulated bonus points back for himself. That unusual mechanic transforms a discarded support character into someone with enormous potential. Rather than joining another elite party immediately, Rein begins again with basic clothes and a copper sword, turning the premise into a second-chance fantasy adventure. How to choose between subbed and dubbed viewing Crunchyroll's English dub announcement establishes a same-day dub launch for the premiere. That is useful if you prefer English audio from the beginning, but it does not establish that every future dubbed episode will arrive at an identical local hour or that every language option is available in every country. The episode's audio selector in your local catalog remains the practical check. Where to watch Crunchyroll lists the anime for North America, Central and South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, CIS and Southeast Asia. Exact release times can vary by region. Watch the official teaser Crunchyroll published promotional footage ahead of the October premiere and confirmed a same-day English dub for October 6, alongside the Japanese-language release. See the Fall 2026 anime calendar for more confirmed October releases. The mechanic behind Rein’s second chance The official series description makes Rein’s support role central to the setup. He is an Enchanter whose work strengthens the weapons and armor of his guildmates. When the party dismisses him, he remembers that those enchantments have accumulated bonus points and takes them back. That premise ties his comeback to work the guild had already benefited from, rather than a sudden unrelated power that appears after he is fired. It is also why “support mage” is a more useful description than calling Rein weak. His contribution was embedded in the party’s equipment; the guild’s mistake was treating a less visible role as disposable. The story turns that imbalance into a fantasy progression hook. This is a reading of the published premise, not a promise that the series will provide a real-world blueprint for workplace disputes. Who voices Rein in the English dub? Crunchyroll's episode-one dub announcement credits Justin Briner as Rein, Hollis Beck as Lily, Lacey Deline as Nina, Kyleigh Zimmerer as Elsie and Rick Robertson as Barrius. These are the English-language credits announced for the first episode; they should not be confused with the Japanese cast. Which version of the story inspired the anime? The production website credits Asa Rokushima's novel, Gyomuyomochi's manga and kisui's original character concepts. It presents the animation as an adaptation of the manga and notes that the novel and manga differ substantially, so readers should not assume they tell every event in the same way. Shu Honma directs the anime at P.A.WORKS. The story's mix of fantasy adventure and comedy gives the enhancement-point premise a lively tone, while the official manga and novel listings offer separate ways to explore the source material. The October launch date is now a starting point for catching up, not a future countdown. What the dub announcement confirms Crunchyroll’s October 5 announcement says the English dub launches on the same date as the Japanese-language streaming premiere, October 6. This is helpful for viewers who prefer English audio from episode one. It does not establish that each later dubbed episode will arrive at the exact same hour as the Japanese stream, or that every audio and subtitle combination appears in every market. The original October 6 premiere has now passed, so the calendar date is a reference point for catching up. Crunchyroll’s live series page is the better check for the newest episode and the options available to a specific account. The seasonal lineup confirms Crunchyroll as the announced international service, while the production and publisher pages provide the character and ability descriptions. Readers should keep those separate: one source explains where to watch, another explains the world and characters, and neither should be used to infer an unannounced episode count. entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · OCTOBER 13, 2026 Le Collège Noir Season 2 Trailer Revealed Ahead of October 31 Premiere Le Collège Noir Season 2 premieres on October 31, 2026. Watch the official trailer and find confirmed streaming regions, creators and story details. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Published: October 13, 2026 · Editorial policy Season two promotional image from ADN's official October 13 announcement . Release at a glance Release date October 31, 2026, in France; exact release hour not confirmed Where to watch ADN in France; RTS in Switzerland. German-speaking territory licensing announced through Peppermint Anime; platform and schedule there not specified. Studio and director Studio La Cachette; Ulysse Malassagne Details checked October 13, 2026 · Official Toei Animation announcement Season 2's final trailer arrives before Halloween Le Collège Noir returns for its second season on October 31, 2026 , and Toei Animation has shared a final trailer ahead of the premiere. The French supernatural animated series is created by Ulysse Malassagne and produced by Studio La Cachette in co-production with Toei Animation. The Halloween launch date was announced before the October 13 trailer update, so the new video—not the date alone—is the central news in this report. Does the final trailer announce a new release date? No. The October 13 trailer is a promotional update ahead of the already announced October 31, 2026 Season 2 launch. It provides a new preview of the supernatural story, not a separate premiere or an additional season announcement. Viewers should consult the distributor's regional listing for the local streaming time and language options rather than infer them from the trailer's publication date. Related reading: Bless Anime Reveals Koki Uchiyama as Akiharu Nakano Ahead of January 2027 Premiere . Watch the official Le Collège Noir Season 2 trailer The player below uses the final trailer published by Toei Animation Europe and linked in its October 13 announcement. The preview artwork is the official season-two visual from ADN. Video availability may vary by region. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Toei Animation When does Le Collège Noir Season 2 come out? The confirmed French premiere is Saturday, October 31, 2026 . ADN lists the season for that date, and Toei Animation's announcement independently confirms it. Neither of these October 13 announcements establishes a precise time of day, so no release hour should be assumed. Where can viewers stream Season 2? ADN is the confirmed French streaming home. Toei Animation also identifies RTS for Switzerland and says Peppermint Anime has licensed the show for German-speaking territories, including Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, German-speaking Switzerland and South Tyrol in Italy. A license announcement does not by itself confirm a streaming platform or simultaneous October 31 launch in each territory. An English-language streaming release has not been confirmed in these announcements. What is Le Collège Noir about? Based on Malassagne's French comic, the story follows five young students at an isolated boarding school in the Cantal mountains. A supernatural encounter involving a missing classmate draws them into mysteries rooted in French folklore, including frightening creatures and an ancient curse. Season two continues the show's blend of mystery, fantasy and eerie adventure; specific new plot turns should not be treated as confirmed without further official details. Who is making Season 2? Ulysse Malassagne created the property and directs the animated adaptation. Studio La Cachette produces the animation, with Toei Animation involved as a co-production partner. ADN lists French as the original audio language. Toei Animation confirms six episodes per season, and France Télévisions lists Season 2 as six 15-minute episodes. What remains unannounced? The October 13 sources do not establish a global English-language streaming platform, an international release timetable or a universal launch hour. AniNextUp will update this report if the rights holders publish those details. Official sources Toei Animation — October 13 season-two final trailer and distribution announcement ; ADN — October 13 trailer and French premiere details ; Toei Animation — earlier renewal announcement ; France Télévisions — Season 2 format ; Toei Animation — six episodes per season . What should viewers know before Season 2? The first season introduces the students and their isolated school through a supernatural mystery. ADN's October announcement says viewers in its market can revisit that season while waiting for the new episodes. Its listing describes the original season as six episodes of approximately fifteen minutes, with French audio. For a returning viewer, that provides a short way to revisit the setting and the group before the new story. The announcement does not establish that every country will have the same catalog, subtitles or release schedule. Check the local service for the version available to your account. How long is the new season? Toei Animation's catalog lists twelve episodes across the two seasons, with six per season. France Télévisions' production listing describes the second season as six fifteen-minute episodes. The format does not establish individual release dates. ADN announces October 31 as the start of Season 2 in France, but its cited announcement does not specify a precise release time or confirm that all six episodes will arrive simultaneously. Viewers who want to plan a marathon should check the platform's episode listing when it becomes available. Why the Cantal setting matters The series draws on a French comic by Ulysse Malassagne and places its young characters in a remote boarding school in Cantal. ADN's synopsis describes a group staying there during the autumn school break, when an encounter connected to a missing classmate brings folklore and a witch's curse into their lives. That premise gives the supernatural events a specific regional setting rather than presenting the school as an unnamed haunted building. The production is French animation made with Toei Animation as a co-production partner. What does the regional licensing announcement mean? Toei's October 13 release names ADN in France and RTS in Switzerland and reports a license to Peppermint Anime for specified German-speaking territories. Those details are useful leads for viewers in those markets, but the announcement does not supply a single international premiere day or an English-language service. For the Dominican Republic and other countries outside the named territories, check a local distributor's announcement before assuming the French date or platform applies. Official local listings are also the place to confirm French audio, subtitles, age ratings and any access requirements. Sources checked October 26, 2026: Toei Animation, ADN and France Télévisions. Availability and schedules can change. Updated: October 26, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error
