entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · 2026-10-09 Live-Action Firefly Wedding TV Drama: 2027 Release Window, Cast and Story Fuji TV confirms a 2027 live-action Firefly Wedding drama. See what is known about the broadcast, story, teaser, cast, manga and streaming status. By AniNextUp Editorial Team Official source-series manga artwork, not a still from the live-action drama. © Oreco Tachibana / Shogakukan. Firefly Wedding live-action drama: the confirmed 2027 release window Fuji TV has confirmed that Firefly Wedding (Japanese title: Hotaru no Yomeiri ) is being adapted into a live-action television drama for broadcast in 2027. The broadcaster identifies Fuji TV as the production copyright holder and names Oreco Tachibana’s manga as the source. It gives no month, premiere day, episode count, timeslot or production schedule. “2027” is the full release window currently confirmed; the anime’s schedule does not set the drama’s date. The announcement came after the television anime’s first episode on October 9, 2026; Fuji TV’s news page was updated on October 10 in Japan. The anime and drama are separate adaptations. The anime’s premiere is not the drama premiere, and the formats can have different staff, casts and distributors. Release at a glance Format Japanese live-action TV drama Release 2027; month and day not announced Broadcaster / production Fuji TV; international distribution not announced Source Firefly Wedding manga by Oreco Tachibana, published by Shogakukan Live-action cast and staff Not announced in the official notice Official teaser Fuji TV’s 2027 announcement PV ; exact upload time and timezone not displayed in the accessible source What is the story about? The manga is set during Japan’s Meiji era, a period of rapid social change. Satoko Kirigaya is a count’s daughter who hopes to make a marriage that benefits her family. After an assassin named Shinpei Goto targets her, she offers marriage as a way to survive. What begins as a desperate bargain becomes a dangerous relationship shaped by Shinpei’s intense attachment, Satoko’s changing feelings and the threats around them. This describes the source material, not a scene-by-scene synopsis of the drama. Fuji TV has not published a drama-specific outline or confirmed how closely it will follow the manga. The original author welcomes seeing the characters in a real-world setting and says the live-action version may use different storytelling and expression. That is an invitation to expect its own interpretation, not a promise that every plot point will be reproduced unchanged. Who is in the live-action cast? No live-action actors have been named. Fuji TV says cast information and further news will be revealed later. Names associated with the anime belong to that separate production; they should not be presented as confirmed drama casting. The same applies to anime directors, character designers, composers and theme performers. Until Fuji TV or the drama’s official channels publish a cast list, the lead performers and creative staff remain unknown. There is no confirmed episode total, filming start or drama-specific teaser beyond the short announcement PV. The clip establishes the adaptation and 2027 broadcast year; it is not a full trailer and does not reveal cast members. These are the key gaps readers should check for in future updates. Is the drama connected to the 2026 anime? They share a source manga but are independent screen adaptations. Fuji TV’s anime began in Japan on October 9, 2026, in the Noitamina programming block, with a listed Friday broadcast from 11:30 p.m. to midnight Japan time. That schedule applies only to the anime. The drama is planned for 2027, and Fuji TV has not said it will use the anime’s timeslot or production team. This distinction answers common questions about whether the drama is “season two” or whether watching the anime is required first. The official notice describes a live-action adaptation of the manga, not an anime continuation. No viewing prerequisite has been announced. Viewers can follow the anime as its own version and later try the drama when its casting and release details arrive. Where can viewers watch it? Fuji TV is the confirmed Japanese broadcaster and production copyright holder. No overseas broadcaster, streaming service, subtitle plan or release outside Japan has been announced for the live-action drama. The anime has separate distribution information, but that does not establish that the drama will be licensed to the same service. International viewers should wait for a notice that explicitly names the live-action title and territory. Shogakukan’s official e-comic listing identifies Oreco Tachibana as the manga’s author and presents the completed series as a 14-volume collection. This is a starting point for readers seeking the source story, though language editions and storefront availability vary by country. The anime’s official news archive tracks that adaptation separately; Fuji TV’s announcement is the primary source for drama developments. Is there an official trailer, and when was it uploaded? Fuji TV and the anime’s official website link to a short announcement PV on the Fuji TV YouTube channel. The video announces the 2027 live-action version. In the page available for this review, the official channel and title were visible, but the original upload date, exact time and timezone were not. A relative label such as “weeks ago” cannot establish that timestamp, so this guide does not state one or attach timestamp-based video structured data. The official link above may be accessible in other regions. The next useful updates will be a formal cast reveal, a more precise broadcast window, episode count and distribution outside Japan. Until then, the dependable answer is that live-action Firefly Wedding is planned for Fuji TV in 2027, while its exact premiere and most production details remain unannounced. Primary sources: Fuji TV’s live-action announcement ; the official anime-site announcement ; and Shogakukan’s manga listing . Exact teaser upload time and timezone were unavailable in the accessible YouTube page; no timestamp is claimed. Updated: October 25, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error

entries.content: OCTOBER 20, 2026 · NEW ANIME Love Live! Hasunosora Release Date: January 10, 2027 & Episodes Love Live! Hasunosora Girls’ High School Idol Club begins its seven-episode TV anime on January 10, 2027. The Japanese schedule is confirmed, while an international streaming service remains unannounced in the sources below. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official TV anime key visual · ©2026 Project Love Live! Hasunosora Girls’ High School Idol Club. Source: Bandai Namco Filmworks / V-STORAGE . Release at a glance Premiere January 10, 2027 · Japan First broadcast TOKYO MX · Sundays at 22:30 JST Episodes 7 · 106th-class April–June story Animation / planning Sublimation / Sunrise International streaming Not yet announced in the cited sources Verified October 25, 2026 · Official broadcast schedule When does the Love Live! Hasunosora anime come out? The Japanese premiere is January 10, 2027. TOKYO MX starts the series at 22:30 JST on Sundays. Sun TV lists 23:30 the same evening. BS11 lists “January 10 at 24:30,” which means Monday, January 11 at 00:30 on a standard calendar. Japanese schedules sometimes use times above 24:00 to keep a late-night program attached to the previous evening. The official schedule also names these stations. All times below are JST: KBS Kyoto: Sundays at 24:00 from January 10 (Monday, January 11 at 00:00). TV Aichi and RKB Mainichi Broadcasting: Sundays at 25:20 from January 10 (Monday at 01:20). Shizuoka Broadcasting: Sundays at 25:50 from January 10 (Monday at 01:50). Hokkaido Broadcasting: Mondays at 25:29 from January 11 (Tuesday, January 12 at 01:29). Hokuriku Broadcasting: Sundays at 16:00 from January 17. These are Japanese television times, not an international streaming timetable. The official notice says broadcast times can change, so check local listings near the premiere. Related reading: Hello, I am a Witch and my Crush Wants me to Make a Love Potion! Release Date & Watch Guide . How many episodes will there be? The official schedule lists seven episodes , covering April through June of the project’s 106th-class story. Those months describe events within the story; they are not an April-to-June broadcast window. The announcement does not give a dated episode calendar, runtimes, or a finale date. The short episode count confirms the season’s scope, but it is not enough to calculate the final broadcast date. How should fans read the seven-episode announcement? The official broadcast page says the television story covers April through June of the 106th class across seven planned episodes. Those are months in the characters' school year; the television premiere begins in January 2027. Different Japanese stations carry the program at different hours, and some use a clock above 24:00 for after-midnight broadcasts. The page cautions that schedules can change. Check the broadcaster's latest listing for a particular episode, and wait for an international distributor to confirm streaming access and subtitles outside Japan. Related reading: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Is Out on Netflix: Episodes & Trailer . Where can you watch Hasunosora outside Japan? No international streaming platform is identified in the official release information cited here. The confirmed outlets are Japanese broadcasters. Check back for a distributor announcement before assuming that Crunchyroll, Netflix or another service will carry the series in your country. Dub and subtitle availability also remain unconfirmed. What is the story about? The setting is the private Hasunosora Girls’ High School in Kanazawa, Ishikawa. The official introduction describes a girl once known for her smile arriving with spring. New meetings and partings bring the girls' pasts into their present, as they pursue the changes they hope to make in themselves. The school-idol setting ties music and shared ambitions to everyday school life. For newcomers, the useful distinction is that this announcement concerns the television series. The broader Hasunosora project also includes music, live performances and other animation, so a film screening or concert date should be checked separately. Related reading: The Detective Is Already Dead Season 2: Release Date, Episodes & Where to Watch . Bandai Namco Filmworks separately notes that the Hasunosora theatrical film Bloom Garden Party opened in May 2026. The film and this TV anime are distinct releases within the same project. The cited announcements do not say that the film is required viewing before the January series, so a watch order should not be assumed. Cast and animation staff The newly introduced students include Maika Kinjo, Aoi Reisawa and Mion Shinowa. Their Japanese cast members are 星宮じゅりあ, 朝陽花菜 and 湯浅かなえ, respectively. The official credits also list returning club members and their performers. The announcement also names Haruna Sakurai as Ginko Momose, Fuka Hayama as Kosuzu Kachimachi, Rin Kurusu as Hime Anyoji, Miu Miyake as Ceras Yanagida Lilienfeld, and Amane Shindo as Izumi Katsuragi. Together with the three new students, these are the Japanese cast members identified in the release. Related reading: Dreamland Anime: Release Date, Episodes & Where to Watch . Go Kurosaki directs, with a screenplay by Fumiaki Maruto and character designs by Haruko Iizuka. Sublimation handles animation, Sunrise is credited for planning and production, and Yoshiaki Fujisawa composes the music. Watch the official announcement livestream The October 18 presentation introduced new cast members and TV anime information. The video below is the official announcement program, not a dedicated TV trailer. The official account scheduled the livestream for 20:00 JST. That is the program’s broadcast time; the YouTube listing does not establish the original upload timestamp, so no VideoObject uploadDate is claimed. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT New cast and TV anime information · October 18, 2026 Sources and updates Bandai Namco Filmworks: January premiere, key visual and cast announcement Official schedule and seven-episode story scope Official story introduction Official cast and staff Browse more new anime announcements or use the anime calendar to plan upcoming releases. entries.content: OCTOBER 23 · ANIME MOVIE Made in Abyss: Awakening Mystery Release Date and Where to Watch The first theatrical installment opened in Japan on October 23, 2026. On October 23, the official site also confirmed Part 2 is in production; it has no announced release date, and international cinema and streaming plans remain unconfirmed. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official main-trailer still · © Akihito Tsukushi, Takeshobo / Made in Abyss Theatrical Series Production Committee. Source: official movie website . Release at a glance Japan release October 23, 2026 · Japanese theaters Project First installment in the Made in Abyss theatrical series Part 2 Production confirmed October 23, 2026 · release date TBA International release No overseas cinema date or streaming launch confirmed First-week bonus Mini-anime screening after the film, October 23–30 in Japan Checked October 25, 2026 · Official movie website · KADOKAWA official theatrical listing When did Made in Abyss: Awakening Mystery release? The first installment in the Made in Abyss theatrical series opened in Japanese theaters on October 23, 2026 . The date is a Japan release, not a worldwide premiere. The official Japanese title is Gekijō Series Dai-ichi-bu: Made in Abyss — Mezamuru Shinpi (劇場シリーズ【第一部】メイドインアビス 目覚める神秘). “Awakening Mystery” is a useful English rendering of the subtitle; the official film pages reviewed use the Japanese title rather than announcing an English-language title. For viewers outside Japan, no international cinema date, regional distributor, or streaming launch appears in the official sources checked on October 25. A Japanese theatrical opening does not establish when the film will reach another country or platform. Check local distributors and theater listings for a region-specific announcement instead of treating October 23 as a global date. Made in Abyss Part 2 is confirmed, but undated On October 23, the official film site confirmed production of Part 2 , describing it as the continuation of Part 1. The announcement also revealed a second key visual featuring the Curse Fleet, Hail Hex, led by Srajo. This is the clearest answer for readers asking whether the theatrical project will continue: yes, another installment is in production. The announcement did not give Part 2 a release date, production schedule, runtime, distributor, or streaming plan. It did not publish a separate staff or cast list for the new installment. Part 1’s confirmed credits therefore should not automatically be presented as Part 2 credits. The project has established that the next film is being made, while its timing and production details remain unknown. What is the first film about? The official introduction recaps the journey from the sixth layer of the Abyss and points toward the seventh. Riko, Reg, Nanachi, and Faputa leave the Village of the Hollows behind after its collapse and continue deeper into the unknown. The setup follows the events of the second television season; the film is a continuation of that journey, not a remake of the original series or an announced third TV season. The official introduction includes significant story detail from earlier chapters, including Prushka’s transformation into Riko’s White Whistle and the fate of the village. New viewers who want to avoid those reveals can begin with the television seasons and consult the film’s synopsis afterward. The project site does not describe the full plot of Part 1 or explain how many manga chapters it adapts, so a precise adaptation breakdown is not confirmed. Who made the film and who returns? The official credits list Akihito Tsukushi as the original creator, Masayuki Kojima as director, Hideyuki Kurata as screenwriter, and Kinema Citrus as the animation studio. Character design is credited to Yuka Kuroda and Kazuya Kise, with Kevin Penkin composing the music. These familiar series credits connect the film to the existing anime, but the official page identifies this project as the first part of a theatrical series. The principal returning voices include Miyu Tomita as Riko, Mariya Ise as Reg, Shiori Izawa as Nanachi, and Misaki Kuno as Faputa. The film also lists Sumire Morohoshi as Tepaste, Takanori Hoshino as Clavari, Nana Mizuki as Srajo, Akino Watanabe as Nishagora, Shunsuke Takeuchi as Yataramaru, Nao Toyama as Sherumi, and Yume Miyamoto as Menae. Those names are confirmed for Part 1; a Part 2 cast announcement has not been made. Official trailer and upload date KADOKAWAanime’s verified YouTube page identifies the official main trailer and displays August 6, 2026 as its publication date. The page does not display an exact upload time or timezone, so this guide reports only the date and does not infer a time or convert it to Japan time. The official movie page links the video directly. The trailer and official introduction establish the project’s title, release, and story context. Promotional footage should not be treated as confirmation of scenes or plot points that the production has not described in its written synopsis. Can Japanese theatergoers still receive the opening bonus? The official first-week campaign runs from October 23 through October 30, 2026. Participating screenings include a short Hime-sama Nikki mini-anime after the feature, and visitors receive one of two Akihito Tsukushi illustrated mini shikishi designs at random. The mini-anime expands an April Fools’ Day illustration into a short screening bonus. The campaign is specific to the listed Japanese opening week; check with the individual cinema for participation and current bonus availability. Because the campaign is time-limited, check the theater before traveling. The official notice says the mini-anime runs after the feature and the printed illustration is distributed at random; neither item is a separate episode release or a Part 2 date announcement. Where can viewers watch it now? As of October 25, the confirmed release information covers Japanese theaters. The official pages reviewed do not confirm overseas screenings, a home-video date, or a streaming service. The same pages confirm Part 2 production but do not provide a release window. Readers looking for a legal option outside Japan should wait for a local distributor or platform to announce availability; no service should be named as confirmed on the basis of the Japanese cinema opening alone. For the most current primary information, follow the official theatrical-series site , its October 23 Part 2 announcement , the Part 1 introduction , and the official staff and cast page . For bonus terms, consult the first-week theater notice ; for the trailer, use the official video page . entries.content: OCTOBER 23 · ANIME MOVIE Maebashi Witches Movie: October 23 Release, New Scenes & Trailer Maebashi Witches – Emoemories opened in Japanese theaters on October 23, 2026. The film reshapes the 12-episode TV anime with new story material, scenes, and songs; overseas release and streaming remain unannounced. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official movie trailer thumbnail · ©PROJECT MBW. Source: official Maebashi Witches movie page . Release at a glance Japan theatrical run Opened October 23, 2026 · Japanese theaters Format Feature-length reconstruction of the 12-episode TV anime, around two hours Added material New episodes/scenes and songs, plus newly recorded material First-week bonus Five mini shikishi designs, October 23–29 while supplies last International release No overseas cinema or streaming date confirmed Details checked October 25, 2026 · Official series website · Current Japanese theater schedule When did the Maebashi Witches movie release? Maebashi Witches – Emoemories: Blooming Witches opened in Japanese theaters on October 23, 2026. That date has passed; the film is currently in its Japanese theatrical run, with showtimes varying by cinema and day. The official theater listing publishes a rolling schedule, so check the local venue before traveling rather than relying on a single nationwide start time. The official project site has not announced an overseas theatrical date or a streaming service for this film. Its October 23 release is specifically the Japanese cinema opening. A Japanese premiere does not establish a later date for the United States, Europe, Latin America, or any other territory. Is it a recap, a sequel, or a new movie? The theatrical edition rebuilds the original 12-episode TV anime into a feature lasting just under two hours. The official description calls it a reconstruction of the series, but also stresses that it is not simply a compilation: the film adds new episodes or story passages, new Witchverse scenes, songs, newly recorded material, and additional dialogue. Director Shunichi Yamamoto says the production reshaped the order and direction while assembling the story into a film-length experience. Related reading: Aikatsu Stars! Movie: January 22, 2027 Release Date & Trailer . That makes this a theatrical re-edit with new material, not an announced second season or a separate sequel. The official October 16 update released six new stills and comments from Yamamoto and series composer and screenwriter Erika Yoshida. The announcements do not give a count of every new scene or a scene-by-scene comparison with the 12 TV episodes, so viewers should not treat a specific “minutes of new footage” figure as confirmed. Can you watch the movie without seeing the TV anime? Yes, the director presents the film as accessible to people who only know the title or are meeting the series for the first time. It condenses the central story into a single visit of roughly two hours, which is a practical entry point for someone who has not watched all 12 episodes. The official comments also say the restructured presentation and new scenes give returning viewers fresh material to notice. What is the story about? The story is set in Maebashi, Gunma Prefecture, and follows ordinary high-school student Yuina Akagi after she meets Az, Kyoka, Choco, and Mai. The five girls begin witch training while working at a magical flower shop, where they face customers’ wishes and try to help the “flowers” in people’s hearts bloom. Keroppe, the frog-like companion, is also part of the group’s story. Related reading: The Apothecary Diaries Movie: Luoqing and Yinshan Character PV . Yoshida frames the story around the effort involved in both maintaining the status quo and choosing to move forward. The girls make mistakes, respond differently to the wishes they encounter, and build solidarity through their choices; those emotional decisions connect the episodic premise into a feature-length story. Who voices the Maebashi Witches? The main cast returns for the theatrical edition: Sakura Kasuga voices Yuina Akagi, Hinano Sakikawa voices Az Niizato, Rena Motomura voices Kyoka Kitahara, Haruka Minami voices Choco Mimata, and Honami Momose voices Mai Kamiizumi. Tomokazu Sugita voices Keroppe. These names are confirmed on the official series cast page. Sunrise is credited with the original work and production. Yamamoto directs, Yoshida handles series composition and script, and Bandai Namco Filmworks is credited for production. The official October 16 comments note that the new script passages and added lines were developed with the film edit, which distinguishes the theatrical work from a simple episode-to-episode splice. Related reading: Medalist Movie Release Date: February 19, 2027, Story and Cast . Does the movie have new songs? Yes. The official movie page highlights new songs and the theatrical theme “Amehare Make up,” with lyrics by Yuuki Iwai and composition/arrangement by EFFY. The production also mentions newly recorded material and re-recording, but has not published a complete track-by-track list in the cited release details. Where can you watch the official trailer? The official Maebashi Witches movie page lists the theatrical trailer and links to the verified TV anime YouTube channel. It is the movie promotion for the October 23 cinema release, separate from the earlier TV-series PVs. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Official theatrical trailer · Japan release: October 23, 2026 The official movie page does not show the trailer’s exact original upload time or time zone. Those details are not asserted here as a precise timestamp. How can you find current Japanese showtimes? The official project site links to a theater directory with daily listings. On October 25, 2026, the directory showed screenings across multiple Japanese regions. Because cinema schedules change, confirm the date, start time, venue, and ticket availability with the theater before traveling. Is there a first-week theater bonus? The official first-week campaign runs October 23–29, 2026, and offers one of five limited mini shikishi designs illustrated by character designer Nozomi Tachibana. The gift is distributed at participating Japanese theaters while supplies last; the date range alone does not guarantee that a particular cinema still has copies. Contact the theater or check its notice before buying a ticket if the bonus matters to your visit. Will Maebashi Witches stream outside Japan? No international streaming platform or release date is confirmed in the official pages reviewed on October 25, 2026. The official theater directory is for Japanese cinemas; it is not evidence of overseas distribution. Viewers outside Japan should wait for a regional distributor or the project’s official channels to announce a license, and should treat the TV series’ availability as separate from this movie’s rights. entries.title: Magic Knight Rayearth 2026: Official Creditless Ending, Hoshiakari & Streaming
entries.description: Magic Knight Rayearth 2026 unveils its official creditless ending with Kawaguchi Yurina's Hoshiakari on October 15. Watch the official video and see streaming details.
entries.content: FALL 2026 · RELEASE GUIDE Magic Knight Rayearth 2026: Official Creditless Ending, Hoshiakari & Streaming The new Magic Knight Rayearth anime began airing October 7, 2026. On October 15, the production released its creditless ending sequence featuring Kawaguchi Yurina’s “Hoshiakari” (星灯). By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Magic Knight Rayearth — artwork from the classic anime, used to illustrate the franchise; not a 2026 key visual. Image source: Amazon Prime Video. RELEASE DATE October 7, 2026 STREAMING Crunchyroll STUDIO E&H production October 15 update: Official creditless ending video released The production behind Magic Knight Rayearth has published a creditless version of its ending animation, set to “Hoshiakari” (星灯) by Kawaguchi Yurina . The sequence begins with Hikaru, Umi and Fuu looking toward the waves at night, then moves through atmospheric scenes featuring Princess Emeraude and other characters. It is a new official music-video release for the anime already airing—not an announcement of another season. What does a creditless ending release mean? A creditless ending video shows the ending animation without the usual on-screen production credits, allowing viewers to see the sequence and its music more clearly. The October 15 release is a promotional update for the existing anime; it does not confirm an additional season, a new premiere date or a change in streaming availability. The announced ending song is Hoshiakari by Kawaguchi Yurina. Watch the official Magic Knight Rayearth creditless ending The anime production also links the clip in its October 15 announcement . Who sings “Hoshiakari,” and when was it released? Kawaguchi Yurina's fifth digital single launched on October 15, 2026 . The anime's official music page credits Katsuhiko Sugiyama with lyrics and Gary Jeon with composition and arrangement. The artist's record-label announcement separately confirms the release date and music-video rollout. Watch Kawaguchi Yurina’s separate “Hoshiakari” music video Alongside the anime’s creditless ending, Kawaguchi Yurina released a separate artist music video on October 15. Directed by MONA (VeAble), it is distinct from the animated ending sequence. Universal Music Japan describes a visual journey from isolation toward renewal, including a symbolic haircut. This artist video should not be mistaken for another anime trailer. Related reading: Paw & Palaces Releases Creditless Ending Video Featuring “Chill Choose!” . Source: Universal Music Japan’s official announcement . Additional episode-two narration credit On the same date, the production confirmed Keiko Han as the narrator of episode two. The official casting announcement describes this as an additional episode-specific credit, not a replacement of the main cast. How is the ending video different from the singer's video? The anime production's October 15 announcement presents the creditless ending as the animated sequence used with Kawaguchi Yurina's “Hoshiakari.” Her separate official music video features the artist rather than that anime ending sequence. Both are official releases connected to the same song, but they serve different purposes. The creditless animation lets viewers revisit the show's ending without credits; the artist video is a separate music release. Neither announcement changes the anime's October premiere or establishes a new season. What returning viewers should expect This production revisits Hikaru, Umi and Fuu rather than introducing an unrelated story under the same title. That makes the central question for returning fans how the new adaptation presents the classic material, not simply which episode follows the older television series. The confirmed October 7 start establishes a premiere date; region-specific streaming times remain a separate question. Related reading: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Anime Shares Creditless Opening and Ending Videos . Is the 2026 anime a continuation? The announced production revisits Hikaru, Umi and Fuu in a new adaptation of the familiar story, rather than following the older television anime with a newly numbered season. Returning viewers can compare the treatment of the original material, while newcomers should not assume that prior television episodes are a required direct lead-in. When does Magic Knight Rayearth 2026 come out? The new Magic Knight Rayearth anime began October 7, 2026 . Crunchyroll lists it among its new Fall 2026 simulcasts, with E&H production handling animation. What to expect The new production brings Hikaru, Umi and Fuu back in a retelling of the classic Magic Knight Rayearth story. E&H production is the animation studio. What viewers should check about streaming times The October 7 date refers to the start of the new anime, not a guarantee that the episode appears at the same hour on Crunchyroll in every country. The Japanese broadcast schedule and the international streaming schedule are separate; viewers should use the official anime site for broadcast details and the regional Crunchyroll listing for their local release time. No universal simulcast hour is confirmed in this guide. Related reading: A Returner's Magic Should Be Special Season 2 . Magic Knight Rayearth 2026 episode schedule The series starts October 7. Crunchyroll's updated Fall 2026 lineup lists subtitled episodes on Wednesdays at 8:15 a.m. Pacific Time. Check your local episode listing for regional availability. Where to watch Crunchyroll lists availability across the Americas, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, parts of the CIS, Southeast Asia and Korea. Watch the official Magic Knight Rayearth trailer Official main PV 2 announced on September 20, 2026; the video is linked in Universal Music's announcement. Official sources Official anime website → Crunchyroll Fall 2026 lineup → AniNextUp: Release dates and streaming availability can vary by region. This guide will be updated when new official information is confirmed. Updated: October 26, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error Official trailer ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Official PV Production evidence: Japanese schedule ; Animation credits ; Main PV 2 announcement and video link . Japanese schedule details: TV Asahi broadcasts from October 7 at 11:45 p.m. JST. The official site lists domestic streaming from Thursdays at 12:15 a.m. JST, with start dates varying by service. These are Japanese schedules and do not establish the international simulcast hour. Video source: official YouTube upload (TMSアニメ公式チャンネル) . International schedule: Crunchyroll: Wednesday at 8:15 a.m. PT under Magic Knight Rayearth .

entries.title: Manchuria Opium Squad Anime: Release Date, Story and Latest News
entries.description: Manchuria Opium Squad is getting an anime adaptation. See confirmed story details, the 2026 announcement and what remains unannounced.
entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · OCTOBER 5, 2026 Manchuria Opium Squad Anime: Release Date, Story and Latest News The 1937-set crime manga is getting an anime adaptation. Its first visual is out, but release and production details remain unannounced. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official announcement visual. © Tsukasa Monma, Shikako, Kodansha / “Manchuria Opium Squad” Production Committee. Source: Pony Canyon . Release at a glance RELEASE DATE Not announced FORMAT Anime adaptation confirmed; format TBA STUDIO / CAST Not announced STREAMING Not announced What is confirmed about the anime? The anime adaptation of Manchuria Opium Squad was officially announced on October 5, 2026, alongside a first visual. Pony Canyon’s announcement identifies the project as an adaptation of Kodansha’s crime-suspense manga, but stops short of naming a release window or production team. This is an announcement of a project in development, not a premiere announcement: the format, studio, director, cast, broadcaster and streaming services are still unconfirmed in the official materials checked for this update. The original story is by Tsukasa Monma. The manga artwork is now by Tsurushima, while Shikako is credited for the original art concept. The series returned to Kodansha’s Weekly Young Magazine in the same October issue that carried the anime news, so readers encounter two related developments at once: the comic is continuing with its new artist, and an animated adaptation is in the works. They are separate releases with separate schedules. What is Manchuria Opium Squad about? Manchuria Opium Squad is set in Manchuria in 1937. Its protagonist, Isamu Higata, is a soldier in the Kwantung Army who loses sight in his right eye during battle. He is reassigned to an agricultural unit, where he discovers poppies being grown as a source of opium. When his mother falls ill, his need to help her pushes him into illegal production. The official manga synopsis describes the choice as the turning point that sends both Isamu’s life and Manchuria’s fate in a new direction. Related reading: Anime News: October 2026 — Streaming Updates & 2027 Announcements . That setup gives the title its crime-suspense engine: a personal emergency becomes entangled with a dangerous trade and the people and powers that try to control it. The story’s appeal is not simply the historical backdrop or a lone criminal protagonist. It puts family duty beside the harm and danger attached to an illegal business, then follows the consequences of that decision. Those are story stakes, not a guide to producing or selling drugs; the official materials provide no technical how-to detail. Historical setting and adaptation scope The year and setting are confirmed by the publisher, but the manga is a work of fiction. Readers should not treat its characters, dialogue or individual events as a documentary account of real people. The official Japanese synopsis emphasizes the frontier setting and the way Isamu’s decision changes his fate and the region around him; it does not present a historical textbook or claim that his fictional case represents every person living in Manchuria at the time. Related reading: Akane-banashi Season 2 Release Date: January 2027 and Story . Is there an official trailer? The announcement visual is a static image that assembles character drawings and production artwork around the series logo. It confirms an anime project, but it is not a trailer and does not reveal how the animation will look in motion. As of October 24, the official materials reviewed still do not provide a verified PV or trailer link. There is consequently no official video upload time to report, and no confirmed animation footage, theme song or episode count. How popular is the manga? What does the project’s popularity look like? Pony Canyon reported that the manga had exceeded 3.5 million copies in circulation by the announcement. That is a cumulative circulation figure supplied by the publisher, not a promise about anime audience size or a count of paid digital reads. It does explain why an adaptation announcement is a significant new milestone for a series that has already built a substantial readership. Manga continuation and anime staff For manga readers, the continuation is especially relevant. Young Magazine’s official listing says serialization has resumed and credits Monma for the original story, Tsurushima for the manga, and Shikako for the original art concept. The anime’s staff and format have not yet been confirmed. That distinction matters: the person drawing the continuing comic is named, but that alone does not tell readers which animation studio will adapt it or who will voice Isamu. Related reading: Cosmoship Yamato √2199 Release Date: Story, Cast and What’s Confirmed . Is the manga suitable for younger readers? The English-language digital listing is available from Kodansha USA. It labels the manga Mature 18+ and warns readers about graphic violence and drug abuse. That rating applies to Kodansha USA’s manga listing; it is not an announced age rating for the anime. The note is useful for readers choosing a series to start and for anyone deciding whether its subject matter is suitable for a younger or sensitive audience. Release date and where to watch When will the anime come out, and where can it be watched? Those are the two most practical questions, and neither has an official answer yet. No premiere month or year, Japanese broadcaster, international distributor, streaming platform or cast has been announced in the official notice. Avoid sites that attach a season or service to the title without linking a dated production announcement; a series page appearing in an anime database does not establish a release plan. Related reading: Dandivine Release Date & Where to Watch: Japan Schedule, Cast and Story . Where to follow official updates For reliable updates, use the official anime site and official X account, and compare them with Pony Canyon’s announcement and Young Magazine’s series page. A dated broadcast notice, staff list, casting release, official video, or streaming partner announcement would be new information. Until one appears, the confirmed facts remain the adaptation, the announcement visual, the manga’s return under Tsurushima, and the story’s 1937 setting. The existing manga is the way to read the story now; the anime is a separate adaptation whose format and release remain open. If you are new to the series, start with Kodansha’s official English listing for the premise and content advisory. If you already follow the manga, watch Young Magazine’s listing for its new chapter releases and the anime site for a future cast, staff or broadcast update. Confirmed: anime adaptation announced October 5, 2026, with an announcement visual. Not announced: release date, studio, cast, staff, broadcaster, streaming service and trailer. Updated: October 24, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error Sources: Pony Canyon announcement ; Weekly Young Magazine series page ; Kodansha USA English listing and content advisory . Trailer status checked October 24, 2026.

entries.content: RELEASE NEWS · OCTOBER 27, 2026 MASHLE Season 3 Release Date: January 2027, Arc and Teaser MASHLE Season 3 arrives in January 2027. Get the confirmed release window, Divine Visionary final exam arc, official teaser and streaming status. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy Official third-season teaser artwork from the MASHLE anime website. © Hajime Komoto / Shueisha, MASHLE Project. Release at a glance Japanese premiere January 2027; exact day TBA Season / story arc Season 3 / Divine Visionary final exam arc Format Continuing television anime International streaming Not established by the announcements reviewed Release details checked October 27, 2026. When does MASHLE Season 3 come out? MASHLE: MAGIC AND MUSCLES Season 3 premieres in January 2027. The anime's July 3 announcement narrowed the previously announced 2027 return to a specific month and introduced a new teaser. A first broadcast day has not been established in the official release information reviewed for this guide. The continuation is titled the Tri-Magicathlon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc . That longer name identifies the story being promoted, while “Season 3” is the easier label to use when organizing a watchlist. Both refer to the same upcoming continuation rather than two separate releases. January places Mash's return in the Winter 2027 television season. Our January anime release guide groups it with other confirmed launches, keeping month-only announcements separate from shows that already have a dated first episode. What is MASHLE about? Mash Burnedead lives in a world that measures people by their ability to use magic. He has no magical power, a disadvantage that threatens much more than his standing in a classroom. His answer is a body trained to an extraordinary degree, allowing him to approach supposedly magical problems through overwhelming physical ability. The original setup sends Mash from a quiet life with his father into a magic school, where becoming a Divine Visionary offers a way forward. The joke comes from that mismatch: the surrounding world expects spells and inherited talent, while Mash responds with strength and an unusually direct understanding of the challenge. Related reading: Frieren Season 3 Release Date: October 2027 & Golden Land Arc . That premise is useful context for newcomers deciding whether to catch up. This is an action comedy built around a sustained absurdity, with school rivalries and relationships giving the fights a wider setting. Starting at the beginning will make the returning characters and Mash's goal easier to follow than jumping directly into the final exam arc. Which arc will the third season cover? The announced arc name places the Divine Visionary examination at the center of the third season's promotion. It signals a continuation of Mash's effort to establish himself within the institution that judges magical ability. The official title is the reliable description of the upcoming storyline. It does not, by itself, supply a complete episode list, a manga chapter stopping point or a guarantee that the whole remaining manga will be adapted in this run. Those are separate production details. For readers avoiding spoilers, the arc title and official teaser provide enough orientation without revealing individual match results or later character developments. The practical watch order is the first television season, the second television season and then this third season. Treat the January return as a continuation of that story, with the earlier installments supplying the relationships, school setting and examination context. Related reading: ONE PIECE: Elbaph Arc English Dub Release Date and Crunchyroll Schedule . Watch the official teaser The July 3 update includes the official third-season teaser and confirms the January window. The artwork reproduced above belongs to the third-season promotion and shows Mash with a dumbbell. Together, the announcement and visual identify the continuation without supplying a specific first broadcast day. The source list below preserves the original announcement for verification. ▶ PLAY OFFICIAL VIDEO MASHLE Season 3 — Official Teaser Cast and production background Aniplex's existing series credits list A-1 Pictures as the animation studio, Tomoya Tanaka as director, Yosuke Kuroda for series composition and Hisashi Higashijima for character design. These credits describe the established adaptation and provide production background; they should not be mistaken for a separately verified, complete third-season staff announcement. The established Japanese cast includes Chiaki Kobayashi as Mash, Reiji Kawashima as Finn, Kaito Ishikawa as Lance, Takuya Eguchi as Dot and Reina Ueda as Lemon. A new season can introduce additional roles, so this familiar core is a starting point rather than a claim that every upcoming character has already been announced. Where will Season 3 stream? The official pages reviewed establish the Japanese January window. They do not establish a country-by-country international streaming timetable for the new season. Listings for the first two seasons on Japanese services should be read as availability for those installments, rather than advance confirmation of a worldwide Season 3 launch. Related reading: Pokémon Horizons Anime Unseals Treasures of Ruin in Latest Wonder Voyage Arc Trailer . For your viewing plan, keep the premiere month and the platform decision as two separate entries. Once a distributor announces its territories, subtitles and local schedule, those details can be added without changing what the Japanese premiere announcement actually says. The where-to-watch hub provides a starting point for checking regional availability across our coverage. Reading the manga before January MASHLE originated as Hajime Komoto's manga. Shueisha confirms that its serialization concluded in July 2023, and VIZ publishes the English edition. VIZ's first volume offers an accessible starting point for readers who want the original introduction to Mash and the magic-school premise. Beginning with Volume 1 also avoids assuming an unannounced anime-to-manga handoff point. Readers who prefer to remain anime-only can instead revisit the first two seasons before January and use this guide for the confirmed continuation window. For another returning action series that month, see our Shangri-La Frontier Season 3 guide . Sources and verification Primary announcements and publisher information checked October 27, 2026. entries.content: RELEASE NEWS · OCTOBER 27, 2026 Medalist Movie Release Date: February 19, 2027, Story and Cast The Medalist movie opens in Japan on February 19, 2027. Explore its championship story, returning cast, ENGI production, official teaser and release scope. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy Official Medalist movie promotional artwork. © TSURUMAIKADA / Kodansha, Medalist Production Committee. Release at a glance Japanese cinema release Friday, February 19, 2027 Place in the series Movie continuation following the television anime Animation studio ENGI International release / streaming Not established in the announcements reviewed Release details checked October 27, 2026. When does the Medalist movie release? The Medalist movie opens in Japanese theaters on Friday, February 19, 2027. The official August 30 announcement supplied the date, following the earlier announcement of a film continuation. This is a Japanese theatrical opening; an overseas cinema date or home-streaming launch requires a separate release announcement. The film continues the figure-skating anime following its television installments. For viewers assembling a watchlist, it belongs after the TV story rather than alongside unrelated standalone anime movies. Its promotional material places Inori and her coach at the next major competitive stage. February 19 is an exact date, so it can appear in our anime release calendar as a confirmed Japanese cinema release. Keep that scope in mind if you are planning to watch from another country: the date tells you when the Japanese theatrical run begins. What is Medalist about? Medalist begins with Inori Yuitsuka, a girl determined to become a figure skater despite being considered late to start. Kodansha's first-volume introduction places her at eleven and describes the skepticism surrounding her ambition. Her family's experience with her older sister's unsuccessful dream complicates that desire. Related reading: Pokémon Horizons Season 4: February 27 Netflix Date, Story and Trailer . Tsukasa Akeuraji has his own history of disappointment in skating. When he becomes Inori's coach, their partnership connects two people who see a possibility that others have been quick to dismiss. The original premise gives the competitive story an emotional foundation before medals or rankings enter the picture. That relationship makes the series approachable beyond an audience already familiar with figure skating. Inori has to develop technical skill while learning to trust herself; Tsukasa must turn his understanding of the sport into guidance another person can use. Watching their collaboration is part of the appeal, alongside the performances on the ice. Which competition does the movie cover? The official film introduction places Inori and Tsukasa at the All-Japan Novice Championship after earning their place through the Chubu block competition. The next major confrontation brings Inori into direct competition with Hikaru Kamisaki, whose coach is Jun Yodaka. That announced setup gives the movie a clear point of focus: the young skaters are moving into a more demanding event, and the rivalry now has an immediate competitive setting. It is enough to understand the stakes without revealing how the event ends or importing later manga developments into the film synopsis. Related reading: THE ONE PIECE Release Date: February 2027, Episodes & Where to Watch . The promotional story also raises the difficulty of Inori's training. Viewers who prefer to avoid detailed performance spoilers can stop at the championship premise and use the teaser for a visual introduction. This guide does not assign an unannounced chapter range, final runtime or ending to the movie. Watch the official teaser The August 30 release-date update includes a newer promotional teaser carrying the February opening information. It follows the initial film-announcement teaser and belongs to the movie campaign. The dated promotional artwork above provides the same Japanese opening date. Both announcements are useful for distinguishing the new theatrical continuation from television reruns. ▶ PLAY OFFICIAL VIDEO Medalist Movie — Official Release-Date Teaser Production background and returning performers The official movie credits list Yasutaka Yamamoto as director, Jukki Hanada as screenwriter and Chinatsu Kameyama for character design and chief animation direction. ENGI produces the animation, with music by Yuki Hayashi. ANIMEC is credited as the Japanese distributor. Skating-specific credits include choreography by Akiko Suzuki and skating direction and 3DCG direction by Koji. These roles are useful context for an adaptation whose dramatic peaks depend on movement: viewers need to understand a performance while also following the person attempting it. Related reading: Aikatsu Stars! Movie: January 22, 2027 Release Date & Trailer . The principal Japanese cast includes Natsumi Haruse as Inori, Takeo Otsuka as Tsukasa, Kana Ichinose as Hikaru and Yuma Uchida as Jun. The official film project and its event coverage connect those central performers to the continuation. An English dub cast, if announced later, would be a separate set of credits. How to catch up before February Begin with the television anime's first and second seasons, then move to the movie. That order introduces Inori's starting point, her partnership with Tsukasa and the competitive relationships the championship story builds upon. A viewer interested primarily in the film will still benefit from seeing why this event matters to them. The official August update announced Japanese reruns of both television seasons, beginning October 1 on TOKYO MX and October 3 in BS Asahi's late-night schedule. Those broadcasts offer a domestic catch-up route. They are television reruns, with their own schedule, rather than a change to the February movie date. Outside Japan, check the season labels and local catalog in your streaming service. Availability of the television anime is useful for preparation but does not establish that the same service will receive the film on its theatrical opening day. Related reading: The Apothecary Diaries Movie: Luoqing and Yinshan Character PV . Can you read the manga first? TSURUMAIKADA created the manga, published by Kodansha in Japan and available in English from Kodansha USA. The opening volume provides the original introduction to Inori and Tsukasa. Starting there lets new readers experience their partnership developing rather than entering at an assumed movie chapter. The manga and anime are different release schedules, so a publisher's latest-volume synopsis should not be treated as the movie's announced plot. For another story about ambition, training and performance, see our Akane-banashi Season 2 guide , which covers its January 2027 return. Sources and verification Primary announcements and publisher information checked October 27, 2026.
