entries.title: One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2: January 2027 Release, New Trailer and JAM Project Opening
entries.description: One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2 premieres January 2027. Watch the official trailer, see the new key visual and learn about JAM Project's opening theme.
entries.content: OFFICIAL ANIME NEWS · OCTOBER 12, 2026 One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2: January 2027 Release, New Trailer and JAM Project Opening Saitama, Garou and the Monster Association return in January 2027. The anime's official website has unveiled a new key visual, its first promotional video for the second cour and the next opening theme from JAM Project. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy Official promotional-video thumbnail. The separate key visual is available from the anime's official announcement. © ONE, Yusuke Murata / Shueisha / Hero Association HQ. Release at a glance Release January 2027; exact date pending Where to watch Check licensed services in your country; no universal platform inferred Applies to Japanese broadcast announcement Still pending Exact day and international distribution schedule Release details checked October 24, 2026 · Official source October 11 update: Season 3 Blu-ray, DVD and exclusive OVA Alongside the January 2027 announcement for the second cour, the official One-Punch Man anime website confirmed a Season 3 Blu-ray and DVD series. Volume 1 is scheduled for January 27, 2027 in Japan . This is the Japanese home-video release date, not a newly announced broadcast date for Part 2. The official Volume 1 product listing confirms four television episodes plus an original animated bonus episode, OVA 3 #01: Saitama and the Toy Saitama Broke , based on an original concept by ONE. The limited edition also lists a special disc with highlights from the September 2025 music event and a 24-page booklet. The Japanese listing gives a tax-exclusive price of ¥12,000 for Blu-ray and ¥11,000 for DVD; pricing and availability elsewhere have not been confirmed here. This packaging announcement is separate from the official Part 2 television announcement . A precise January 2027 broadcast day for the second cour remains unannounced in that notice. Related reading: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Anime Shares Creditless Opening and Ending Videos . When does One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2 come out? The second cour of One-Punch Man Season 3 premieres in Japan in January 2027 . The anime's official website confirmed the month on October 11, 2026. It is a continuation of the third season, rather than a separately numbered fourth season. No exact broadcast day or episode count has been announced in the October update. Is January 27 the premiere date? No. January 27, 2027 is the Japanese release date for the first Season 3 Blu-ray and DVD volume, not the premiere of the second cour. The official production announcement confirms January 2027 as the television broadcast month but does not name the exact day. The promotional video and home-video product listing refer to different releases, so they should not be combined into one schedule. Related reading: Ascendance of a Bookworm Part 4 Anime Officially Announced . What does the new opening announcement confirm? The production has announced JAM Project's return for the second-cour opening, titled Never Done . That is a confirmed music credit, not evidence of a particular episode count or exact broadcast time. See the official October 11 production announcement . Watch the official Season 3 Part 2 trailer The first promotional video for the second cour teases the next stage of the Monster Association conflict, including major confrontations involving Garou and the S-Class heroes. The new footage accompanies the updated key visual unveiled by the production. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Opens on YouTube What does the new key visual reveal? The newly released visual brings together the characters preparing for the second cour's battles. Its composition emphasizes the clash between heroes and monsters and the looming confrontation involving Garou. The visual can be viewed on the official October 11 announcement . The image above is a still from the official PV, not a mislabeled key visual. JAM Project returns with a new opening song JAM Project will perform the second cour's opening theme, titled “Never Done ~Saikyo VS Saikyo~” (Japanese: Never Done～最強VS最恐～ ). The announcement includes a comment from JAM Project vocalist Hironobu Kageyama. The song's title evokes the series' conflict between overwhelming heroic power and terrifying adversaries, but it should not be treated as a plot synopsis. What story will Part 2 cover? Season 3 follows the struggle between the Hero Association and the Monster Association, with Garou's role becoming increasingly important. The second cour continues that conflict after the first cour's conclusion. Promotional footage highlights high-stakes confrontations, but the production has not released a complete episode-by-episode outline. Specific manga chapters and exact adaptation endpoints should not be presented as confirmed. Is there a new studio or staff change? J.C.STAFF is the animation studio behind Season 3, following its work on Season 2. The October 11 announcement focuses on the release month, promotional video, key art and opening theme; it does not announce a studio replacement for Part 2. Where can you watch One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2? The confirmed information in the latest Japanese announcement concerns the January 2027 television broadcast . International streaming schedules, regional platform availability and exact simulcast times for the second cour may differ. Fans should wait for a distributor announcement covering their country rather than assume the previous cour's licensing arrangements apply unchanged. How to confirm a streaming date in your country To verify a local launch, look for a distributor notice that names both your territory and the second cour, then check whether it gives a same-day simulcast or a later catalog date. A service carrying Season 3 Part 1 is not, by itself, confirmation that it has Part 2. A useful listing should identify the cour, the first available date in your country, and whether episodes arrive weekly or all at once. Subtitles and dubs can follow different schedules, so check the specific language track instead of assuming it launches with the Japanese broadcast. Until those details appear, January 2027 is the confirmed Japanese window; the local platform and time remain open. Frequently asked questions Is One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2 coming in 2026? No. Its Japanese premiere window is January 2027. Is Season 3 Part 2 the same as Season 4? No. The production identifies it as the second cour of Season 3. Who sings the opening? JAM Project returns with “Never Done～最強VS最恐～”. Is the exact premiere date confirmed? Not yet. Only January 2027 has been announced. Official sources One-Punch Man official announcement — October 11, 2026 · Official first PV · Crunchyroll's report . Browse the AniNextUp release calendar and latest anime news for further updates. entries.title: The Otome Heroine's Fight for Survival Anime Premieres July 2027
entries.description: The Otome Heroine's Fight for Survival anime premieres July 2027. See the confirmed cast, staff, official teaser timestamp, novel details and streaming status.
entries.content: NEW ANIME · OCTOBER 6, 2026 The Otome Heroine's Fight for Survival Anime Premieres July 2027 The Otome Heroine's Fight for Survival has locked in a July 2027 TV premiere. The latest announcement also reveals its teaser PV and visual, lead voice actor and core production staff. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Release at a glance Release window July 2027 · exact date TBA Format TV anime Lead cast Fuka Izumi as Alia Where to watch International platform unannounced Details checked October 24, 2026 · Official announcement RELEASE WINDOW JULY 2027 · EXACT DATE TBA Release status: July 2027 is confirmed The Otome Heroine’s Fight for Survival is set to begin as a TV anime in July 2027 . The official site has not announced an exact premiere day, weekly broadcast slot, episode count or international distributor. That makes July the useful planning answer for now; a more precise date would be speculation. The Japanese teaser PV was published by FURYU Pictures Channel on October 6, 2026 at 02:00:06 Pacific Daylight Time (09:00:06 UTC / 18:00:06 Japan Standard Time). The page’s datePublished metadata supplies the timestamp and original offset. What is the story about? The heroine begins as Alicia, an orphan whose parents are killed by monsters when she is four. She grows up in a church orphanage where the official synopsis describes her treatment as abusive. After an incident reveals that she is the heroine of an otome game, Alicia recognizes that even her parents’ deaths and present circumstances belong to a scripted scenario. She rejects that role, takes the adventurer’s name Alia and decides to survive on her own. The premise changes the usual question from “Which route will the heroine choose?” to “What can she do after refusing the route written for her?” That is an interpretation of the official premise, rather than a claim that the anime removes romance. Readers tracking other official fantasy adaptations can compare its character-first setup with The True Saint Was Banished . Readers tracking other official fantasy adaptations can compare its character-first setup with The True Saint Was Banished . The official site describes the adaptation as dark fantasy with battle and action, and introduces Alia as someone who disguises her hair color so her original identity is harder to recognize. Is Alia reincarnated into the game? No. The official introduction explicitly calls her a non-reincarnated protagonist. She is Alicia, a girl born into the game’s world; the revelation is that the world follows an otome-game scenario, not that she has arrived from another life. That distinction matters for readers comparing the series with familiar “villainess” or reincarnation stories: Alia has to make choices with the life and circumstances she already has, rather than relying on memories from a previous world. Related reading: The Fledgling Demon Lord's Starter Shop Anime Premieres January 2027 . Who is in the cast and production team? Fuka Izumi voices Alia. The anime is directed by Noriyoshi Sasaki, with series composition by Touko Machida and character designs by Hiroyuki Miseki. KOHTA YAMAMOTO, Shun Narita and Yuki Furuhashi are composing the music. STUDIO CLUTCH and Animation Studio Seven are jointly credited for animation production. These are the names announced by the official anime site; it has not yet published a complete supporting cast list. Izumi’s official comment describes Alia as emotionally restrained but determined, and says she is approaching the role with the character’s resolve in mind. The director’s comment points to Alia’s resistance to the heroine’s assigned fate, the surrounding villainess characters and the series’ action-fantasy emphasis. Those production comments help explain the adaptation’s announced direction without predicting how individual scenes will be staged. How did the release announcement develop? The project was announced as in development in January 2025. On October 6, 2026, the official update confirmed the July 2027 window, teaser visual and PV, plus principal cast and staff. The month is now set; a Japanese broadcast timetable is still pending. Related reading: Haru to Gen Anime Premieres January 4, 2027: Cast and Teaser . Where does the anime’s source material start? The original light novels are written by Haru no Hiyori, illustrated by Hitaki Yuu and published in Japan by TO Books. The official anime site listed 11 novel volumes and nine manga volumes as of October 2026; it notes that manga volume nine went on sale October 15. The comic is drawn by Wakasakobato. The anime announcement does not say which volume or chapter the first season will adapt, so there is no confirmed “read from volume X after the finale” answer yet. For another fantasy series with a game-adjacent premise, see our Reincarnated as a Goblin release guide . For another fantasy series with a game-adjacent premise, see our Reincarnated as a Goblin release guide . The official introduction also reports that the series passed 900,000 copies in cumulative publication by October 2026, compared with 400,000 when the anime project was first announced. This is a series-wide publication figure, not a forecast of anime viewership or a promise about the adaptation’s length. It does show that the anime is arriving after several years of growth for the original novels and comic. If you want to sample the story before the broadcast, begin with the first novel or first manga volume rather than jumping ahead. The two formats share the core premise but are separate editions with different creators and pacing. The publisher’s own book listings are the reliable place to check the available volumes; translated editions and regional release dates may differ. Related reading: Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story Premieres January 2027 on Crunchyroll . Where can I watch it, and how many episodes will it have? No streaming platform or territory has been officially confirmed, and no episode total has been announced. A July Japanese TV window does not by itself confirm a same-day global release. Check your local service after a distributor publishes its lineup, and treat any currently circulating platform or episode-count claim as unconfirmed unless it appears in an official announcement. The useful confirmed facts are the month, the lead cast member, the principal staff, the two animation studios and the teaser. Still open are the exact day and time, broadcast stations, episode count, additional cast, theme songs and overseas streaming rights. AniNextUp will update those details when the production committee or a licensed distributor confirms them. Watch the official teaser PV ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER FURYU Pictures Channel Verified upload time: October 6, 2026 at 02:00:06 PDT (UTC−07:00), which is 18:00:06 JST. YouTube’s original video page exposes this exact datePublished timestamp. Official sources Official July 2027 broadcast window, teaser visual and PV Official lead-cast, staff and studio announcement Official story introduction, character profile and books list TO Books light-novel listing and story description TO Books manga volume 9 listing Official teaser PV and YouTube publication metadata Updated: October 24, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error

entries.title: Paw & Palaces Releases Creditless Ending Video Featuring “Chill Choose!”
entries.description: Paw & Palaces' Japanese dub releases its creditless ending video featuring Riko Azuna's Chill Choose! Watch the official video and see confirmed credits.
entries.content: OFFICIAL ANIME NEWS · OCTOBER 14, 2026 Paw & Palaces Releases Creditless Ending Video Featuring “Chill Choose!” The Japanese-dubbed edition of Paw & Palaces has unveiled a creditless ending sequence featuring Riko Azuna's song “Chill Choose!” The anime's official Japanese website confirmed the video and music credits on October 10, 2026. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy Still from the official creditless ending video published by the anime's Japanese production. Release at a glance Anime Paw & Palaces ( Shikin Gonyanbo: Shikinjo Neko Keibishitsu ) New video Creditless ending animation Official announcement October 10, 2026 Ending song “Chill Choose!” — Riko Azuna Opening song “Truly” — Riko Azuna Japanese-dub broadcast Began October 10, 2026 What is new in the ending announcement? The latest promotional update focuses on the closing sequence, not a new season or a change to the broadcast schedule. A creditless ending removes the overlaid production credits, allowing viewers to see the animation without text covering the imagery. The October 10 update on the Japanese production website also pointed fans toward an episode-five preview. That makes the clip useful both for fans following the Japanese-dub release and for viewers interested in the show's music and artwork. It is a promotional sequence rather than a full episode; the embedded video below is the official ending clip referenced by the announcement. Official creditless ending video released The official website for Paw & Palaces (Japanese title: Shikin Gonyanbo: Shikinjo Neko Keibishitsu ) announced the creditless ending video on October 10, alongside an episode-five preview. The new sequence highlights the series' feline cast and provides a clear look at the ending animation without the on-screen staff credits. ▶ PLAY OFFICIAL VIDEO Paw & Palaces · Creditless ending Does the creditless ending include a new episode? No. A creditless ending is the show's existing closing animation presented without overlaid staff credits. The October 10 promotional video is separate from the episode-five preview mentioned in the same announcement. It also does not announce a new season or an international streaming date; viewers looking for full episodes should use an officially licensed service in their region. Ending theme: “Chill Choose!” by Riko Azuna The official announcement credits Riko Azuna with writing and composing “Chill Choose!”, with arrangement by NRP. The same notice separately identifies “Truly” as the opening theme, also performed by Azuna. This distinction matters because some secondary reports have mixed up the two songs. About the Japanese dub The series follows six cats who guard the cultural memories held within the Forbidden City's treasures. The Japanese-dubbed edition began broadcasting in Japan on October 10, 2026. Crunchyroll also carries the show in supported regions, although audio options and availability vary by territory. What is Paw & Palaces about? The fantasy series follows six cats connected to the Forbidden City's historical treasures. Its premise mixes animal characters with stories about protecting cultural memories, giving the ending sequence a different context from the action-heavy previews common to seasonal anime. The creditless release is an opportunity to focus on the closing animation itself. Where can viewers watch it? The official video is available through the player above, which loads YouTube only after the play button is selected. For the Japanese-dubbed episodes, availability depends on the broadcaster or streaming platform and the viewer's location. The release of an ending video does not itself confirm worldwide streaming rights or additional language tracks. What does the music announcement confirm? Riko Azuna is credited for both theme songs, but they serve different roles: “Chill Choose!” closes the episodes, while “Truly” opens them. The production notice names NRP as the ending track's arranger. Fans looking for the song featured in this video should therefore search for the ending title, not the opening. Official sources Official anime website — October 10 ending-video and song announcement · Crunchyroll News — October 13 coverage Who are the six guardians? The official Japanese character profiles introduce Soubi as the team's leader, Oboi as a powerful fighter and Heian as an observant former stray. Zeze specializes in gathering information, while the older Rohan supports the group with his knowledge of history and folklore. Momo, Oboi's younger sister, also works in a support role. In the Japanese dub, Kazuki Ura voices Soubi, Makoto Furukawa voices Oboi, Sora Amamiya voices Heian, Takeo Otsuka voices Zeze, Kentaro Tone voices Rohan and Hikaru Tono voices Momo. These are credits for the Japanese-language edition; viewers should consult their local platform for the audio and subtitles offered there. How did the Japanese release begin? The production's September broadcast notice scheduled the first four episodes together on Tokyo MX on October 10 at 8 p.m. Japan time. From episode five, it listed a Wednesday 11:30 p.m. slot. BS Nippon TV has a separate schedule, so its late-night listing should not be assumed to match Tokyo MX or an international streaming service. On Japanese television, a time such as 25:00 refers to 1 a.m. on the following calendar day. The official schedule can change, and Crunchyroll's episode listing may display a different local date or time. Check the service in your region for the current episode and language options rather than using the Japanese broadcast hour as a worldwide release time. How does this version relate to the original series? The Japanese production describes this edition as a Japanese dub of a Chinese animated series, based on a comic inspired by cats living in Beijing's Forbidden City. Its official credits identify iQIYI as producer and KADOKAWA as producer of the Japanese version. The Japanese voices and theme songs accompany the existing story; the ending clip does not establish that a new season has been announced. The October 10 music notice lists “Chill Choose!” as the ending, with lyrics and composition by Riko Azuna and arrangement by NRP. It separately lists “Truly” as the opening, arranged by eba. Both were listed for digital release on October 11. The two titles are distinct, even though the same artist is credited for both. Sources checked October 26, 2026: the official Japanese production website and its broadcast and music notices. Regional availability can change. Updated: October 26, 2026 · Published: October 14, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections

entries.title: Pokémon Horizons Anime Unseals Treasures of Ruin in Latest Wonder Voyage Arc Trailer
entries.description: A new Pokémon Horizons: Wonder Voyage trailer highlights the Treasures of Ruin—Wo-Chien, Chien-Pao, Ting-Lu and Chi-Yu—as the anime's Paldea storyline continues.
entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · 2026-10-09 Pokémon Horizons Anime Unseals Treasures of Ruin in Latest Wonder Voyage Arc Trailer A new Pokémon Horizons: Wonder Voyage trailer highlights the Treasures of Ruin—Wo-Chien, Chien-Pao, Ting-Lu and Chi-Yu—as the anime's Paldea storyline continues. By AniNextUp Editorial Team Release at a glance Release October 16, 2026: episode 153 Where to watch TV Tokyo in Japan Region and timing Wonder Voyage began May 22 in Japan. The U.S. Season 4 Netflix milestone is February 27, 2027. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Pokémon Horizons official TV Tokyo page · Pokémon Japan official announcement · Pokémon’s Season 4 Netflix announcement New Wonder Voyage trailer spotlights the Treasures of Ruin A new trailer for Pokémon Horizons: The Series puts four Legendary Pokémon from the Paldea region in the spotlight. Wo-Chien, Chien-Pao, Ting-Lu and Chi-Yu, collectively known as the Treasures of Ruin, appear in the latest preview for the anime's continuing Wonder Voyage storyline. Crunchyroll reported the trailer on October 9, 2026. Who are the four Treasures of Ruin? The quartet first appeared in the Pokémon Scarlet and Violet games. Wo-Chien is a Dark/Grass-type Pokémon, Chien-Pao is Dark/Ice, Ting-Lu is Dark/Ground, and Chi-Yu is Dark/Fire. The games associate the four with ancient objects and seals, providing background for why their appearance is important to a Paldea-centered story. The trailer's release does not by itself establish the outcome of their role in the anime. Where does the trailer fit in Wonder Voyage? The Wonder Voyage arc began airing in Japan on May 22, 2026. Its story continues the journey of Liko, Roy, Dot and Ult alongside the Rising Volt Tacklers. Earlier official promotional material introduced the arc's new adventures and characters; the October preview shifts attention toward the consequences of the Treasures of Ruin being unsealed. Related reading: Pokémon Horizons Season 4: February 27 Netflix Date, Story and Trailer . What does the new trailer leave unanswered? The official promotional material shows the Treasures of Ruin entering the Wonder Voyage storyline, but it does not establish how the conflict will end or whether the four Pokémon will play equal roles. The October 16 Japanese story date is also not the same as the separately announced February 27, 2027 U.S. Netflix release for Wonders Ahead . Keeping those two schedules distinct helps avoid misleading international viewers. When did the Paldea story begin? The Japanese Paldea story began on October 16, 2026. TV Tokyo’s official listing records a 6:55–7:25 p.m. broadcast that day. As of this October 26 update, that date is in the past. It is a Japanese broadcast date, not a simultaneous worldwide streaming launch. Watch the official announcement Find the preview through Crunchyroll’s October 9 trailer coverage . The existing article also links the Pokémon YouTube upload and official anime announcement . For episode dates and the premise of the Paldea investigation, consult the broadcaster’s listing below. A promotional video and a television schedule answer different questions about the same story. Related reading: Frieren Season 3 Release Date: October 2027 & Golden Land Arc . Explore the anime release calendar and latest news . What the official episode synopsis establishes TV Tokyo places the October 16 story at Orange Academy's school festival. Liko and her companions receive a request from Raifort to investigate unusual phenomena around Paldea. The incidents appear to be occurring near shrines associated with an ancient calamity. The synopsis also says Navie meets Team Star during the visit. These are details from the broadcaster's advance description, rather than a claim that the trailer reveals every event in the episode. This makes the shrines the useful starting point for understanding the news. The story connects a familiar Paldea location with a mystery affecting several places across the region. It does not follow that the anime will reproduce the games' quest in exactly the same order. A synopsis can establish an investigation and its setting without confirming who resolves it, which Pokémon are caught or how the conflict ends. Related reading: MASHLE Season 3 Release Date: January 2027, Arc and Teaser . Wonder Voyage and Wonders Ahead use different release calendars The Japanese arc name and the English season title should be kept distinct when checking availability. The Pokémon Company's October 6 international announcement names the fourth English season Pokémon Horizons: Season 4—Wonders Ahead and sets Part 1 for February 27, 2027, exclusively on Netflix in the United States. It also says further episodes will arrive later. That announcement describes Liko, Roy and the Rising Volt Tacklers continuing their travels, with Dot, Ult, Navie and a stowaway Ditto among the characters mentioned. It provides a season-level introduction rather than a dated list for every Japanese episode. Readers should therefore avoid treating February 27 as a separately confirmed release date for this particular Treasures of Ruin story. The press release does not provide that episode-by-episode mapping. Where the wider arc started The official May 8 Japanese announcement sets the start of Wonder Voyage for May 22 and introduces its new adventures for Liko, Roy, Dot and Ult. Its promotional visual includes Navie, Ditto, Koraidon and Miraidon. That earlier announcement helps place the October trailer inside a continuing arc, rather than presenting it as the start of an unrelated Pokémon series. Related reading: ONE PIECE: Elbaph Arc English Dub Release Date and Crunchyroll Schedule . For viewers catching up, choose the regional edition you are actually watching before comparing dates or episode numbers. Japanese broadcast information, a trailer's upload date and a Netflix season launch describe different releases. Use the linked official announcements for their respective territories, and check your local service for the episodes currently available to your account. Updated October 26, 2026. entries.title: Pokémon Horizons Season 4: February 27 Netflix Date, Story and Trailer
entries.description: Pokémon Horizons Season 4 Part 1 premieres February 27, 2027 on Netflix in the U.S. and Latin America. Get the official story, trailer and confirmed details.
entries.content: POKÉMON · OCTOBER 6, 2026 Pokémon Horizons Season 4: February 27 Netflix Date, Story and Trailer Pokémon Horizons: Season 4—Wonders Ahead Part 1 premieres on Netflix on February 27, 2027 in the United States and Latin America. Here is what the official announcements confirm about the story, returning characters, trailer and later episodes. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official Wonders Ahead Season 4 artwork. Source: The Pokémon Company International press release . U.S. RELEASE FEBRUARY 27, 2027 · NETFLIX · U.S. & LATIN AMERICA Release at a glance Release February 27, 2027; Part 1 Where to watch Netflix in the United States and Latin America Still unannounced Part 1 episode count, later-batch dates and availability in other regions Release details checked October 24, 2026 · Official U.S. announcement · Official Latin American announcement When does Pokémon Horizons Season 4 come out? Part 1 of Pokémon Horizons: Season 4—Wonders Ahead premieres February 27, 2027 on Netflix. The Pokémon Company International announced the date on October 6, 2026. Its English-language release confirms the same day for viewers in the United States, while the company's Latin American announcement also gives February 27 for that region. This is the start of Season 4's international Netflix rollout. It should not be read as a promise that every episode will arrive at once: the official wording identifies the launch specifically as Part 1 and says additional episodes will follow later. Where can you watch Wonders Ahead? Netflix is the confirmed exclusive home for Part 1 in the United States and Latin America . The English press release covers the U.S.; Pokémon's official Spanish-language release separately confirms Latin America. Viewers in territories outside those announcements should check their regional Pokémon and Netflix listings, because no single worldwide date is stated in the sources reviewed here. Related reading: Pokémon Horizons Anime Unseals Treasures of Ruin in Latest Wonder Voyage Arc Trailer . The first three seasons are already available on Netflix in the U.S., according to the official announcement. That gives new viewers a direct catch-up route before the February premiere. Availability can differ by country, so the title's presence in one Netflix catalog does not establish another catalog's schedule. How many episodes are in Part 1? An episode count has not been announced for Part 1. Pokémon also has not dated the later Season 4 batches. “Part 1” confirms a divided release, but it does not reveal the size of the first batch or the total number of Season 4 episodes. We will treat those figures as unknown until Pokémon or Netflix publishes them. What is Pokémon Horizons Season 4 about? The official synopsis begins after Laquium is no longer a threat. Liko, Roy and the Rising Volt Tacklers set out to experience the Pokémon world afresh aboard the Brave Olivine. Their next travels include unusual Pokémon encounters, learning about Pokémon sleep styles and racing alongside Legendary Pokémon. Related reading: Medalist Movie Release Date: February 19, 2027, Story and Cast . The new chapter continues the characters' growth with their partner Pokémon rather than resetting the story. Pokémon's synopsis also names Dot and Ult among the returning travelers. New faces include a stowaway Ditto and a lively girl named Navie, both highlighted as part of the adventures ahead. The announcement does not identify a single new central villain or disclose the outcome of these storylines. Do you need to watch the earlier seasons first? Wonders Ahead is a continuation, so watching the earlier Pokémon Horizons seasons is the clearest way to understand Liko and Roy's development, the Rising Volt Tacklers and why the end of the Laquium threat matters. The official material calls Season 4 a new chapter, but it does not describe it as a reboot or a stand-alone entry. If time is limited, viewers should at least finish the most recent Season 3 episodes before starting Part 1. The Season 4 synopsis openly builds on the previous conflict, so skipping directly to Wonders Ahead may reveal where that storyline leaves the cast. Related reading: THE ONE PIECE Release Date: February 2027, Episodes & Where to Watch . What does the official trailer confirm? The 47-second trailer presents the returning group, the Brave Olivine's renewed journey and quick looks at the new encounters described in the synopsis. It is promotional footage rather than an episode guide, so it does not confirm the Part 1 episode count or later release dates. YouTube's original page metadata records the official upload at 9:00:03 a.m. UTC−07:00 on October 6, 2026 (4:00:03 p.m. UTC). The video was published by The Official Pokémon YouTube channel; that timestamp is retained in the page's VideoObject data rather than inferred from YouTube's rounded “days ago” label. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER The Official Pokémon YouTube channel What time will Season 4 appear on Netflix? Pokémon's announcements give the calendar date but do not publish an exact Netflix release time . February 27, 2027 falls on a Saturday. A viewer should use the title page inside their own regional Netflix account as the final availability check on release day, because catalog updates and displayed times can depend on territory and account location. AniNextUp will not convert the date into an unsupported midnight estimate. Searching Netflix for Pokémon Horizons is also more reliable than looking for a separate series page: the official release identifies Wonders Ahead as Season 4 of the continuing show. If Netflix later lists a countdown or episode total, that platform data would answer questions the October announcements leave open. What remains unknown? Pokémon has confirmed the title, February 27 date, Netflix platforms for the announced regions, returning team and basic premise. The Part 1 episode count, later-part dates and schedules for other territories remain unannounced. Those distinctions matter when planning a catch-up: February 27 is a verified regional Part 1 premiere, not a confirmed worldwide full-season release. AniNextUp status: February 27, 2027 and Netflix are confirmed for Part 1 in the U.S. and Latin America. Episode totals, later-part dates and other regional schedules remain TBA. Updated: October 24, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error Official sources The Pokémon Company International: U.S. Season 4 press release The Pokémon Company International: Latin American Season 4 press release Pokémon.com: Wonders Ahead Netflix announcement Trailer verification: The Official Pokémon YouTube channel ; original upload metadata checked October 24, 2026.

entries.title: Prisma Illya FINALE: 2027 Release, Cast & Broadcast Update
entries.description: Prisma Illya FINALE concludes the anime series on Japanese TV in 2027. See the confirmed broadcasters, returning cast, story context and what remains unknown.
entries.content: 2027 · RETURNING SERIES · OCTOBER 24, 2026 Prisma Illya FINALE: 2027 Release, Cast & Broadcast Update Fate/kaleid liner Prisma Illya FINALE will begin Japanese television broadcasts in 2027 on TOKYO MX, ABC TV and AT-X. The October 18 announcement confirms the broadcasters, while an exact premiere month, episode count and international streaming service remain unannounced in the cited materials. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases ©2027 Hiroshi Hiroyama, TYPE-MOON / KADOKAWA / Fate/kaleid liner Prisma Illya FINALE Production Committee. Official promotional image from the production website . Release at a glance Release window 2027 · exact month and day TBA Japan TOKYO MX, ABC TV and AT-X Studio SILVER LINK. International streaming Not confirmed in the cited announcements Official sources checked October 24, 2026 · Official website What changed in the October 18 announcement? The franchise revealed the named Japanese broadcasters during its Machi Asobi stage event on October 18. The official broadcaster notice confirms a 2027 television start on TOKYO MX, ABC TV and AT-X. It does not give an opening day or weekly airtime. The 2027 television project was already announced in July. The October update therefore adds broadcast destinations rather than a new premiere date. Readers should keep that distinction when comparing older announcement stories with the latest schedule information. Is FINALE a television series or another movie? FINALE is a television production. The July announcement from KADOKAWA presents it as the anime series' conclusion. The official site connects the project to the previously announced continuation of Prisma Illya Licht: The Nameless Girl . This is a continuation of the Prisma Illya story, rather than an announced standalone reboot. Viewers looking for a first entry should distinguish the earlier television installments and films from the forthcoming FINALE release. Returning studio, staff and Japanese cast The official FINALE website lists SILVER LINK. as the animation studio. Shin Oonuma returns as director, with Ken Takahashi as series director, Kenji Inoue and Hazuki Minase on scripts, and Kazuya Hirata on character design. Mai Kadowaki as Illyasviel von Einzbern Kaori Nazuka as Miyu Edelfelt Chiwa Saito as Chloe von Einzbern Sumire Morohoshi as Pandora Natsuki Hanae as Julian Ainsworth Katsuyuki Konishi as Darius Ainsworth These are Japanese voice credits. They do not establish an English dub cast or a dubbed release schedule. What is the final story about? The official introduction places Illya, Miyu and Chloe against Darius as the consequences of opening Pandora's box threaten their world. The continuation builds on the Ainsworth storyline and the mystery surrounding Pandora. That framing is also why FINALE should not be presented as an unrelated new Fate adaptation. Official visuals and promotional videos The official site displays the FINALE promotional artwork, including its second teaser visual. The image above is the production's official social preview for this specific project, rather than artwork from an older film. Related reading: Kagurabachi Episodes 1–2 to Premiere March 25, 2027: World Tour Finale Details . For current promotional materials, use the official FINALE site . No FINALE-specific playable YouTube trailer has been verified for this guide; a video for an earlier Prisma Illya installment should not be relabeled as a trailer for the new series. Where will Prisma Illya FINALE stream? The October announcement identifies Japanese television channels. It does not announce worldwide streaming, subtitle languages or regional availability. Previous installments' distribution arrangements cannot establish where FINALE will be licensed. What is still unconfirmed? The exact premiere date, episode count, international streaming partner and English dub timetable are not established by the cited announcements. This same guide can be updated when the production or a regional distributor publishes those details. For more confirmed announcements, browse our latest anime news and January 2027 anime guide . A Japanese broadcast announcement does not establish international streaming availability. Should you watch earlier entries before FINALE? Yes, especially if Prisma Illya is new to you. The official announcement calls FINALE the end of the anime series, and KADOKAWA’s July update describes it as a continuation tied to the film Licht: The Nameless Girl . The current synopsis begins after Illya’s battle with the Ainsworth family and centers on Darius, Pandora, Illya, Miyu and Chloe, so the returning conflict matters to the setup. A practical catch-up route is to watch the TV entries in release order— Prisma Illya , Zwei! , Zwei Herz! and 3rei!! —then see Licht before FINALE. The franchise also has other films and specials; the new announcement does not say that every side story is required. Use the official series portal and the official Licht film site to identify those earlier entries. This is a practical viewing route, not a checklist issued by the production committee. How should readers compare the July and October updates? The two announcements answer different questions. KADOKAWA introduced FINALE as a 2027 television project in July; the October 18 notice later named TOKYO MX, ABC TV and AT-X. The newer broadcaster list does not narrow the year to a particular month or day. If another article gives a specific premiere date without a separate production or station notice, that date should be treated as unconfirmed. The same distinction applies to airtime: a confirmed channel list is not yet a weekly schedule. Checking the official FINALE site and the listed Japanese stations is the clearest way to follow a later timetable without confusing a new detail with the earlier announcement. What does the returning cast confirm? The six published Japanese cast credits cover Illya, Miyu, Chloe and Pandora, along with Julian and Darius from the Ainsworth side of the conflict. They confirm returning roles at the center of the announced story, but the production has not described this as a complete cast list. These names also do not confirm an English dub, dubbing studio or overseas schedule. For someone deciding whether FINALE stands alone, the returning characters and the official synopsis point to a direct continuation of the Ainsworth storyline rather than a separate entry. Viewers can treat the July cast notice as a first group of credits and wait for later announcements for additional roles. entries.title: PSYREN Anime Release Date, Time & Where to Watch
entries.description: PSYREN premiered October 5, 2026. Compare Japan and Crunchyroll times, meet the cast, find the manga and check what remains unconfirmed.
entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · OCTOBER 26, 2026 PSYREN Anime Release Date, Time & Where to Watch PSYREN began on October 5, 2026. Here is how its Japanese broadcast differs from Crunchyroll streaming, where to start the manga, and which adaptation details remain unconfirmed. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official PSYREN promotional artwork. © Toshiaki Iwashiro, Shueisha/PSYREN Secret Society. Official source . WHERE TO WATCH Crunchyroll Release at a glance Release Premiered October 5, 2026; Crunchyroll debut at 07:30 PDT (14:30 UTC) Where to watch Crunchyroll in licensed territories Japan / studio TOKYO MX and BS11: Mondays 23:00 JST · Satelight Release details checked October 26, 2026 · Crunchyroll’s PSYREN release announcement When did PSYREN start, and where can you watch? PSYREN premiered on October 5, 2026. Crunchyroll's release announcement places the subtitled debut at 7:30 a.m. Pacific Time, with availability worldwide excluding Japan and China. That was the opening episode's announced streaming time; it should not be read as a promise covering every later episode, language track or service. For the premiere date, 7:30 a.m. Pacific was 14:30 UTC: 10:30 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time, 10:30 a.m. in Santo Domingo and 3:30 p.m. British Summer Time. These are conversions of the October 5 announcement. Daylight-saving changes can alter later local-clock equivalents, so check your regional episode listing before planning a weekly reminder. Why the Japanese schedule shows a different time The official Japanese schedule lists TOKYO MX and BS11 on Mondays at 23:00 JST from October 5. Sun TV lists Monday at 24:00, meaning midnight at the start of Tuesday. Mie TV begins October 7 at 24:20, meaning October 8 at 00:20 JST. Japanese late-night notation preserves the broadcaster's programming day; your calendar may display the following date. Related reading: Chitose Is in the Ramune Bottle Cour 2 Release Date & Time . Japanese streaming begins from October 5 at 23:30 JST, with exceptions for some services. The schedule includes ABEMA, Prime Video, Hulu and U-NEXT among its subscription options. Those Japanese licenses do not establish international availability on the same brands. Use Crunchyroll's territorial announcement for its simulcast and the Japanese schedule for domestic distribution. What is PSYREN about? The official premise starts with first-year high-school student Ageha Yoshina finding a red telephone card in a public phone booth. His childhood friend Sakurako Amamiya has a matching card, then disappears. Searching for her draws Ageha toward Psyren, a rumored secret society linked to disappearances across Japan, and into a game with lethal stakes. This is a useful starting point for viewers choosing between a battle series and a mystery: the rescue gives Ageha a personal reason to enter, while the cards and disappearances provide questions beyond who wins a fight. That is our reading of the published setup, rather than a verdict on the full adaptation. The premise does not reveal the game's answers, and this guide avoids them. Related reading: DARK MACHINE THE ANIMATION Release Date & Time . Do you need to read the manga first? No preparatory reading is necessary to understand the announced introduction. The anime starts with Ageha's discovery, making Episode 1 the practical entry point. If you prefer reading, VIZ's official Psyren page identifies Toshiaki Iwashiro as the creator and offers a Volume 1 preview. It describes a dangerous alternate dimension and powers that complicate Ageha's understanding of both worlds. The manga is complete: VIZ labels Volume 16 as the final volume . Starting at Volume 1 lets you follow its clues in order. Avoid jumping to the last book's synopsis if you want the central mystery preserved. A completed source series does not by itself confirm how much a television season adapts. Who makes the anime and voices the characters? The official production credits name Satelight as animation studio, Katsumi Ono as director, Shin Yoshida for series composition and Akira Okuma for character design. Yoshitaka Taniguchi designs the creatures. Takashi Ohmama, Tatsuhiko Saiki and Shu Kanematsu compose the music. Related reading: The Vermilion Mask Release Date, Time & Where to Watch . Rikuya Yasuda voices Ageha, with Mayuko Kazama as Sakurako. Shunsuke Takeuchi plays Hiryu Asaga, Soma Saito plays Oboro Mochizuki and Yukihiro Nozuyama plays Kabuto Kirisaki. The cast also includes Yuhko Kaida as Matsuri Yagumo and Nobuyuki Hiyama as Dolkey. These are Japanese cast credits; they are not an English-dub lineup. What are the opening and ending songs? The official music page identifies CLAN QUEEN's “WARNING!!” as the first-cour opening and Who-ya Extended's “ICARUS” as its ending. A first-cour song credit is not an episode-total announcement. Opening and ending videos are also separate promotional uploads from a teaser or story trailer. How do you choose the right episode listing? Start with the series page in the service available to you, then check the episode number and audio language. A premiere article answers when the show launched; it cannot establish whether today's episode has appeared in every catalog. If the entry is missing, compare your account's territory with the announced exclusions before assuming the Japanese broadcast was delayed. Subtitles and dubbed audio can have separate release listings. Related reading: The World's Strongest Witch Release Date, Time & Where to Watch . What still needs confirmation? This review did not establish an exact episode total, the television adaptation's final manga chapter, or a verified English-dub release schedule. The earlier version claimed that the entire manga would be adapted; the primary pages checked here did not substantiate that promise, so it has been removed. Check the platform's language selector for what is actually available in your territory. Watch the official promotional videos The official video gallery separates its trailer, two teasers and clean theme sequences. Use those labels when comparing clips. The embedded clip is Crunchyroll in Spanish’s official Spanish-language trailer, published July 12, 2026. The English gallery links a separate official trailer. The precise original upload time and timezone could not be independently verified, so no precise upload timestamp or VideoObject is asserted. ▶ WATCH SPANISH TRAILER Crunchyroll in Spanish Updated: October 26, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error Official release reference: Crunchyroll premiere date, time and territories .

entries.description: Expelled from Paradise sequel reveals a new main trailer and Beyond the Night theme song. Release date, cast, and official video.
entries.content: NOVEMBER 13 · ANIME MOVIE Expelled from Paradise Sequel Reveals Main Trailer and Beyond the Night Theme Song The new main trailer previews the sci-fi sequel and its theme song “Beyond the Night” ahead of the November 13, 2026 Japanese theatrical release. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official key visual by Masatsugu Saito. © Toei Animation · Nitroplus / Expelled from Paradise Society 2. Official announcement · Image source . Release at a glance Release November 13, 2026 Where to watch Japanese theaters Applies to Japanese theatrical opening, not worldwide streaming Still pending International cinema dates and streaming partners Release details checked October 13, 2026 · Official source JAPAN RELEASE November 13, 2026 FORMAT Theatrical anime film STUDIO Toei Animation New main trailer and key visual revealed The official film project has released a new main trailer and key visual for Rakuen Tsuihou: Kokoro no Resonance , the sequel to Expelled from Paradise . The footage follows Gabriel and fellow agents as they investigate the Fallen, while a preview of the new theme song accompanies the action. Character designer Masatsugu Saito drew the new key visual. The official site dates its main trailer announcement to October 12 and its theme song announcement to October 13, 2026, in Japan. Neither announcement specifies an exact publication time. The film remains scheduled for Japanese theaters on November 13, 2026 . “Beyond the Night” theme song: artists and release dates TeddyLoid wrote, composed and arranged “Beyond the Night.” It features Ayane Sakura , who voices Gabriel, and Nagi Inoue of Nogizaka46. The song arrives digitally on November 11, 2026 , with a CD release scheduled for November 18, 2026 . These updates concern the Japanese theatrical opening and music release. International cinema and streaming dates have not been confirmed in the announcements. Related reading: Noa Is My Senior, and My Friend Anime: 2027 Release, Main Cast and First Visual . What connects the sequel to Expelled from Paradise The conflict between DEVA's virtual society and people living on Earth's surface remains a useful lens for approaching Kokoro no Resonance. The sequel's pursuit of the Fallen suggests that crossing between those worlds continues to carry political and personal consequences. Returning creative staff offers continuity, but the announced premise should not be mistaken for a full account of the film's plot. Do viewers need to see the first film? Kokoro no Resonance is explicitly presented as a sequel to Expelled from Paradise . Its returning DEVA-versus-Earth setting and references to earlier events mean the 2014 film offers relevant background for Gabriel's investigation of the Fallen. The official synopsis does not establish that prior viewing is mandatory, but watching the first movie is the clearest way to understand the world and its history before the new theatrical release. Planning to watch outside Japan November 13 is the confirmed Japanese theatrical opening, not a worldwide streaming premiere. No international subscription-platform date is established by that announcement. Fans outside Japan should look for a separate distributor or cinema notice before making release-day plans. Related reading: Fool Night Release Date: November 26 on Netflix . When does Kokoro no Resonance release? Rakuen Tsuihou: Kokoro no Resonance opens in Japanese theaters on November 13, 2026. It is the long-awaited sequel to the 2014 science-fiction anime film Expelled from Paradise. What is the movie about? The sequel returns to the conflict between the virtual society of DEVA and life on Earth. Gabriel and other agents pursue the mysterious Fallen—former security personnel who escaped to the surface after the events involving Angela Balzac—expanding the world established by the first movie. Who is making the sequel? Seiji Mizushima returns as director and Gen Urobuchi writes the screenplay. Masatsugu Saito handles character design, NARASAKI composes the music and Toei Animation produces the film, reuniting core creative staff from the original project. Related reading: The Moon on a Rainy Night Anime: 2027 Release, Trailer & Cast . Where to watch The November 13 date currently refers specifically to the Japanese theatrical release . An international streaming date has not been announced, so AniNextUp is keeping theatrical and streaming availability separate until an official platform announcement is made. Who voices Gabriel and the other characters? The film's official cast list names Ayane Sakura as Gabriel, Saori Hayami as Arma and Yoshino Aoyama as Danelle. Sally Amaki voices Raguel, Sumire Morohoshi voices Penemue and Rie Kugimiya returns as Angela Balzac. Sakura also appears on the theme song in character as Gabriel, connecting the music announcement to the film's lead. These credits come from the Japanese production's announced cast. They do not establish an English dub or the language options that might accompany a future international release. Those details will depend on any later distributor or platform announcement. Related reading: Witch on the Holy Night Movie: Release Date and Theaters . How does the Fallen investigation begin? The official synopsis places the story in the year 2400, when humanity lives in the digital world of DEVA. After events associated with Angela's rebellion, a group of security agents escapes to Earth with physical bodies and hardware containing their personal data. Known as the Fallen, they become the subject of a search ordered by DEVA. Gabriel and her fellow agents must pursue that assignment on the surface, where the effects of a nanohazard remain. The setup gives returning viewers a connection to Angela's earlier story while introducing a new investigation; the official synopsis does not reveal its outcome. What does the main trailer show? Aniplex says the main trailer uses new footage centered on Gabriel's perspective and concludes with a look at the new Mega Arhan machine. The promotional video offers a preview of the sequel's action and theme song, but it is not a substitute for a complete synopsis or a release announcement outside Japan. entries.content: FALL 2026 · RELEASE GUIDE The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 premieres October 1, 2026 PT / October 2 JST on Netflix. Release date, studio and streaming details for Fall 2026. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official promotional visual. Artwork source: official release announcement . RELEASE DATE October 1, 2026 PT / October 2 JST STREAMING Netflix STUDIO STUDIO KAI Release at a glance Release October 1 PT / October 2 JST, 2026 Where to watch Netflix; weekly episodes Region and timing These are time-zone-specific dates from Netflix’s announcement. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Netflix’s October anime lineup What to remember about the four central relationships Koyuki's difficulty opening up to others remains important as her friendships with Miki, Minato and Yota evolve. The continuation's emotional stakes come from how those relationships change, rather than from a new cast replacing the existing group. The announced weekly Netflix rollout also gives viewers time to follow those shifts episode by episode. Why Netflix gives two premiere dates October 1 in Pacific Time and October 2 in Japan can refer to the same worldwide launch viewed from different time zones. They should not be read as evidence of a delayed Japanese release. The weekly rollout also means that the premiere date is the start of the new story, not the day every episode becomes available. When does The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 premiere? Season 2 premieres worldwide on Netflix on October 1, 2026 PT / October 2 JST. Netflix's October anime announcement lists a weekly episode rollout rather than a full-season drop. Where to watch The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 is a Netflix release. Because the global launch crosses time zones, Netflix describes the premiere as October 1 Pacific Time and October 2 in Japan. Does the Netflix premiere date mean every episode is available? No. Netflix's announced schedule is a weekly rollout, so October 1 in Pacific Time and October 2 in Japan mark the beginning of the new season rather than a full-season release. Viewers looking for a later episode should check the local Netflix episode list instead of assuming the entire season arrived on the premiere date. What happens in Season 2? The story continues the intertwined relationships of Koyuki Hikawa, Miki Azumi, Minato Amamiya and Yota Hino. Koyuki has difficulty opening up to other people, while the more outgoing Minato disrupts the emotional walls she has built around herself. Netflix's Season 2 trailer focuses on the four friends as their feelings begin to shift and their relationships become harder to define, continuing the coming-of-age romance from the first season. Who created The Ramparts of Ice? The anime adapts Kocha Agasawa's manga. AniNextUp: Netflix release dates can display differently depending on local time zone. What Netflix’s season-two trailer adds The August announcement does more than repeat the premiere window. Netflix says the four central characters return to a story where several relationships begin to shift: Koyuki and Minato move toward feelings beyond friendship, while Yota finally tells Miki what he has carried for years. The trailer and key art present that movement as the continuation of an ensemble drama, rather than a change to a new cast or a separate adaptation. The announcement gives a direction for the season, not a complete account of how those conversations resolve. Netflix also lists the production team: MANQ directs, Hikaru Ishii is assistant director, Yasuhiro Nakanishi handles series composition and Miki Ogino designs the characters. Studio KAI produces the animation. These credits are useful when following a continuing series because viewers can distinguish confirmed staff from speculation about changes between seasons. No episode total or end date appears in the cited season-two announcement. Who voices the four central characters? Netflix's Season 2 announcement credits Anna Nagase as Koyuki Hikawa, Fuka Izumi as Miki Azumi, Shoya Chiba as Minato Amamiya and Satoshi Inomata as Yota Hino. The same announcement lists supporting characters as well, including Tsukiko Shimojima and Tsubasa Igarashi. These are the performers named in Netflix's Japanese production credits. Viewers who prefer another language should check their own Netflix audio options: the announcement does not promise the same dubbed tracks for every territory. How does the adaptation connect to the manga? The series is based on Kocha Agasawa's manga, published in Japan by Shueisha. The anime's continuing story follows the same central group as their friendships and romantic feelings become more complicated. Netflix describes the second season as an ensemble story, so each character's perspective matters alongside Koyuki and Minato's developing relationship. The official trailer and key art offer different glimpses of that group: Netflix describes the artwork as a warm classroom moment while the trailer highlights emotional distance. Neither reveals every outcome. Watching the first season gives viewers the background to understand how the characters reached this point before following the weekly continuation. Planning a weekly watch The date format is easy to misread if you compare a U.S. schedule with a Japanese broadcast listing. Netflix labels the worldwide weekly start as October 1 Pacific Time and October 2 Japan Standard Time. These are two renderings of the same launch across a date boundary, not evidence that Japan has an extra episode or a one-day delay. Subsequent availability can still appear at different local clock times depending on the service and territory. Season 2 began in October, so this page now helps readers identify the continuation and its cadence. Netflix confirms weekly episodes; it has not stated a full episode count in the release notice. The local title page is the best source for a particular account’s current episode list, audio and subtitle choices. An announcement of worldwide availability does not guarantee that every language track is offered in every market. entries.description: Ranma 1/2 Season 3 began in October 2026. Understand Japan’s late-night slot, US date conversions, Netflix’s weekly release and the official trailer.
entries.content: STREAMING GUIDE Ranma 1/2 Season 3: Netflix Schedule, Cast and Watch Guide Season 3 of the MAPPA remake began in October 2026. Check how Japan’s late-night schedule relates to the US calendar, what Netflix has confirmed and where to start watching. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official Season 3 key visual. © Rumiko Takahashi / Shogakukan / Ranma 1/2 Production Committee. Official July 25 visual reveal . WHERE TO WATCH Netflix Release at a glance Japanese premiere October 3 late-night slot: October 4, 00:55 JST Weekly Japanese TV Nippon TV, Saturdays 24:55 JST Studio MAPPA Streaming Netflix after the Japanese broadcast; check local episodes Checked October 24, 2026 · Official Season 3 schedule announcement Has Ranma 1/2 Season 3 started? Yes. Season 3 began in Japan in the October 3, 2026 late-night television slot. Nippon TV lists Saturdays at 24:55 JST, which is Sunday at 00:55 on a standard calendar; the opening broadcast therefore fell on October 4 at 00:55 JST. The July production announcement confirmed that schedule together with exclusive Netflix distribution after the Japanese broadcast. A date listed as October 3 and a Japanese clock date of October 4 can both describe the same launch. What does that mean for viewers in the US? The first Japanese television start corresponds to October 3 at 15:55 UTC: 11:55 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time or 8:55 a.m. Pacific Daylight Time. Those are conversions of the television start, not independently announced Netflix upload times. The production says Netflix follows the broadcast, so it would be misleading to promise an episode at the converted start time. US daylight-saving changes later in the season also mean a fixed Japanese slot does not always convert to the same American clock hour. Where can you watch the season? Netflix’s own MAPPA anniversary announcement identifies Season 3 as coming worldwide and exclusively to Netflix. The anime’s Japanese production notice likewise says Netflix distribution follows the television broadcast. Use your local series page for the available episodes, subtitles and dubbed tracks. The official on-air site has separate season tabs, including older-season platform lists; services carrying an earlier season should not automatically be described as carrying Season 3 at launch. Related reading: My Happy Marriage Special Episodes: Release Date & Netflix Guide . Is this a weekly release or a full-season drop? The Japanese schedule is weekly, with the Netflix release linked to that broadcast. It is not an announcement that the full season appears at once. If you are planning a catch-up session, distinguish episodes already available in your catalog from later installments still awaiting their weekly release. Local broadcasters across the Nippon TV network also join on different schedules, so their listings may be behind the first Japanese broadcast without indicating a streaming delay. What is Ranma 1/2 about? Ranma Saotome and Akane Tendo are engaged through an arrangement made by their parents, but their martial-arts romantic comedy is anything but straightforward. During training in China, Ranma fell into the cursed springs of Jusenkyo. Cold water now transforms him into a girl, while hot water returns him to a boy. That complication feeds the misunderstandings, rivalries and slapstick around the couple. Season 3 continues this remake rather than introducing an unrelated protagonist or starting the story over. What does the Season 3 trailer reveal? Netflix’s June announcement highlights Ryoga Hibiki, whose rivalry with Ranma and feelings for Akane intensify in the new run. It also points to his newly mastered Breaking Point Blow. The July key visual surrounds Ranma, Akane and Ryoga with characters appearing in Season 3. Those are useful previews of the ensemble and the coming martial-arts complications, but neither a promotional image nor a trailer proves the season’s final manga chapter or the eventual resolution of the romance. Related reading: Suikoden: The Anime — Schedule, Cast, Trailer and Game Guide . Who are the returning Japanese cast members? Kappei Yamaguchi voices Ranma, with Megumi Hayashibara voicing his female form, while Noriko Hidaka plays Akane. Koichi Yamadera returns as Ryoga, and Rei Sakuma as Shampoo. The production’s season-specific cast list also names Toshihiko Seki as Mousse and Kaori Nazuka as Ukyo Kuonji. These are Japanese cast credits. For a dubbed version, consult the credits and audio options of the episode you can actually access rather than assuming that every language track follows the same availability pattern. Which studio and staff are making it? MAPPA produces the animation, with Konosuke Uda directing, Kimiko Ueno handling series composition, Hiromi Taniguchi designing the characters and Kaoru Wada composing the music. Rumiko Takahashi’s manga is the original work, published by Shogakukan. The official staff page separates credits by season, so a list copied from the first season can miss later production changes. The roles above are supported by the Season 3 production information, rather than inferred from MAPPA’s involvement alone. Related reading: Anime Mysterious Codes (October 2026): Reports & Redemption Guide . Where should a new viewer begin? Start with Seasons 1 and 2 of the current remake before Season 3. That is the clearest route through its recurring relationships, rivalries and running jokes. Watching an older Ranma adaptation can be enjoyable background, but it is not the same viewing order as continuing this MAPPA series. When searching Netflix, match the current adaptation’s season listing instead of using an episode number from a different version as your starting point. Watch the original official trailer The trailer below is the Season 3 video from Netflix Anime. Its original YouTube metadata records June 19, 2026, at 05:55:00 UTC−07:00, equivalent to 12:55:00 UTC and 21:55:00 JST. Its duration is 1 minute 40 seconds. This upload accompanied the earlier October release-window announcement, while the more specific October 3 late-night schedule came later. Keeping those announcements separate avoids using the trailer’s publication date as the season’s premiere date. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER ON YOUTUBE Netflix Anime · Official Season 3 trailer What is still unclear from these announcements? The cited releases do not establish an exact Netflix upload minute for every territory, a uniform set of language tracks, or a final adaptation endpoint. Do not read the weekly television slot as a promise of a full-season drop or an announced manga ending. The anime’s current on-air page is the reference for Japanese station changes; the local Netflix episode list is the practical reference for what you can watch now. entries.content: OCTOBER 4 · 2026 Reborn as a Space Mercenary Anime: Release Date & Where to Watch Reborn as a Space Mercenary is scheduled in AniNextUp’s Fall 2026 calendar for October 4. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official promotional visual. Artwork source: official release announcement . WHERE TO WATCH Crunchyroll Release at a glance Release October 4, 2026 Where to watch Crunchyroll; Japanese audio and English dub launch together Region and timing Licensed territories; local catalog times vary. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Crunchyroll’s English dub announcement Why this isekai has a different appeal The familiar transported-into-another-world premise is expressed through science-fiction game systems rather than a medieval fantasy kingdom. Hiro's mercenary work, starship combat and space colonies make the series a closer fit for viewers who enjoy space adventures alongside reincarnation stories. The same-day English dub is also a practical difference for viewers who prefer dubbed premieres. When does Reborn as a Space Mercenary premiere? Reborn as a Space Mercenary: I Woke Up Piloting the Strongest Starship! premiered October 4, 2026. Crunchyroll began streaming the first episode on Sunday alongside the Japanese release, and an English dub launched the same day. Where to watch Crunchyroll carries the series in supported international territories. The announced distribution covers most of the world outside Japan, China, Korea and Mongolia, although catalog availability can still vary by location. What is the anime about? After waking in the universe of his favorite science-fiction game, Satou Takahiro takes on the identity of mercenary Hiro. Instead of a conventional fantasy isekai adventure, his new life revolves around starships, space battles, colonies and dangerous jobs across an interstellar setting. Related reading: So What's Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? Release Guide . What to check if you want to start with the dub Crunchyroll's same-day English-dub announcement establishes that an English version begins with the premiere; it does not guarantee every audio track in every country or establish the exact hour at which later dubbed episodes appear. Check the language selector and episode list in your own Crunchyroll catalog. The cast named below are the English-language performers, not the Japanese voice cast. Is there an English dub? Yes. Crunchyroll confirmed a same-day English dub beginning October 4. Kyle Phillips voices Hiro, with Kelsey Cruz as Elma, Emily Neves as Mimi and Jaclyn Thomas as Serena. What Hiro's mercenary work adds to the premise Hiro's new life revolves around starships, contracts and interstellar travel. His knowledge of the game-like setting offers a starting advantage, but the synopsis does not establish how his future missions unfold. This gives viewers a practical way to distinguish the series from fantasy adventures centered on magic and kingdoms. AniNextUp: Release timing and streaming availability can vary by region. What the October premiere confirms The October 4 date is the series’ Japanese television premiere, while the Crunchyroll listing is the practical check for international streaming in a viewer’s region. Those are related but separate schedules: a Japanese broadcast slot does not by itself establish when a licensed stream becomes available everywhere. Crunchyroll’s October 2 dub notice adds a second viewing track, but the announcement’s same-day premiere information should not be stretched into a promise that every later dubbed episode will follow the same regional hour. That distinction matters for a show whose long title can lead readers to assume “reborn” means a conventional fantasy-world reset. Hiro instead finds himself in a science-fiction setting with a capable starship and a mercenary’s choices to make. The available premise points to a working life built around contracts, equipment and travel through space. It does not make the show a simulation of real-world military procedure, and details beyond the official synopsis should be treated as interpretation. Who makes the anime? Crunchyroll's production report credits Norihiko Nagahama as director at studio A-CAT. Takamitsu Kono handles series composition, Masami Sueoka designs the characters and Kenta Higashioji composes the music. These are the announced animation credits; the English dub performers listed above are a separate group. Is there a light novel or manga? The series adapts a science-fiction light novel by Ryuto, illustrated by Tetsuhiro Nabeshima. Seven Seas Entertainment publishes the novels in English as well as Shunichi Matsui's manga adaptation, according to Crunchyroll's production report. Those editions provide another way to explore Hiro's setting, but their volume releases do not determine the anime's episode schedule. Hiro's starship and the skills he brings from the game shape his new mercenary life. The premise sets up space travel and assignments rather than a traditional medieval fantasy quest. Readers who want to avoid later plot details can start with the anime's official synopsis and check the streaming episode list as they watch. How to use the guide while the season airs For a first-time viewer, the most useful checks are the episode list and audio selector on the official streaming page. A platform may list Japanese audio, subtitles and a dub without offering every combination in every country. If an episode appears later than expected, compare the service’s local listing before assuming the Japanese TV broadcast was delayed. The series’ premiere has already taken place, so the date now serves as an anchor for catching up rather than a future appointment. The official materials establish the October launch, the streaming partner and an English dub announcement. They do not establish a final episode count, a complete season length or an identical dub schedule across territories. AniNextUp will keep those fields open until a production or distributor notice supplies them. That separation lets readers answer the immediate question—where to start watching—without confusing promotional announcements with a full season calendar.
