entries.content: NEW ANIME · OCTOBER 5, 2026 The Record of a Fallen Vampire Anime: 2027, Cast and Trailer The Record of a Fallen Vampire is officially getting a TV anime in 2027. The announcement includes a teaser PV and visual, the two lead cast members and the main production staff. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official teaser visual. © Kyo Shirodaira, Yuri Kimura / SQUARE ENIX / The Record of a Fallen Vampire Production Committee. Source: official anime project . Release at a glance Release window 2027; exact date TBA Format TV anime Studios ZERO-G and Liber Streaming / broadcaster Not announced in reviewed materials Checked October 24, 2026 · Original production announcement When will The Record of a Fallen Vampire premiere? The Record of a Fallen Vampire is scheduled to become a television anime in 2027. The October 5 announcement confirms the year, but not a season, month, date or weekly broadcast slot. A teaser and named production team give the project more substance than an adaptation announcement alone, yet neither establishes when episodes will arrive. As of October 24, a specific premiere date would go beyond the official information reviewed for this guide. Where can you watch the anime? No international streaming partner or territory list is named in the official teaser description. That means there is no confirmed Netflix, Crunchyroll or HIDIVE release to put on a viewing calendar yet. Pony Canyon publishes the promotional video, while ZERO-G and Liber handle animation production; those roles do not themselves identify the service that will distribute episodes in your country. Look for an explicit licensing or streaming announcement before treating a platform listing as settled. What is the story about? The central figure is Rose Red Strauss, the vampire king associated with the destruction of the Kingdom of Night a thousand years earlier. He is trying to recover his beloved queen, Adelheid, who has been sealed away. The official introduction places him in conflict with dhampirs hunting his life and the Black Swan, a powerful enemy. It also promises the gradual revelation of what happened a millennium ago, so the mystery of the past matters alongside the present-day battles. Who is the Black Swan? VIZ’s first-volume description explains the threat in more detail: the Black Swan inhabits a young human girl every 50 years and gives her the power to destroy the vampire king and queen. Each incarnation grows stronger. That premise creates a repeating danger across Strauss’s long search, rather than a single opponent he can simply outlive. Readers who want to avoid later manga revelations should stay with the first-volume synopsis; descriptions of subsequent books expose major changes in alliances and motivation. Why do some listings call Strauss Akabara? The Japanese anime credits identify the lead as Rose Red Strauss, voiced by Yuma Uchida. VIZ’s English manga listing uses Akabara in its synopsis. These are naming differences around the same central vampire king, not evidence of two protagonists or separate adaptations. For searches, the Japanese title Vampire Juujikai and the English title The Record of a Fallen Vampire lead to the same manga property by Kyo Shirodaira and Yuri Kimura. Who are the confirmed voice actors? Yuma Uchida plays Strauss, while Aino Shimada voices Bridget Irving Frostheart. The official teaser lists these two lead performers. Their presence should not be presented as a complete cast list: the queen and other characters mentioned in the premise do not gain confirmed voice actors merely because they are part of the story. Additional casting, dubbed-language performances and international audio options remain separate announcements to watch for. Which studios and staff are making it? Mankyu is responsible for directing and series composition. Animation production is credited jointly to ZERO-G and Liber, with character design by jimao and music by Evan Call. These are the roles listed in the original official video. The credits establish who is attached, but do not explain how the two studios divide individual episodes or production tasks. Call’s music credit also does not announce an opening singer, ending theme or soundtrack release date. Watch the official teaser The teaser is published by Pony Canyon, with ABC Animation Channel shown as a collaborating channel on YouTube. Original upload metadata records October 5, 2026, at 02:00:01 UTC−07:00, equivalent to 09:00:01 UTC and 18:00:01 JST. The metadata duration is 48 seconds. This timestamp describes the promotional upload, not an episode premiere. The title and description confirm television broadcast in 2027; they do not narrow the release to a particular anime season. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER ON YOUTUBE Pony Canyon · Official teaser Should you read the manga first? The source manga credits Kyo Shirodaira for the story and Yuri Kimura for the art. The official anime video identifies the original Square Enix edition as nine volumes. English readers can start with VIZ’s Volume 1 listing, which supplies the premise, creator credits and a Teen age rating. That label belongs to the manga edition, not an announced television classification. Starting at Volume 1 preserves the story’s gradual introduction of Strauss and the mystery surrounding his past. Is the original manga complete? Yes. VIZ’s series catalog identifies Volume 9 as the final volume, matching the nine-volume count in the official anime announcement. That gives prospective readers a bounded reading commitment rather than an unfinished monthly story to catch up with. You can read the original manga in volume order while waiting for the anime, although later book descriptions disclose twists that the first-volume premise keeps hidden. Completion of the source manga does not tell us how quickly the television adaptation will cover that material. What does the anime announcement leave open? The production has not stated an episode count or identified an adaptation endpoint in the reviewed materials. Nine manga volumes do not automatically imply nine episodes, a complete adaptation or multiple seasons. No broadcast hour exists to convert into a local viewing time yet. For the next meaningful update, follow the official anime site and social account, then check any future distribution notice for territories and language details. Those facts will determine when and how viewers can actually watch. entries.content: RELEASE UPDATE · OCTOBER 5, 2026 Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story Premieres January 2027 on Crunchyroll Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story now has a January 2027 premiere window, a new key visual and full PV, six additional voice announcements, and confirmed Crunchyroll streaming worldwide outside Asia. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases RELEASE WINDOW JANUARY 2027 · CRUNCHYROLL Release at a glance Release January 2027; exact day unannounced Where to watch Crunchyroll worldwide excluding Asia Region and timing Japan: TOKYO MX, BS Nippon TV and Yomiuri TV; local episode hours unannounced. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story official site · Crunchyroll’s trailer and January 2027 release announcement What the January window establishes January 2027 is a confirmed broadcast month, not an episode-by-episode timetable. Crunchyroll's announced rights outside Asia also leave Asian distribution as a separate question. Viewers should therefore distinguish the Japanese broadcaster list from the international streaming territories instead of assuming that one announcement covers every market. When does Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story release? The TV anime will begin broadcasting in January 2027 on TOKYO MX, BS NTV and Yomiuri TV in Japan. An exact premiere day has not been announced yet. Where can you watch it? Crunchyroll has confirmed it will stream the anime worldwide excluding Asia when the series premieres in January 2027. New cast announced The newly announced cast includes Takuya Sato as Jill, Atsushi Tamaru as Antonio, Motoko Kumai as Rodrigo, Kotaro Nishiyama as Paolo, Sakiko Uran as Thumbelina and Ryoko Shiraishi as narrator. They join Yume Miyamoto as Red Riding Hood and Akira Sekine as Pinocchio. Related reading: The Detective Is Already Dead Season 2: Release Date, Episodes & Where to Watch . Studio and staff Itsuro Kawasaki directs and writes the anime at BENTEN Film . Manami Minakata and Yuko Yahiro handle character designs, while Jun Ichikawa composes the music. What is the anime about? The series turns familiar fairy-tale settings into mystery cases. Red Riding Hood travels through the storybook world and repeatedly finds herself caught up in incidents, using her curiosity and sharp reasoning to solve each mystery. What the October announcement means for viewers The production now has a January 2027 Japanese broadcast window, a fuller cast and confirmed Crunchyroll distribution outside Asia. The exact first-airing day and streaming arrangements within Asia remain separate unanswered questions; the new promotional video does not establish either. Related reading: ONE PIECE: Elbaph Arc English Dub Release Date and Crunchyroll Schedule . Why the fairy-tale detective premise stands out Red Riding Hood's role is different from that of a conventional fairy-tale protagonist: the announced premise puts her in the position of investigating incidents rather than simply escaping a familiar danger. For viewers, that changes the central question from “what happens in the original tale?” to “how will this mystery be solved?” This is AniNextUp's interpretation of the synopsis, not a claim about the structure of any unshown episode. How to read the streaming announcement by region The January 2027 broadcast window and Crunchyroll's announced distribution rights answer two separate questions. Japanese broadcaster names identify domestic television outlets; “worldwide excluding Asia” describes Crunchyroll's stated streaming territory. Neither statement establishes which platform will carry the show within Asia. If you live in an excluded territory, wait for a separate local distributor announcement rather than assuming that the Japanese broadcast or Crunchyroll listing applies to you. What to check when the first episode gets a date A specific premiere day, a local streaming time and available subtitle or dub languages are distinct details. Once a dated schedule appears, readers should check the official anime site for Japanese broadcast information and their regional platform listing for actual access. The confirmed January window alone cannot be used to calculate a reliable episode countdown. Related reading: SSS-Class Revival Hunter Anime: January 2027 Premiere, New Trailer, Cast and Crunchyroll . Editorial distinction: The viewing guidance above is original AniNextUp analysis based on the announced premise and distribution scope. It does not introduce additional cast, plot details, release dates or streaming licenses. What is the anime based on? The television series adapts Aito Aoyagi's Japanese mystery novels, published by Futabasha. Crunchyroll reports that the original series began publication in August 2020 and had four volumes in Japan when the October anime announcement appeared. The Japanese title is Akazukin, Tabi no Tochuu de Shitai to Deau ; the announced English title is Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story . The source combines recognizable fairy-tale settings with detective fiction. According to the anime's official introduction, Red Riding Hood encounters cases during her journey and uses her curiosity and intelligence to solve them. Familiar names offer a starting point, but the anime's own version of each encounter should be judged as its episodes are released. Related reading: The Fledgling Demon Lord's Starter Shop Anime Premieres January 2027 . What did the main trailer announcement include? The October update paired a main promotional video and key visual with the January broadcast window and six additional voice credits. The official video is available below. It introduces the adaptation ahead of broadcast, while the cast list provides the Japanese performers associated with the characters announced so far. Yume Miyamoto voices the traveling Red Riding Hood and Akira Sekine voices Pinocchio. The newly named roles expand that lineup to Jill, Antonio, Rodrigo, Paolo and Thumbelina, as well as the narrator. These are Japanese voice credits; the announcement does not establish an English-dub cast or a dub release date. Will every episode arrive on the same day? The announcement identifies the month and broadcasters, but does not give a complete episode count or release timetable. A January start alone cannot confirm a weekly cadence or a full-season drop. Check the official broadcast schedule and your local Crunchyroll listing when the first episode is dated. Watch the official PV ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER YouTube · click to play AniNextUp status: January 2027 and Crunchyroll are confirmed. Exact premiere day remains TBA. What returning viewers need to know The official series description centers on Fran and her sentient sword companion, whose partnership began when the sword was reborn in another world and chose to help a young girl seeking justice. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official anime visual. © Nazuna Miki, Tsukasa Araki / Shueisha / Tengobu Production Committee. Official anime site . RELEASE DATE October 5, 2026 STREAMING Crunchyroll STUDIO BAKKKA Release at a glance Japanese premiere October 5, 2026 · TOKYO MX, Mondays 22:00 JST Studio BAKKKA Japan’s advance streaming ABEMA / Prime Video; one week ahead from Episode 2 International streaming Crunchyroll; check local availability Checked October 24, 2026 · Official schedule Has Reincarnated Goblin already premiered? Yes. So What’s Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? began its Japanese television run on October 5, 2026. The first TOKYO MX slot is Monday at 22:00 JST, equivalent to 13:00 UTC. The title also appears in Crunchyroll’s Fall 2026 lineup. This guide separates Japan’s broadcast schedule from platform availability, because an episode being scheduled on Japanese TV does not establish its availability in every country or on every subscription service. Japan’s weekly television schedule TOKYO MX lists Mondays at 22:00 JST. BS11 lists Monday at 24:00, and Sun TV Monday at 24:30; on a standard calendar those late-night slots fall on Tuesday at 00:00 and 00:30 JST. AT-X began on October 7 with a Wednesday 20:00 JST slot. These are different broadcasts of the same series, not four release dates for distinct editions. Use the broadcaster you actually receive when setting a reminder. Why are some Japanese services an episode ahead? The official on-air page gives ABEMA and Prime Video a one-week lead over terrestrial television from Episode 2. The opening release on October 5 at 22:00 JST included Episode 1 alongside Episode 2: the first episode was simultaneous with TV, while the second began the advance schedule. Other Japanese services started distributing after the television broadcast. This explains why Japanese platform listings can show different episode numbers on the same day without either schedule necessarily being wrong. Related reading: Reborn as a Space Mercenary Anime: Release Date & Where to Watch . Where should international viewers check? Crunchyroll’s announced lineup includes the series, but its local title page is the practical place to check current episodes, subtitles and audio tracks. Japan’s official streaming list also names services such as Hulu, U-NEXT and d Anime Store. Those domestic listings should not be turned into worldwide licensing claims. In particular, the Japanese Prime Video advance arrangement is not evidence that every international Prime Video catalog receives episodes a week early. What is the story about? Akira Yagami is an office worker trusted by his colleagues who dies while saving a child from traffic. He wakes in another world as a goblin, a species whose normal lifespan is only seven days. His unusual ability, called Octogenarian in the anime site’s English introduction, gives him a much longer life. As goblins around him die, he inherits their skills. Demons, elves and dragons eventually become part of the wider circle gathering around him. Related reading: Cosmoship Yamato √2199 Release Date: Story, Cast and What’s Confirmed . What makes Akira’s skill different? The contrast between a seven-day goblin lifespan and Akira’s eighty years is the premise’s central advantage. It gives him time to accumulate abilities that short-lived goblins cannot develop in the same way. That makes the setting more specific than a generic reincarnated office worker gaining strength: his growth is tied to the passing of others in his community. This is a reading of the published setup, rather than a claim about how any particular later battle ends. Who are the cast and staff? Kikunosuke Toya voices Akira, Yoko Hikasa plays Karen, and Azusa Tachibana plays Chloe. The Japanese cast also includes Banjo Ginga as Simon, Sayumi Suzushiro as Eirene, M・A・O as Dike and Wakana Kuramochi as Eunomia. Ryuta Kawahara directs the anime at BAKKKA, with series composition and scripts by Yuichiro Momose, character design by Hiroyuki Saida and music by Takenoko Shonen. These credits describe the Japanese production; dubbed-language casting is a separate matter. Related reading: New Anime on Netflix in October 2026: What to Watch . What are the opening and ending songs? Sou performs the opening theme, Hello, while the ending is Chiisana Bokura by AHUB, known in Japanese as Eihabu. The production’s September announcement names both songs, and the main PV previews the opening. Their presence in promotional material helps identify the correct anime trailer when searching the long English title. A theme-song announcement should not be mistaken for an episode soundtrack release or a guarantee that a streaming service carries separate music videos. Watch the official main PV The main promotional video linked from the producer’s September 9 press release is on the Showgate channel. Its original YouTube metadata records September 9, 2026, at 03:00:17 UTC−07:00, equivalent to 10:00:17 UTC and 19:00:17 JST. The metadata duration is 1 minute 38 seconds. This is the upload timestamp of the trailer, not the October premiere. Use the original video below to distinguish it from reposts and older teaser uploads. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER ON YOUTUBE Showgate · Official main PV Where can you read the manga? The manga is written by Nazuna Miki and illustrated by Tsukasa Araki. Shueisha publishes it in Japan through Tonari no Young Jump, while Yen Press publishes the English edition. Yen Press’s Volume 1 listing is a useful starting point if you want the source story without jumping into later plot developments. It credits Caleb Cook as translator and labels the book Teen. That is the manga edition’s rating, not an independently announced age classification for the anime. What remains unconfirmed in this guide? The reviewed release notices do not identify how many manga chapters the anime will adapt or where its season will end. Do not choose a manga starting chapter based on an assumed final episode: begin with Volume 1 for the original version, or wait for the adaptation’s coverage to be clear. For weekly viewing, follow the appropriate local service’s episode list. For Japanese broadcast changes, the anime’s on-air page and the receiving broadcaster are the relevant references. Sources checked October 24: official on-air page ; BS11 schedule ; official introduction ; cast and staff ; producer’s September 9 release ; Yen Press Volume 1 ; Crunchyroll lineup . entries.content: FALL 2026 · RELEASE GUIDE A Returner's Magic Should Be Special Season 2 Season 2 premiered in Japan on October 7, 2026, and streams on Crunchyroll with a same-day English dub. Here are the verified broadcast times, regional streaming details, story setup and official trailer notes. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official Season 2 main visual. Source: Aniplex . RELEASE DATE October 7, 2026 STREAMING Crunchyroll Release at a glance Japan premiere October 7, 2026 · Fuji TV +Ultra at 24:45 JST International streaming Crunchyroll simulcast; territory exclusions apply English dub Same-day launch on October 7 Details checked October 25, 2026 · Aniplex's Japan schedule · Crunchyroll's Fall lineup As of October 25, 2026, A Returner's Magic Should Be Special Season 2 is airing: its first episode premiered on October 7. If you are catching up, the useful distinction is between the Japanese television slot, which is listed using late-night 24-hour notation, and Crunchyroll's international simulcast time. The dates can appear to differ by a day even when they describe the same weekly episode. When did Season 2 premiere in Japan? When did Season 2 premiere in Japan? Aniplex's official broadcast and streaming notice lists Fuji TV's +Ultra block from Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 24:45 JST. In ordinary clock notation, 24:45 on Wednesday is 12:45 a.m. on Thursday, October 8. Japanese television schedules commonly keep a late-night program attached to the preceding evening's lineup; calendar apps that do not use hours beyond 23:59 may therefore display October 8. The official listing also gives Kansai TV's Thursday 26:15 slot, with the first episode at 26:25, Tokai TV's Saturday 26:00 slot, and AT-X's Saturday 9:30 p.m. slot. These are separate Japanese broadcasts, not separate premiere dates. Where can you stream the new episodes? Crunchyroll carries Season 2 as part of its Fall 2026 simulcast lineup. Its schedule lists the subtitled release on Wednesdays at 10:15 a.m. Pacific Time. That is a platform release time for the listed territories, not the Fuji TV broadcast time; the two schedules use different time zones and distribution windows. Crunchyroll describes its availability as worldwide except Japan, China, Korea and Mongolia. Catalog rights can vary, so viewers should confirm the show page in their own country before subscribing or planning a watch party. Where can you stream the new episodes? Japan also has a separate set of streaming options. Aniplex lists d Anime Store , d Anime Store Nico Nico Branch, d Anime Store for Prime Video, d Anime Store for LINE Manga, U-NEXT and Anime Hodai from October 7 at 25:15 JST. That converts to 1:15 a.m. on Thursday, October 8. A broader group of Japanese services, including FOD, ABEMA, Hulu, Lemino and Prime Video, is listed from October 11 at noon JST. Those domestic listings should not be mistaken for worldwide platform availability. Related reading: Magic Knight Rayearth 2026: Official Creditless Ending, Hoshiakari & Streaming . Does the English dub release at the same time? Crunchyroll announced the English dub for the same day as the Japanese-language premiere: Wednesday, October 7. Its Fall lineup lists the dub airtime alongside the subtitled Wednesday 10:15 a.m. PT slot. The same-day announcement means viewers did not have to wait for a later dub launch, though an episode may appear at a different local clock time after conversion. Crunchyroll announced Austin Tindle as Desir, Sarah Roach as Romantica, Macy Anne Johnson as Pram, and Anastasia Muñoz as Azest in its cast-and-crew notice. Check the platform listing for the audio options available in your region. What is the Season 2 story about? The official synopsis continues Desir Herrman's second chance after humanity's defeat by the Shadow Worlds. Sent thirteen years into the past, he is reliving academy life and gathering three allies: wind mage Romantica Eru, swordsman Pram Schnaizer and ice magic knight Azest Kingscrown. Their task is to confront a Shadow World that has appeared again and correct the history behind it. The season's new setup adds Desir's nightmare of Romantica's death and identifies the Devil of Destruction as the figure connected to that fear. This gives returning viewers a clear new conflict without revealing how the group resolves it. Does the English dub release at the same time? Who is making the second season? Aniplex lists Taishi Kawaguchi as director, Takamitsu Kono for series composition and scripts, Hiromi Kato for character design, and Kenta Higashiohji for music. Arvo Animation is the animation studio, produced by HAYATE. The principal Japanese cast returns: Takuma Terashima voices Desir, Sayumi Suzushiro voices Romantica, Natsumi Fujiwara voices Pram, and Asami Seto voices Azest. These credits make it easier to distinguish confirmed production details from fan speculation about staff changes. Related reading: My Happy Marriage Special Episodes: Release Date & Netflix Guide . What is the Season 2 story about? The opening theme is “Sorrow,” performed by FLOW. The official September 15 PV announcement says the video introduced the song's audio and revealed the new main visual, which places the returning party alongside new opponents. Crunchyroll's Official Trailer 2 was published on September 9, 2026. The official YouTube listing provides that date, but the accessible official source does not show the original upload time or timezone. AniNextUp therefore does not claim an exact trailer timestamp or add a VideoObject uploadDate. The trailer remains available above, and the date-only limitation is stated rather than filled with a guess. For new viewers, the simplest entry point is Season 1, which establishes the Shadow Worlds, the Shadow Labyrinth and the original timeline before Desir returns to the academy. Season 2 is a direct continuation, not a reboot or a stand-alone story. Viewers who only need the essentials can remember that Desir has already seen the world's collapse, has reunited with Romantica, Pram and Azest, and is trying to change the outcome. The official synopsis does not require readers to know the source web novel to follow the anime's stated setup. Who is making the second season? The confirmed guide details are the October 7 Japanese premiere, Fuji TV's Wednesday 24:45 broadcast slot, Crunchyroll's Wednesday simulcast and same-day English dub, the named core staff and cast, and FLOW's opening song. Aniplex and Fuji TV publish the Japanese schedule; Crunchyroll provides the simulcast, territory and dub information. The exact international episode timing can change by territory, while a second-cour order, total episode count, and a date for the season finale are not stated in the official notices reviewed for this update. Updated: October 25, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error Official trailer Crunchyroll's verified YouTube channel lists Trailer 2 as published September 9, 2026. Its official listing does not expose the original upload time or timezone, so AniNextUp does not assert a precise timestamp or mark up an unsupported VideoObject. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Crunchyroll Official references: Fuji TV broadcast schedule and Crunchyroll regions .

entries.content: FALL 2026 · RELEASE GUIDE Romelia War Chronicle: Release Date, Story & Where to Watch Romelia War Chronicle began streaming in Japan on October 3, 2026, at 9:00 p.m. JST, with Japanese television broadcasts starting October 5. International streaming began October 3; exact availability varies by region. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official anime visual. Source: Romelia War Chronicle official website . Release at a glance JAPAN STREAMING Oct 3 · 9:00 p.m. JST JAPAN TV From Oct 5 · weekly INTERNATIONAL Crunchyroll · from Oct 3 Release date, streaming start and Japanese TV schedule Romelia War Chronicle began streaming in Japan on October 3, 2026, at 9:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time (JST). The official schedule lists Anime Times, U-NEXT and Netflix for that advance streaming launch. Japanese television followed on October 5, when TOKYO MX, BS11, Sun Television and KBS Kyoto began their broadcasts. CBC joined on October 10. These are separate release routes for the same TV anime, not different premieres. The official schedule describes the television run as two cours. It lists TOKYO MX, BS11 and Sun Television on Mondays at 11:30 p.m. JST, KBS Kyoto on Mondays at midnight, and CBC on Saturdays at 2:43 a.m. in the broadcaster's extended schedule notation. CBC's first episode was listed for 2:58 a.m. Sunday, October 11, by ordinary calendar time. Japanese listings can show late-night hours above 24:00; check a local electronic program guide if the displayed day matters. The anime's official site warns that broadcast and streaming times may change. Where can viewers outside Japan watch? The production's official schedule lists Crunchyroll for international streaming from October 3, excluding Japan, mainland China and South Korea. For South Korea, it lists Tooniverse from the same date. The site does not give a universal release hour for those services, so the Japanese 9:00 p.m. start should not be copied as a global Crunchyroll time. Catalogues, subtitle availability and episode timing can vary by country; viewers should use the schedule shown by the service in their region. Related reading: Tokyo Revengers: War of the Three Titans Release Schedule & Where to Watch . That distinction answers a common release-date question: October 3 is the announced Japan streaming date and the international streaming start date, but only the Japanese services have a precise 9:00 p.m. JST time on the official schedule. October 5 is the Japanese television start. A calendar entry saying “October 3” alone does not mean every territory received the episode at the same moment. What is the story about? The official introduction opens after Romelia and Prince Henri return from defeating the Demon King Zelgis. Henri ends his engagement to Romelia, while the celebrations around the victory overlook the damage left in her homeland. The country is still scarred by war, and people have lost homes and livelihoods during the conflict with the demons. Romelia chooses to return and address the problems that remain instead of treating the Demon King's defeat as a complete resolution. Her stated approach includes organizing an army, restarting economic activity and navigating conspiracies. The official synopsis also warns that her decisions will bring the threat of another war. This makes “what happens after the Demon King is defeated?” a useful way to understand the premise: the story shifts from winning a quest to rebuilding the institutions and everyday life that war has disrupted. The anime's official material establishes those goals, but it does not promise that every plan succeeds or explain the later political outcomes. Related reading: Akane-banashi Season 2 Release Date: January 2027 and Story . The broken engagement redirects Romelia's path, but the official premise gives similar weight to military preparation and reconstruction. That distinguishes the setup from a story focused only on courtship: it asks how a country might recover and how political conspiracies could complicate that work. How many episodes or cours are confirmed? The official Japanese broadcast page says the series will air for two cours. That confirms a longer run than a single cour, but the schedule page does not state an episode count, finale date, or whether a break separates the cours. Those details should not be inferred from the phrase alone. The same page gives weekly Japanese broadcast slots, which indicate the planned cadence, while a distributor's regional episode list remains the best source for local streaming dates. Related reading: Cosmoship Yamato √2199 Release Date: Story, Cast and What’s Confirmed . Who made the anime, and who is in the cast? Atra is the animation studio. Koji Saito is series director, Takahiro Hirata assistant director, and Aya Satsuki is credited with series composition and scripts. Yoshiko Saito and Yuta Otaka design the characters, while KOHTA YAMAMOTO composes the score. The opening theme is “Akatsuki ni Naru” by Chogakusei; the ending is “Nightfall feat. Maika Loubté” by KOHTA YAMAMOTO. Yuna Nemoto voices Romelia, Jin Ogasawara plays Al, Tomohiro Ono plays Ray, and Yuya Hirose plays Henri. The official cast page also lists additional characters including Elisabeth, Ekaterina, Ryoki and Gran. These credits help viewers distinguish confirmed production information from details that remain unannounced, such as later guest roles or episode-specific performers. Is the anime based on a light novel or manga? The official staff page credits the original work to Ryō Ariyama and identifies the source novel as a Gagaga Books publication from Shogakukan. It separately credits Ryo Ueto's manga adaptation, published in Mag Garden's BLADE Comics line. The anime therefore has both a credited novel source and a manga adaptation; the official credits do not say that the TV series adapts only the manga. Viewers who want to explore the story in print can use those publisher names to identify the relevant editions, while checking local book retailers for language and availability. Related reading: Dandivine Release Date & Where to Watch: Japan Schedule, Cast and Story . What is still unconfirmed? The official schedule supplies the Japanese start time, networks and weekly slots, but it does not give one release hour for every international platform. It also does not publish an episode total or a final broadcast date on that schedule. The official Movie page lists a second promotional video, a first PV and a teaser. Its linked original video page did not provide an accessible exact upload time and timezone during this review, so AniNextUp does not assign a precise trailer timestamp or add a VideoObject date. Use the production's official video page for the videos themselves. See the Fall 2026 anime calendar for other confirmed series and release dates. Updated: October 25, 2026 · Sources, updates & corrections · Report an error Official sources Official broadcast and streaming schedule · Official trailers · Staff, cast and source credits · Story introduction The official Movie page lists a second PV, first PV and teaser. Exact upload time and timezone were unavailable from the accessible original video page, so this guide does not publish a trailer timestamp or VideoObject date.

entries.title: Sakamoto Days Season 2 Release Date, Netflix, Trailer & Cast
entries.description: SAKAMOTO DAYS Season 2 returns in January 2027 on Netflix. Get the confirmed release window, official character trailer, story details and new cast characters.
entries.content: NETFLIX ANIME · JANUARY 2027 Sakamoto Days Season 2 Release Date, Netflix, Trailer & Cast SAKAMOTO DAYS is coming back in January 2027. Netflix has confirmed the streaming service and released a new character trailer, but the exact premiere day has not been announced. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Image: official Season 2 character trailer thumbnail from Netflix . Release at a glance Premiere window January 2027 Exact date Not announced Where to watch Netflix Season 2 trailer Official character trailer Episode count Not announced Release details checked October 16, 2026 · Netflix announcement · Netflix Tudum update PREMIERE January 2027 STREAMING Netflix NEW UPDATE Official character trailer When does Sakamoto Days Season 2 come out? SAKAMOTO DAYS Season 2 premieres in January 2027. Netflix has announced the month, but it has not confirmed a specific day or release hour. Until the service or the anime’s production committee posts a dated schedule, January is the most precise confirmed window. The second season will stream on Netflix. The announcement does not give a separate release schedule for other services, so this guide will be updated if additional platforms or territory-specific dates are confirmed. What does the new trailer reveal? The official character trailer introduces three faces expected to matter in the next chapter: Etsuko Satoda, Sakamoto’s former teacher at JCC; Amane Yotsumura, a student at the assassin training institution; and Satoru Yatsumura, whose history is tied to Sakamoto. Netflix’s October update also revisits the season’s central setup: Sakamoto and Shin go undercover at JCC while members of ORDER face a dangerous assignment in Kyoto. Related reading: Bass X Machina: Official Full Trailer, Netflix Release Date & Cast . The trailer gives viewers a first look at those characters and the series’ mix of undercover comedy and assassin action. It does not establish an episode count, a weekly-versus-binge release pattern, or a full international schedule. Watch the official Season 2 character trailer ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Netflix Anime · YouTube The video is hosted by Netflix’s verified YouTube channel. Playback loads only after you press play. What is Season 2 about? The story follows Sakamoto and Shin as they enter JCC, Japan’s assassin training institution, to investigate the elusive figure known as X, or Slur. At the same time, ORDER members Nagumo, Shishiba, and Osaragi travel to Kyoto for an assignment that turns into an ambush. Netflix’s synopsis says the season will also bring the shared past of Sakamoto, Nagumo, Rion, and Slur into focus. That setup gives the sequel two connected threads: Sakamoto’s undercover work at the school and a wider conflict involving the assassin organization. The official materials point to those story elements without confirming how many manga chapters the season will adapt. Who is in the Sakamoto Days Season 2 cast? Netflix’s current Season 2 updates identify the returning characters Natsuki Seba and Akira Akao, alongside new characters Etsuko Satoda, Amane Yotsumura, and Satoru Yatsumura. The latest Netflix announcement does not provide voice-actor credits for every new character, so we are keeping the character list separate from unconfirmed casting details. Netflix previously listed the Season 1 Japanese leads as Tomokazu Sugita (Taro Sakamoto), Nobunaga Shimazaki (Shin Asakura), Ayane Sakura (Lu Shaotang), Nao Tōyama (Aoi Sakamoto), and Hina Kino (Hana Sakamoto). Those are Season 1 credits; AniNextUp will update this section when Netflix confirms the Season 2 voice cast. Where can you watch Season 1? Netflix lists both parts of Season 1 on its service. Catching up before January is the clearest way to follow Sakamoto’s move from retired hitman to shop owner whose old world keeps pulling him back in. Who is making Sakamoto Days Season 2? TMS Entertainment is producing the new season. Netflix credits Daisuke Nakajima as director and Masaki Watanabe as supervisor, with Taku Kishimoto handling series composition. Yo Moriyama is responsible for character design, and Yuki Hayashi is composing the music. These are the production credits announced for Season 2, rather than a prediction about how individual episodes will be staffed. For viewers who enjoyed the contrast between ordinary family life and high-stakes fights in the first season, the premise of the sequel keeps both sides of that world in view. The JCC investigation sends Sakamoto back into an institution connected to his past, while the Kyoto assignment shifts attention to the professional assassins of ORDER. What should you remember before watching? Taro Sakamoto has left his former life as a feared assassin behind and now runs a neighborhood store with his family. Shin, a young man who can read minds, becomes an important ally as threats from Sakamoto’s past return. Season 1 establishes their partnership and the wider network of assassins that makes a quiet retirement difficult. The upcoming investigation also centers on X, known as Slur, whose connection to Sakamoto and his former associates is central to the new season’s setup. Nagumo, Shishiba, and Osaragi belong to ORDER, so their Kyoto mission offers another perspective on the conflict. If these names sound unfamiliar, watching both parts of Season 1 on Netflix is a useful starting point before the sequel arrives. Is there an exact release date or episode schedule? January 2027 is a confirmed month, not a specific premiere date. Netflix has not announced the total episode count or whether episodes will arrive weekly for this season. A previous release pattern should not be treated as a guarantee: check the official Netflix listing for your region as the premiere approaches, particularly if you want to plan around a local release time. What has not been confirmed yet? Netflix has confirmed a January 2027 return and its streaming platform. The exact premiere day, release hour, number of episodes, weekly release pattern, and a complete Season 2 voice cast announcement remain unconfirmed in the official sources linked here. We will revise the guide when those details are published. entries.description: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 has released creditless opening and ending videos, featuring MADKID's Unbroken and nonfic!'s Sukipi no Okage!.
entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · 2026-10-09 Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Anime Shares Creditless Opening and Ending Videos Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 has released creditless opening and ending videos, featuring MADKID's Unbroken and nonfic!'s Sukipi no Okage!. By AniNextUp Editorial Team Release at a glance Release Season 2 began October 7, 2026 in Japan Confirmed songs Opening: MADKID’s Unbroken; ending: nonfic!’s Sukipi no Okage! Region and timing The production music pages confirm the songs. Physical record release dates differ from the anime premiere. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Sasaki and Peeps official broadcast schedule · Sasaki and Peeps official opening theme credits · Sasaki and Peeps official ending theme credits Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 shares its creditless themes Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 has released creditless versions of its opening and ending animation. Crunchyroll reported the clips on October 9, 2026, following the season's Japanese television debut. The opening features MADKID's “Unbroken,” while the ending uses “Sukipi no Okage!” by nonfic! Both credits can be checked against the anime's official music page . For viewers following the new season, the clips offer a convenient way to revisit its theme sequences separately from the episodes. A creditless release removes the production names normally overlaid on the animation. It does not mean the animation has no credited creators, and it should not be confused with a newly announced episode or an extended edition of the television series. Where to find the opening and ending videos The two sequences are presented in Crunchyroll's October 9 announcement . Use the opening and ending sections there to locate the corresponding players. This article links to that announcement rather than inserting a video address that has not been checked against the release. Expect a television theme sequence rather than a full episode. These clips are best approached after starting Season 2 if you prefer discovering characters and situations through the story itself. Opening and ending animation can reveal imagery that a viewer would rather encounter in context, even when the accompanying news announcement contains no plot summary. Related reading: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Release Date: October 7 & Where to Watch . MADKID returns with “Unbroken” The official opening-theme page identifies “Unbroken” as the Season 2 opening and lists it on MADKID's thirteenth single, “Unbroken / Bonbaraman,” with an October 14, 2026 release date. That date has already passed as of this article's October 26 source check; it is a music-product date, not a second premiere for the anime. The same page includes a comment from MADKID member LIN. In paraphrase, he says the lyrics were written with Sasaki and Peeps' thoughts, choices and changing emotions in mind, and describes working with Q-MHz on the song. This provides an attributable explanation of the track's connection to the protagonists, rather than asking listeners to treat a fan interpretation as an official statement. MADKID also performed the first season's opening, “FLY,” according to the series' music index. The new title therefore marks a change of song while retaining the opening artist. When searching music services or video platforms, including both “Unbroken” and “MADKID” helps distinguish the Season 2 theme from the earlier opening. Related reading: Magic Knight Rayearth 2026: Official Creditless Ending, Hoshiakari & Streaming . nonfic! performs “Sukipi no Okage!” The ending's Japanese title is すきぴのおかげ！ , and its artist is のんふぃく！ , rendered here as nonfic! The official ending-theme page is the clearest reference when English reports display an unfamiliar spelling or a broken character in the group's name. That page lists a December 8, 2026 music release and describes a planned six-track product with multiple editions. In the accompanying artist comment, the group presents the theme as a bright, positive pop song about affection. Those details concern the announced release; they do not establish that every track or edition is already available internationally. The three dates serve different purposes: October 7 is the Japanese television launch, October 14 is the opening single's listed release, and December 8 is the ending product's announced date. Hearing a song in an episode before its physical release is not a contradiction. The creditless clip, commercial recording and television broadcast are separate ways of encountering the music. Related reading: Paw & Palaces Releases Creditless Ending Video Featuring “Chill Choose!” . When Season 2 began and where to check streaming The official broadcast schedule lists an October 7, 2026 launch with a one-hour premiere. AT-X and TOKYO MX began that Wednesday, while BS Nippon TV's opening broadcast followed on October 8. These are Japanese broadcast dates, so they should not be read as a single worldwide streaming time. For Japan, the schedule also lists Prime Video from October 7 and a later rollout to additional services from October 12. Crunchyroll's announcement identifies the season as part of its fall simulcast lineup. Check the show's listing in your own region for available episodes, subtitles and audio options; a Japanese platform schedule alone cannot establish those details for another country. For the broader release overview, see our Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 guide . The anime release calendar provides a separate route to other seasonal releases. Related reading: One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2: January 2027 Release, New Trailer and JAM Project Opening . The series behind the music The official introduction follows an office worker whose pet bird is a sage from another world. Peeps gives Sasaki access to magic and travel between worlds, while supernatural encounters also complicate his life in modern Japan. The Season 2 staff credits name Yushi Ibe as director, Yamato Ouchi as assistant director, Deko Akao for series composition and Saori Nakashiki for character design, with animation by SILVER LINK. The adaptation credits Buncololi's original work and Kantoku's original character designs. These production details place the theme release within the continuing adaptation without implying another season has been announced. Sources checked October 26, 2026: official music, broadcast, introduction and staff pages, plus Crunchyroll's creditless-video announcement. entries.content: FALL 2026 · SEASON 2 Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Release Date: October 7 & Where to Watch Season 2 began in Japan on October 7, 2026. Here are the confirmed TV and streaming schedules, the difference between Japan and international availability, and the story and staff details. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Season 2 key visual. Source: official anime website . Release at a glance Japan premiere October 7, 2026 · first broadcast is a one-hour special Japan streaming Prime Video · Wednesdays at 10:30 p.m. JST International streaming Crunchyroll in its listed Fall 2026 territories; check local catalog Studio SILVER LINK. Schedule checked October 25, 2026 · official broadcast and streaming schedule When did Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 premiere? Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 began on October 7, 2026. As of October 25, the sequel is airing in Japan. The main practical detail is that there is no single schedule for every viewer: Japanese television, Japanese streaming services and Crunchyroll publish separate listings, and their clocks should not be mixed together. The official anime schedule lists AT-X on Wednesdays at 10:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time (JST), starting October 7 with a one-hour special. Tokyo MX also began that night at 11:00 p.m. JST, with a one-hour premiere slot. BS NTV's first broadcast was Thursday, October 8 at 11:00 p.m. JST. The difference is the channel timetable, not a second premiere for another season. For each station, the official schedule lists later installments in regular 30-minute weekly slots. Does the first broadcast contain two episodes? The official wording calls the opening a one-hour special. That describes the length of the Japanese premiere slot; it does not establish how every international streaming service divides or labels the material in its episode menu. KADOKAWA's schedule separately identifies the weekly 30-minute slots for episodes after the special. If a service displays one long premiere or separate episode entries, follow that service's listing rather than assuming the Japanese TV format guarantees two numbered streaming episodes. Related reading: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Anime Shares Creditless Opening and Ending Videos . Where can you stream it in Japan? The official anime website names Prime Video as the earliest, exclusive streaming service in Japan. Its schedule lists new episodes on Wednesdays from October 7 at 10:30 p.m. JST. The same official page lists a wider group of Japanese services beginning Monday, October 12 at 10:30 p.m. JST. The subscription services include d Anime Store, ABEMA, U-NEXT, Anime Hodai, Nico Nico, DMM TV, Lemino, FOD, Bandai Channel, Hulu, TELASA, J:COM STREAM and milplus. It also lists several pay-per-view stores. Availability can change, so use the linked service pages for current catalog status. These Japan-specific rights do not mean that Prime Video is the international platform in every country. Related reading: Anime Mysterious Codes (October 2026): Reports & Redemption Guide . Where can viewers outside Japan watch? Crunchyroll included Season 2 in its Fall 2026 lineup for North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, the CIS, India and Southeast Asia. The platform listing is the relevant source for those territories, while local catalog and language options should be checked in the viewer's country. The published lineup did not give one clock time that can safely be applied to every region. AniNextUp therefore does not convert a Japanese broadcast time into a claimed worldwide streaming time. That distinction matters if a calendar app shows October 7 in one place and October 8 in another. Japan's BS NTV broadcast begins on October 8, while AT-X and Tokyo MX start on October 7; international availability follows the local platform's schedule. A date-only season announcement cannot tell a viewer what hour an episode appears in a different time zone. What is Season 2 about? The official introduction starts with Sasaki, a tired office worker who buys a Java sparrow at a pet shop. The bird, Peeps, is a renowned sage reborn from another world. Peeps gives Sasaki magic and a way to cross between modern Japan and a fantasy setting. Sasaki uses that access to trade goods, run a restaurant and train in magic, hoping the other world can offer relief from corporate life. Related reading: Anime News: October 2026 — Streaming Updates & 2027 Announcements . The story then complicates that escape: on his way home from work, Sasaki encounters a person with supernatural abilities. He uses otherworldly magic to get through the encounter, is mistaken for an ability user himself, and is recruited by a Japanese government office dealing with paranormal phenomena. That premise explains the series' unusual mix of fantasy commerce, workplace comedy and modern supernatural conflict. Season 2 continues those threads with Peeps and the returning cast; the official synopsis, rather than fan speculation, is the safest guide to what the adaptation has confirmed. Who is making the new season? SILVER LINK. returns as the animation studio. The official KADOKAWA listing credits Yushi Abe as director, Yamato Ouchi as assistant director, Deko Akao for series composition and Saori Nakashiki for character design. Music is credited to Koji Fujimoto and Osamu Sasaki. The main Japanese cast includes Tomokazu Sugita as Sasaki, Aoi Yuki as Peeps, Akari Kito as the Neighbor, Rie Takahashi as Hoshizaki, Naomi Ohzora as Futari Shizuka, and Miyu Tomita as Elsa. KADOKAWA's full cast list includes the additional returning characters and performers. Related reading: BLEACH × Graniph: 17-Item Collection Launches in Japan on October 20 . What does the trailer confirm? The official trailer promotes the October start and the first-season setup; later promotional material gives the exact October 7 premiere and one-hour-special format. The trailer is useful for seeing the new visual and returning characters, but it does not replace the broadcast schedule. The official Crunchyroll YouTube listing shows a June 3, 2026 publication date. The accessible listing does not expose the original upload time with a timezone, so AniNextUp does not invent that precision or add a VideoObject uploadDate. The current official anime schedule is linked below for the details that affect when and where to watch. What is confirmed, and what remains unclear? Confirmed details include the October 7 start, a one-hour Japanese premiere slot, the station-by-station timetable, Prime Video's Japanese Wednesday release, the wider Japanese streaming rollout, Crunchyroll's listed territories, the studio, principal staff and cast. The official pages reviewed do not state a complete season episode count, a finale date, or a universal international release hour. Those points should remain open until the production committee or regional streaming service publishes them. Official sources Official anime website: Season 2 broadcast and Japanese streaming schedule KADOKAWA: Season 2 schedule, staff, cast and premise · KADOKAWA official series profile Crunchyroll Fall 2026 lineup and listed territories · Official Crunchyroll trailer The official trailer listing identifies June 3, 2026, but the accessible listing does not show its exact original upload time and timezone. No precise upload timestamp or VideoObject is asserted. entries.content: OCTOBER 19, 2026 · NEW ANIME Sekiro: No Defeat Release Date: January 2027, Episodes & Trailer Sekiro: No Defeat premieres as an eight-episode series in January 2027. The expanded television version follows the Japanese theatrical release and adds material that was not included in the film. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official TV anime key visual · ©KADOKAWA/Sekiro: No Defeat PARTNERS. Original game ©2019 FromSoftware, Inc. Source: September 25 production announcement . Release at a glance Series premiere January 2027 · exact day and time TBA Episodes 8 · expanded television version Streaming Crunchyroll · supported territories Animation studio Qzil.la Verified October 19, 2026 · Official TV anime website When does Sekiro: No Defeat come out? Sekiro: No Defeat is scheduled to premiere in January 2027. The official announcement confirms an eight-episode television series, but gives no specific January day, broadcast time or international episode schedule. “January 2027” is a confirmed month, not a complete calendar date. We will update this guide when the production or distributor publishes a precise schedule. Where can you watch the Sekiro anime? Crunchyroll has announced that it will stream the anime outside Japan, China, Korea, Russia and Belarus. This is the distributor’s announced territory scope; it does not guarantee that every title appears in every local catalog on the same day. Check the service’s listing in your country near the premiere. The subtitle and dub languages, episode release hour and regional scheduling differences have not been confirmed in the sources linked here. Is the September release a movie or the January anime? Both formats exist, which explains the two dates readers may see. The Japanese theatrical edition opened on September 4, 2026, after the project was introduced as a limited cinema release. On September 25, the production committee clarified that the work began as an eight-part television series and that the film was an edited version released first so audiences could experience its visuals and sound on a large screen. Related reading: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Is Out on Netflix: Episodes & Trailer . The January 2027 release is the television series. Producer ARCH says it follows the movie’s story but is rebuilt with episodes, scenes and cuts that the theatrical edit did not include. The series is not simply the movie divided into eight identical parts. If you saw the film, the weekly version is still described as a distinct experience; if you missed the cinema run, the official announcement presents the TV edition as another way to encounter the story. The dates answer different questions: September 4 was the Japanese theatrical opening, while January 2027 is the confirmed TV-series window. Use the January window when planning to watch the episodic edition. Related reading: The Detective Is Already Dead Season 2: Release Date, Episodes & Where to Watch . What is the story about? The adaptation is based on FromSoftware’s Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice and takes place during Japan’s Sengoku period. Ashina is a land caught in war. Wolf, a shinobi raised to serve as a retainer, is bound to Kuro, the young Divine Heir. Kuro’s Dragon’s Heritage carries the power of immortality, making him a target for people who want to use that power in the struggle over Ashina. The official synopsis adds a moral conflict to the rescue story: Kuro learns that immortality brings a deadly illness called Dragonrot to others and decides to seek a way to sever the Dragon’s Heritage. Wolf then fights to change the fate his lord has chosen. That is a useful starting point for newcomers without requiring knowledge of the game’s mechanics, bosses or optional routes. Related reading: Dreamland Anime: Release Date, Episodes & Where to Watch . Do you need to play the game first? The official description introduces the central relationship and stakes on its own, so viewers can approach the anime as a story about a protector, a young lord and the cost of immortality. The announcement does not say that viewers must play the game first. Because the game has multiple possible endings, the anime’s official announcements do not yet say which path the adaptation will use. Claims that it follows one particular ending remain speculation. Watch the official Sekiro: No Defeat trailer The production’s official website links the theatrical trailer on KADOKAWAanime’s YouTube channel. Its public listing gives June 26, 2026 as the upload date and promotes the September 4 Japanese cinema release. The YouTube page does not expose a verifiable upload hour or time zone in the source available for this review, so this guide reports the date only and does not give an exact timestamp. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Official theatrical trailer · TV series: January 2027 Cast, studio and production staff The official TV cast list includes Daisuke Namikawa as Wolf, Miyuki Satou as Kuro, Kenjiro Tsuda as Genichiro Ashina, Jin Urayama as the Sculptor, Shizuka Ito as Emma, Akimitsu Takase as Hanbei, Takaya Hashi as Owl, Tetsuo Kanao as Isshin Ashina, and Risa Shimizu as the Divine Child of Rejuvenation. Kenichi Kutsuna directs, with Takuya Sato handling series composition and Takahiro Kishida designing the characters. The official staff list also credits deputy director Shunsuke Fukui, chief animation director Kaito Mogi and action animation director Takashi Mukoda. Qzil.la is the animation studio; ARCH produces the project. Shuta Hasunuma composes the music, and the theme is Ryuichi Sakamoto’s “Blu.” These confirmed credits identify the principal creative team without implying that every production role or track has been announced. What is still unconfirmed? The official site confirms January 2027, eight episodes and a television version with material not in the film. ARCH says the episodes will be released weekly, but that does not establish the weekday, local time or whether every country receives each episode simultaneously. Crunchyroll’s international distribution is announced for the listed territories, but a country-specific catalog date, language lineup and simulcast time remain unconfirmed here. The public trailer listing supplies a calendar date but no verifiable time zone, and the anime’s ending has not been announced. We will keep these details marked TBA until a primary source resolves them. Sources and verification Official production announcement: January 2027, eight episodes and the difference between the film and series Official TV anime website Official story synopsis Official cast and staff list Crunchyroll’s September 2026 series and distribution announcement Official theatrical trailer on KADOKAWAanime For another game-to-anime adaptation, see our Ghost of Tsushima: Legends anime guide . entries.content: OCTOBER 20, 2026 · RETURNING SERIES Shangri-La Frontier Season 3 Release Date: January 10, 2027 Shangri-La Frontier Season 3 begins in Japan on January 10, 2027, with two consecutive cours. The official story introduction points Sunraku and his allies toward an exhibition match in a new competitive arena. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official third-season key visual · ©Katarina, Ryosuke Fuji, Kodansha / Shangri-La Frontier Production Committee, MBS. Production announcement . Release at a glance Japanese premiere January 10, 2027 · Sundays at 5:00 p.m. JST Broadcaster MBS/TBS network · 28 stations Run Two consecutive cours · episode count TBA Animation studio C2C International streaming Service and local time not confirmed by the cited official schedule Confirmed September 16, 2026 · Official date and run announcement · Official broadcast page When does Shangri-La Frontier Season 3 come out? Shangri-La Frontier Season 3 premieres in Japan on January 10, 2027. The official broadcast page lists MBS and TBS's nationwide 28-station network, with new episodes on Sundays at 5:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time (JST). The production announced the specific date, weekly slot, and two-cour plan on September 16, 2026. The schedule may still change, so the official on-air page is the best place to check for a later notice. That 5:00 p.m. time is the Japanese television slot. It is not an international streaming timestamp. Viewers outside Japan should avoid converting it into a local simulcast time until a distributor posts a schedule for their region. What does “two consecutive cours” mean? The production says Season 3 will run for two consecutive cours. In Japanese television scheduling, a cour is a programming block of roughly three months, so the announcement signals a continuous run across two blocks rather than a short special. It does not announce an exact episode count, guarantee that every week will have an episode, or state the finale date. Those details remain unconfirmed in the official schedule. The January 10 start also gives fans a practical planning answer: the Japanese broadcast is a Sunday evening program, not a January release with a day still to be announced. If you are tracking the season from another country, keep the date and the local streaming time as separate facts. Where can you watch Season 3? The official Japanese on-air page confirms the MBS/TBS broadcast, but it does not provide a Season 3 international streaming timetable in the material reviewed here. It lists streaming services for Seasons 1 and 2, which can help returning viewers catch up in Japan; those lists do not prove that Season 3 will be available on every service or in every country. A global platform, regional catalog, subtitle launch, and dubbed release should be treated as separate announcements. For viewers asking whether Season 3 will stream on Crunchyroll, this page does not confirm a service or simulcast time from a directly verified distributor notice. Check the official platform listing for your country closer to January rather than relying on an older season's catalog or a time-zone conversion of the Japanese TV broadcast. What is the new season about? The official introduction moves the story from the game Shangri-La Frontier to the Global Game Competition. Sunraku takes a short break from his main game after a run of major encounters, including the unique monster Lycagon and the defeat of Wethermon. Oikatzo invites him to compete, and Pencilgon joins the effort as they enter Galaxia Heroes: Chaos , a new virtual-reality fighting game built on the Shangri-La Frontier engine. The immediate challenge is a match against Star Rain, described by the official site as a leading American professional fighting-game team. This setup explains why the next arc looks different from the earlier monster hunts: Sunraku and his friends have to apply their game knowledge in a competitive arena, learn a new game's rules, and face experienced opponents. The official synopsis names this direction, but it does not reveal every match result or how much of the tournament the season will adapt. For anyone returning after Season 2, the useful point is that the GGC is a continuation of the same characters' story, not a separate spin-off. Sunraku, Oikatzo, and Pencilgon are still central; the change is the game they are playing and the opponents in front of them. The teaser and new character material promote that transition without confirming a full episode-by-episode outline. Is there an official Season 3 trailer? Yes. The production's July 7, 2026 announcement says a third-season teaser PV was released and embeds the official video below. The official article gives the publication date, but the accessible official page does not show the exact upload time or timezone. That distinction matters: an article date cannot establish a precise YouTube upload timestamp, so this guide does not invent one or attach a VideoObject timestamp that cannot be verified. The teaser is promotional footage, not a full episode preview or a confirmed episode count. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TEASER Season 3 · January 2027 Who is returning, and which studio is animating it? C2C is the animation studio. The official staff page lists Toshiyuki Kubooka as chief director, Hiro Oki as director, Kazuyuki Fudeyasu for series composition and scripts, and Ayumi Kurashima for character design and chief animation direction. The credits also include action and effects direction by Satoshi Sakai and music by Ryōichi Takada, Kōhei Hirokawa, and Kuniyuki Takahashi of MONACA. Yuma Uchida returns as Sunraku/Rakurō, Azumi Waki as Saiga-0/Rei, Yōko Hikasa as Arthur Pencilgon/Towa, and Makoto Koichi as Oikatzo/Kei. The official cast list also names Yumi Uchiyama as Natsume Megumi, Minami Takahashi as Silvia Goldberg, and Daiki Hamano as Lucas Garcia. Those credits make the competition arc's new opponents easier to follow, while the returning trio keeps the series connected to its earlier seasons. What has not been announced yet? As of the official sources linked below, the Japanese premiere date, 5:00 p.m. JST broadcast slot, two-cour run, main staff, and credited cast are confirmed. A precise total episode count, finale date, full weekly schedule, international streaming service and local release hour, and English dub timetable are not confirmed on the cited Japanese pages. The official teaser's exact YouTube upload time and timezone are also not published there. We will update this guide when the production or a distributor provides those details. entries.title: SSS-Class Revival Hunter Anime: January 2027 Premiere, New Trailer, Cast and Crunchyroll
entries.description: SSS-Class Revival Hunter premieres January 2027. The second official trailer reveals eight more cast members and an ending theme collaboration. Here is what is confirmed.
entries.content: OFFICIAL ANIME NEWS · OCTOBER 12, 2026 SSS-Class Revival Hunter Anime: January 2027 Premiere, New Trailer, Cast and Crunchyroll The Korean fantasy hit's TV anime arrives in January 2027. A second promotional video brings eight additional Japanese voice actors into focus and reveals the artists behind its ending theme. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · Editorial policy Official promotional visual. Source and artwork credit: official anime website . Release at a glance Release January 2027; exact date pending Where to watch Crunchyroll in announced territories, including the Americas Applies to Japan broadcast window and licensed international streaming Still pending Exact premiere day and regional episode times Release details checked October 24, 2026 · Official source When does SSS-Class Revival Hunter premiere? January 2027 is the confirmed Japanese television premiere window for SSS-Class Revival Hunter (Japanese title Shishite Ikiru SSS-kyu Hunter ). The official site lists Fuji TV's +Ultra programming block and other channels. An exact premiere day and episode count have not yet been announced. What does the second trailer confirm about the premiere? The October 11, 2026 promotional video introduces more of Kim Gongja's story and its cast, but no exact broadcast date. The production currently specifies January 2027 on Fuji TV's +Ultra block and other Japanese channels. An episode count and international streaming schedule remain unannounced. Related reading: ONE PIECE: Elbaph Arc English Dub Release Date and Crunchyroll Schedule . Second official trailer reveals new characters On October 11, 2026, the production published its second promotional video after a New York Comic Con preview. YouTube’s original metadata credits HAYATE’s channel and records the upload at 6:30:00 p.m. PDT (UTC−07:00) on October 10 — 10:30:00 a.m. JST on October 11 . That is the video’s upload timestamp, not an anime broadcast time. The trailer follows F-rank hunter Kim Gongja as he gains a rare ability tied to his own death and encounters the Sword Emperor, rival hunters and powerful guild leaders. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Opens on YouTube Confirmed Japanese voice cast The latest announcement adds eight performers to the two previously confirmed leads: Takeo Otsuka as Kim Gongja. Satoshi Hino as Sword Emperor. Toshiki Masuda as Flame Emperor. Megumi Han as Witch of the Black Dragon. Sayaka Kinoshita as Paladin. Risa Shimizu as Countess. Makoto Furukawa as Poisonous Viper. Natsumi Fujiwara as Inquisitor. Yuka Iguchi as Master Alchemist. Shunsuke Sakuya as Blade Saint. These names reflect the official October 11 cast announcement, not speculation based on the webcomic's character roster. Who performs the ending theme? The anime's ending theme is a collaboration between THE SPELLBOUND and BOOM BOOM SATELLITES . The artists were announced on October 11, but the song title and full audio were not revealed at that time. No opening theme should be assumed from this announcement. Studio, director and production staff STUDIO fu is producing the anime, with Hiroaki Sakurai directing, Sayuri Oba handling series scripts, and Takahiro Yoshimatsu designing the characters. Ryo Kawasaki and Tomoyuki Kono are credited for the music. These are the announced production roles as of October 2026. Where can you watch SSS-Class Revival Hunter? Crunchyroll has confirmed streaming in North, Central and South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, the CIS, the Indian subcontinent, Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia and Singapore. This is a distribution plan, not an exact same-day release timetable: the Japanese broadcast date, local episode time and subtitle availability are separate details. Crunchyroll has not published territory-specific launch times, so check the local catalog when the January schedule becomes more specific. What is SSS-Class Revival Hunter about? A mysterious tower filled with monsters attracts hunters chasing wealth and prestige. Kim Gongja begins as an overlooked F-rank hunter who envies the powerful Flame Emperor. When he gains an extraordinary S-rank ability, he discovers a dangerous condition: the power activates only when he dies . Together with the Sword Emperor, he begins a high-stakes climb that challenges the usual rules of the hunter genre. What does Gongja’s death-triggered skill do? Tapas’s official English webcomic listing clarifies the rule behind the hook: Gongja receives a skill that copies another hunter’s ability, but the exchange costs his life. After the Flame Emperor kills him, Gongja copies a second power that sends him back in time on death. The two linked rules explain the revival premise and why each fatal attempt can change his next move. This is source-material context; it does not confirm which chapters the anime will adapt. The anime adapts a Korean fantasy story that originated as a web novel by Sinnoa and later became a popular webcomic. The animated adaptation is a Japanese television production. Where can you read the source material? Tapas hosts the official English webcomic listing and credits Neida, Sinnoa and Bill K; Yen Press lists its English print volumes. These give readers options to start online or collect physical books, but they describe the source comic rather than the anime’s episode order. The production has not said how many chapters or story arcs the January 2027 season will cover, so a volume count is not yet a viewing guide. Frequently asked questions Is SSS-Class Revival Hunter coming out in 2026? No. The confirmed Japanese premiere window is January 2027. Will it stream on Crunchyroll? Yes, Crunchyroll has confirmed streaming in numerous regions, including the Americas and Europe. How many episodes will there be? The episode count has not been officially confirmed. Is there a new trailer? Yes. The official second PV was uploaded by HAYATE at 6:30:00 p.m. PDT (UTC−07:00) on October 10, 2026, which was 10:30:00 a.m. JST on October 11. It adds eight cast members and names the ending-theme artists. Official sources and further reading Official anime website · October 11 cast and trailer announcement · official English webcomic listing · Yen Press print edition · Crunchyroll's streaming and cast confirmation .
